19.20.16.a.m: If he does not return, he should offer this very boiled rice oblation to the Ādityas.

19.20.17.a.m: He should also bind the pegs into the firewood.

19.20.18.a.m: He should place them on [the fire] together with the firewood.

19.20.19.a.s: avagataḥ kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ vāruṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapati
19.20.19.a.d: अवगतः कृष्णानां व्रीहीणां वारुणं चरुं निर्वपति
19.20.19.a.m: Having returned, he offers a boiled rice oblation of black rice to Varuṇa.

19.20.20.a.m: The offering is completed according to the established rule.

19.21.1.a.m: One desirous of life should offer a hundred-kṛṣṇala oblation to Prajāpati.

19.21.2.a.s: śataṃ hiraṇyakṛṣṇalāni kākiṇyā māṣeṇa vā saṃmitāni
19.21.2.a.d: शतं हिरण्यकृष्णलानि काकिण्या माषेण वा संमितानि
19.21.2.a.m: There are one hundred gold kṛṣṇala berries, measured by the weight of a kākiṇī or a māṣa.

19.21.3.a.m: He pours them into the clarified butter over the strainers.

19.21.5.a.m: At the time of offering, he cuts off eight for the deity.

19.21.5.c.m: Two for the prāśitra portion; eight for the iḍā.

19.21.6.a.s: caturdhākaraṇakāle sarvāṇi prāśitre samopyaikadhā brahmaṇa upaharati
19.21.6.a.d: चतुर्धाकरणकाले सर्वाणि प्राशित्रे समोप्यैकधा ब्रह्मण उपहरति
19.21.6.a.m: At the time of dividing into four parts, having thrown all of them together into the prāśitra vessel, he presents them at once to the brahman priest.

19.21.8.a.m: For the others, the consumption is omitted.

19.21.9.a.m: He sets down the boiled rice oblation for Sūrya, clasping it between two gold plates.

19.21.10.a.m: At each fore-offering of it, he sacrifices a kṛṣṇala berry.

19.21.11.a.m: Having removed the two gold plates, he proceeds with the boiled rice oblation.

19.21.12.a.m: These very two gold plates are the sacrificial gift.

19.21.13.a.m: [With the words], "To Agni the giver, an eight-potsherd sacrificial cake," [there are] three [oblations].

19.21.14.a.m: Among them, the third belongs to Prajāpati, consisting of mixed sacrificial substance.

19.21.15.a.m: Curd, honey, clarified butter, water, roasted grains, and unhusked rice: according to some, [this is] a modification of clarified butter.

19.21.16.a.m: Honey and water being mixed, when primary, have their own ritual rules.

19.21.17.a.s: ghṛtaṃ na pūtamubhe suścandreti yājyānuvākye bhavataḥ
19.21.17.a.d: घृतं न पूतमुभे सुश्चन्द्रेति याज्यानुवाक्ये भवतः
19.21.17.a.m: "Like clarified butter, purified…" and "Both of great radiance…" are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

19.21.18.a.s: āgneyasya ca saumyasya caindre samāśleṣayediti saṃhitāni havīṃṣyadhiśrayedityarthaḥ
19.21.18.a.d: आग्नेयस्य च सौम्यस्य चैन्द्रे समाश्लेषयेदिति संहितानि हवींष्यधिश्रयेदित्यर्थः
19.21.18.a.m: [With the rule,] "One should join the [substance] of Agni and that of Soma onto that of Indra," the meaning is that one should place the sacrificial substances [on the fire] adjoining one another.

19.21.19.a.m: Or, one should join the two scrapings onto it.

19.21.20.a.m: [With the formula,] "May I destroy the people among the brahmins," everything belongs to Bṛhaspati (Brahmaṇaspati).

19.21.21.a.m: One should make the invitatory and consecratory verses addressed to the Maruts.

19.21.22.a.m: Then he places this three-layered [cake] on eleven upturned potsherds.

19.22.1.a.s: prathamaṃ puroḍāśamadhiśritya paritapanāntaṃ kṛtvā tasminnuttaraṃ jyāyāṃsamadhiśritya tadantameva kṛtvā tasminnuttaraṃ jyāyāṃsamadhiśrayati
19.22.1.a.d: प्रथमं पुरोडाशमधिश्रित्य परितपनान्तं कृत्वा तस्मिन्नुत्तरं ज्यायांसमधिश्रित्य तदन्तमेव कृत्वा तस्मिन्नुत्तरं ज्यायांसमधिश्रयति
19.22.1.a.m: Having placed the first sacrificial cake [on the potsherds] and carried [the procedure] up to scorching, he places a larger one on top of it, carries [the procedure] up to that very [scorching], and then places a [yet] larger one on top of it.

19.22.2.a.m: At the time of performance, he should sacrifice from the southern half to the first deity,

19.22.3.a.m: It has been said: "Bringing them all together, he cuts [portions]."

19.22.4.a.s: prācyāṃ diśi tvamindreti tisra ṛco vyatyāsamanvāha
19.22.4.a.d: प्राच्यां दिशि त्वमिन्द्रेति तिस्र ऋचो व्यत्यासमन्वाह
19.22.4.a.m: He recites the three verses, "In the eastern quarter you, O Indra…", in alternate order.

19.22.5.a.m: Having recited the first [as the invitatory verse], he should sacrifice with the middle one [as the consecratory verse];

19.22.5.b.m: having recited the middle one [as the invitatory verse], he should sacrifice with the last one [as the consecratory verse];

19.22.5.c.m: having recited the last one [as the invitatory verse], he should sacrifice with the first one [as the consecratory verse].

19.22.6.a.m: In this manner are all the consecratory and invitatory verses.

19.22.8.a.m: As traditionally prescribed, with [the formula], "Since to Indra Rathantara…", he places [the cake] on twelve upturned potsherds.

19.22.9.a.m: At the time of performance, he sacrifices to the first deity from the eastern half;

19.22.10.a.m: similarly to the others, turning clockwise, ending in the north.

19.22.11.a.m: It has been said: "He cuts portions all around progressively."

19.22.12.a.s: abhi tvā sūra nonuma iti ṣaḍṛco vyatyāsamanvāha
19.22.12.a.d: अभि त्वा सूर नोनुम इति षडृचो व्यत्यासमन्वाह
19.22.12.a.m: He recites the six verses, "Unto thee, hero, we shout…", in alternate order.

19.22.13.a.m: He should not pronounce the vaṣaṭ-call with a bṛhatī verse.

19.22.14.a.m: He should carry four syllables of the invitatory verse over into the consecratory verse.

19.22.15.a.s: anuṣṭubhaṃ ca ha vā etatsaṃpādayanti paṅktiṃ ceti te manyāmahe
19.22.15.a.d: अनुष्टुभं च ह वा एतत्संपादयन्ति पङ्क्तिं चेति ते मन्यामहे
19.22.15.a.m: "Indeed, thus they produce an anuṣṭubh and a paṅkti," so we think.

19.22.16.a.s: abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'dugdhā iva dhenavaḥ /
19.22.16.a.d: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमो ऽदुग्धा इव धेनवः ।
19.22.16.a.m: "Unto thee, hero, we shout like unmilked cows,

19.22.16.b.s: īśānamasya jagataḥ suvardṛśamīśānamomityanūcya [ndratasthuṣa] stvāmiddhi havāmaha iti yajet
19.22.16.b.d: ईशानमस्य जगतः सुवर्दृशमीशानमोमित्यनूच्य [न्द्रतस्थुष] स्त्वामिद्धि हवामह इति यजेत्
19.22.16.b.m:
ruler of this moving world, beholding the sun, ruler—om!" Having recited this, he should sacrifice with: "[…of what stands, O Indra,] thee indeed we invoke!"

"Thee indeed we invoke, the makers [of hymns], for the winning of booty;

19.23.1.b.s: tvāṃ vṛtreṣvindra satpatiṃ narastvāṃ kāṣṭhomityanūcya [svarvato] 'bhi tvā śūra nonuma iti yajet
19.23.1.b.d: त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठोमित्यनूच्य [स्वर्वतो] ऽभि त्वा शूर नोनुम इति यजेत्
19.23.1.b.m: thee, O Indra, true lord among the Vṛtras, the heroes [call] thee, at the goal—om!" Having recited this, he should sacrifice with: "[…of heaven,] unto thee, hero, we shout!"

19.23.2.a.m: As the fourth among these [verses], he places: "Never art thou barren…"

19.23.3.a.m: It has been said: "To Agni the radiant, an eight-potsherd sacrificial cake."

19.23.4.a.s: caturdhākaraṇakāle sauryāṃstrīnpiṇḍānuddhṛtyodu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ sapta tvā harito rathe citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkamiti piṇḍānyajamānāya prayacchati
19.23.4.a.d: चतुर्धाकरणकाले सौर्यांस्त्रीन्पिण्डानुद्धृत्योदु त्यं जातवेदसं सप्त त्वा हरितो रथे चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकमिति पिण्डान्यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
19.23.4.a.m: At the time of making the fourfold division, having taken up three lumps of the [mess] for Sūrya, he hands the lumps to the sacrificer with: "Up that known to all beings…", "Seven bay steeds in the chariot [draw] thee…", [and] "The wondrous countenance of the gods has arisen…"

19.23.6.a.m: One who desires a village should offer the Sāṃgrahaṇī [iṣṭi] dedicated to the Viśvedevas.

19.23.8.a.m: With [the formulas] beginning with, "Thou art steadfast…", he lays down the enclosing sticks, each to its mantra.

19.23.10.a.s: yo jyogāmayāvī syādyo vā kāmayeta sarvamāyuriyāmiti tasmā etāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapet /
19.23.10.a.d: यो ज्योगामयावी स्याद्यो वा कामयेत सर्वमायुरियामिति तस्मा एतामिष्टिं निर्वपेत् ।
19.23.10.a.m: One should offer this iṣṭi for one who has been ill for a long time, or who wishes, "May I attain the full span of life."

19.23.11.a.m: At the time of setting out the vessels, he employs a four-cornered vessel of khadira wood,

19.23.11.b.m: and a golden ear-ornament made of a hundred measures.

19.23.12.a.s: atho khalu yāvatīḥ samā eṣyanmanyeta tāvanmānaṃ syāt
19.23.12.a.d: अथो खलु यावतीः समा एष्यन्मन्येत तावन्मानं स्यात्
19.23.12.a.m: Or rather, of as many years as he expects he will live, of that many measures it should be.

19.23.13.a.s: yannavamaittannavanītamabhavadityājyamavekṣyājyagrahaṇakāle tūṣṇīṃ khādire caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sādanakāla uttareṇa dhruvāṃ khādiraṃ sādayitvā tasminpravartamavadadhāti
19.23.13.a.d: यन्नवमैत्तन्नवनीतमभवदित्याज्यमवेक्ष्याज्यग्रहणकाले तूष्णीं खादिरे चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा सादनकाल उत्तरेण ध्रुवां खादिरं सादयित्वा तस्मिन्प्रवर्तमवदधाति
19.23.13.a.m: Having looked at the clarified butter with, "Because it gathered afresh, that became fresh butter…", at the time of taking the clarified butter, having taken four ladlings silently into the khadira vessel, and at the time of placing [it] having set the khadira vessel north of the dhruvā ladle, he drops the ear-ornament into it.

19.24.1.a.s: upahomakāle śvinoḥ prāṇo 'sītyetaiḥ pratimantraṃ catura upahomāñjuhoti
19.24.1.a.d: उपहोमकाले श्विनोः प्राणो ऽसीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं चतुर उपहोमाञ्जुहोति
19.24.1.a.m: At the time of the minor libations, he offers four minor libations, each to its mantra, with [the formulas] beginning with, "Thou art the breath of the Aśvins…"

19.24.2.a.s: hutvāhutvā pravartamabhighārayati rāḍasi virāḍasi samrāḍasi svarāḍasīti
19.24.2.a.d: हुत्वाहुत्वा प्रवर्तमभिघारयति राडसि विराडसि सम्राडसि स्वराडसीति
19.24.2.a.m: Each time after offering, he bastes the ear-ornament with: "Thou art the king, thou art the wide ruler, thou art the sovereign ruler, thou art the self-ruler."

19.24.3.a.s: yatkhādira ājyaṃ tadagreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ sādayati
19.24.3.a.d: यत्खादिर आज्यं तदग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां सादयति
19.24.3.a.m: Having brought the clarified butter which is in the khadira vessel around past the front of the āhavanīya, he sets it down on the southern hip of the altar ground.

19.24.4.a.m: The sacrificer looks at it with: "The stream of clarified butter, the path of immortality."

19.24.5.a.m: Then the brahman takes his right hand.

19.24.6.a.s: brahmaṇa itara ṛtvijo hastamanvārabhya yajamānaṃ paryāhuḥ pāvamānena tvā stomeneti
19.24.6.a.d: ब्रह्मण इतर ऋत्विजो हस्तमन्वारभ्य यजमानं पर्याहुः पावमानेन त्वा स्तोमेनेति
19.24.6.a.m: The other priests, holding onto the hand of the brahman, address the sacrificer all around with: "With the Pāvamāna stoma…"

19.24.7.a.m: Then the sacrificer sips the clarified butter from the gold.

19.24.8.a.m: [The adhvaryu] consecrates him while he is eating with: "Make him, O Agni, unto life and brilliance…"

19.24.9.a.s: uddhṛtya hiraṇyaṃ prakṣālyāyuṣṭe viśvato dadhaditi yajamānāya prayacchati
19.24.9.a.d: उद्धृत्य हिरण्यं प्रक्षाल्यायुष्टे विश्वतो दधदिति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
19.24.9.a.m: Having taken out the gold and washed it, he hands it to the sacrificer with: "Bestowing life upon thee from all sides…"

19.24.10.a.s: tadyajamāna ācamya pratigṛhya pradakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇa ābadhnātyāyurasi viśvāyurasi sarvāyurasi sarvamāyurasi sarvaṃ ma āyurbhūyātsarvamāyurgeṣamiti
19.24.10.a.d: तद्यजमान आचम्य प्रतिगृह्य प्रदक्षिणं दक्षिणे कर्ण आबध्नात्यायुरसि विश्वायुरसि सर्वायुरसि सर्वमायुरसि सर्वं म आयुर्भूयात्सर्वमायुर्गेषमिति
19.24.10.a.m: The sacrificer, having sipped water and accepted it, binds it clockwise on his right ear with: "Thou art life, thou art all-life, thou art full life, thou art the full span of life; may all life be mine, may I attain the full span of life."

19.24.11.a.m: With the remainder of the section, "Agni is possessed of life…", the adhvaryu takes his right hand.

19.24.12.a.m: The iṣṭi concludes in the established manner.

19.25.1.a.m: Having poured out [grains for] a sacrificial cake for Indra-Varuṇa, he should offer a curdled milk offering for Indra-Varuṇa.

19.25.2.a.m: Having taken it off [the fire] and adorned it, he places the sacrificial cake down into the curd mixture (payasyā).

19.25.3.a.m: Having covered it with this very [curd mixture], he sets it down.

19.25.4.a.s: athāsmātpratidiśaṃ payasyāṃ vyūhati yā vāmindrāvaruṇā yatavyā tanūrity
19.25.4.a.d: अथास्मात्प्रतिदिशं पयस्यां व्यूहति या वामिन्द्रावरुणा यतव्या तनूरित्य्
19.25.4.a.m: Then, in every direction from it, he pushes aside the curd mixture with: 'O Indra and Varuṇa, whatever body of yours is to be propitiated…'

19.25.5.a.m: With the very same [formulas] he pushes it back together.

19.25.6.a.m: He bends the endings of the formulas, saying: 'is released.'

19.25.7.a.m: He cuts portions of the curd mixture together with the sacrificial cake.

19.25.8.a.m: The supplementary oblations are: 'O Indra and Varuṇa, whatever weak part in Agni…'

19.25.9.a.m: 'To Agni the gatherer, a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds'—this has been explained.

19.25.10.a.m: He recites fifteen kindling verses, beginning with: 'Harness the most divine-invoking…'

19.25.12.a.m: 'Surely for us, in search of cattle…' are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

19.25.13.a.m: 'Whose [offering] he enjoyed…' and 'For we know thee…' are the concluding verses.

19.25.14.a.m: On the full moon of the Citrā month, he should perform the Citrā sacrifice.

19.25.15.a.m: The supplementary oblations are: 'O Agni, come to us with cattle…'

19.25.16.a.m: Having moved away under abundant constellations, one desiring rain should sacrifice with the Kārīrī.

19.25.17.a.s: agnīnanvādhāyāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśya yajamāno mārutamasi marutāmoja iti kṛṣṇaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇatūṣaṃ paridhatte
19.25.17.a.d: अग्नीनन्वाधायापरेणाहवनीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविश्य यजमानो मारुतमसि मरुतामोज इति कृष्णं वासः कृष्णतूषं परिधत्ते
19.25.17.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires, stepped past south of the āhavanīya and sat down, the sacrificer puts on a black garment with black fringe, with: 'Thou art related to the Maruts; thou art the vigor of the Maruts.'

19.25.18.a.m: With 'Stay, O Maruts, the advancing falcon!', he pushes back the west wind.

19.25.19.a.m: He brings forth the east wind with: 'Come, O wind!'

19.25.20.a.m: A black horse stands in front, facing west.

19.25.21.a.m: He touches it with this garment, with: 'Neigh!'

19.25.22.a.m: If it neighs, shakes itself, or drops dung or urine, he should know that it will rain.

19.26.1.a.s: purovāto varṣannityaṣṭau vātanāmāni hutvāntarvedi kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya tasminkharjūrasaktūnkarīrasaktūnvā māndā vāśā iti kṛṣṇamadhuṣā saṃyutya tisraḥ piṇḍīḥ kṛtvā puṣkarapalāśaiḥ saṃveṣṭya samudyamya kṛṣṇājinasyāntānvṛṣṇo aśvasya saṃdānamasīti kṛṣṇena dāmnopanahyati
19.26.1.a.d: पुरोवातो वर्षन्नित्यष्टौ वातनामानि हुत्वान्तर्वेदि कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्खर्जूरसक्तून्करीरसक्तून्वा मान्दा वाशा इति कृष्णमधुषा संयुत्य तिस्रः पिण्डीः कृत्वा पुष्करपलाशैः संवेष्ट्य समुद्यम्य कृष्णाजिनस्यान्तान्वृष्णो अश्वस्य संदानमसीति कृष्णेन दाम्नोपनह्यति
19.26.1.a.m: Having offered the eight wind-names beginning with 'The east wind, raining…', having spread inside the altar ground a black antelope skin with its neck to the east and its fleece upward, having mixed on it date meal or karīra-fruit meal with black bee's honey with 'Māndā, Vāśā…', having made three balls, having wrapped them with lotus leaves, having raised the edges of the black antelope skin, he ties it up with a black cord with: 'Thou art the hobble of the vigorous horse.'

19.26.2.a.m: On the rubbish heap stands a cart with three hurdles, having its pole pointing east.

19.26.4.a.s: devā vasavyā iti pūrvasyāṃ gadhāyāṃ kṛṣṇājinamābadhnīyāt
19.26.4.a.d: देवा वसव्या इति पूर्वस्यां गधायां कृष्णाजिनमाबध्नीयात्
19.26.4.a.m: He should tie the black antelope skin to the eastern hurdle with: 'O Vasu-granting gods…'

19.26.5.a.m: It remains tied for a day and a night.

19.26.6.a.m: If it rains, he offers the balls alone.

19.26.7.a.s: yadi na varṣeddevāḥ śarmaṇyā iti madhyamāyāmābadhnīyāt
19.26.7.a.d: यदि न वर्षेद्देवाः शर्मण्या इति मध्यमायामाबध्नीयात्
19.26.7.a.m: If it does not rain, he should tie it to the middle one with: 'O gods who give protection…'

19.26.8.a.m: It remains tied for a day and a night.

19.26.9.a.m: If it rains, he offers the balls alone.

19.26.10.a.s: yadi na varṣeddevāḥ sapītaya iti jaghanyāyāmābadhnīyāt
19.26.10.a.d: यदि न वर्षेद्देवाः सपीतय इति जघन्यायामाबध्नीयात्
19.26.10.a.m: If it does not rain, he should tie it to the hindmost one with: 'O gods of common drinking…'

19.26.11.a.m: It remains tied for a day and a night.

19.26.12.a.m: If it rains, he offers the balls alone.

19.26.13.a.s: yadi na varṣecchvo bhūte dhāmacchadādīni trīṇi havīṃsi nirvapati kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇām
19.26.13.a.d: यदि न वर्षेच्छ्वो भूते धामच्छदादीनि त्रीणि हवींसि निर्वपति कृष्णानां व्रीहीणाम्
19.26.13.a.m: If it does not rain, on the next day he offers three oblations of black rice, beginning with that to Dhāmacchad.

19.26.14.a.m: Having set them down, he sets down the black antelope skin on the rubbish heap.

19.26.15.a.m: Wearing black turbans, dressed in black garments, and with their sacred threads suspended round their necks (nivīta), the priests officiate.

19.26.16.a.m: 'Even those immovable things thou…' are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

19.26.17.a.s: upahomakāle divā cittamaḥ kṛṇvantītyetaiḥ pratimantraṃ piṇḍīrābadhnāti
19.26.17.a.d: उपहोमकाले दिवा चित्तमः कृण्वन्तीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं पिण्डीराबध्नाति
19.26.17.a.m: At the time of the supplementary oblations, he ties up the balls with the verses beginning with 'Making darkness even by day…', verse by verse.

19.26.19.a.m: Then he addresses their smoke with a formula:

19.27.2.a.s: utkare kṛṣṇāmāmapakvāṃ sthālīmadbhiḥ pūrayati sṛjā vṛṣṭimiti
19.27.2.a.d: उत्करे कृष्णामामपक्वां स्थालीमद्भिः पूरयति सृजा वृष्टिमिति
19.27.2.a.m: On the rubbish heap, he fills an unbaked black earthen pot with water, with: 'Release the rain!'

19.27.3.a.m: If it breaks, he should know that it will rain.

19.27.4.a.s: anasa upastambhane śaṅkau vā kṛṣṇāvirbaddhā bhavati
19.27.4.a.d: अनस उपस्तम्भने शङ्कौ वा कृष्णाविर्बद्धा भवति
19.27.4.a.m: A black ewe is tied to the prop of the cart or to a peg.

19.27.5.a.m: He sprinkles it with: 'Born in the waters art thou.'

19.27.6.a.m: In its case, he takes note [of signs] as with the horse.

19.27.7.a.s: utkare varṣāhūstambaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyonnambhaya pṛthivīmiti varṣāhvāṃ juhoti
19.27.7.a.d: उत्करे वर्षाहूस्तम्बं प्रतिष्ठाप्योन्नम्भय पृथिवीमिति वर्षाह्वां जुहोति
19.27.7.a.m: Having set up a clump of varṣāhū plants on the rubbish heap, he offers the varṣāhvā plant with: 'Make the earth swell!'

19.27.8.a.m: Some say he offers a ladle full of water.

19.27.9.a.m: Then he throws it into the āhavanīya.

19.27.10.a.s: athāsya dhūmamanumantrayate hirṇyakeśo rajaso visāra iti
19.27.10.a.d: अथास्य धूममनुमन्त्रयते हिर्ण्यकेशो रजसो विसार इति
19.27.10.a.m: Then he addresses its smoke with: 'Golden-haired, spreader through the atmosphere…'

19.27.11.a.s: ye devā divibhāgā ityuparyāhavanīye kṛṣṇājinamavadhūnotyūrdhvagrīvaṃ bahiṣṭādviśasanam
19.27.11.a.d: ये देवा दिविभागा इत्युपर्याहवनीये कृष्णाजिनमवधूनोत्यूर्ध्वग्रीवं बहिष्टाद्विशसनम्
19.27.11.a.m: With 'O gods whose share is in heaven…', he shakes the black antelope skin above the āhavanīya, with its neck upwards and the slit on the outside.

19.27.12.a.m: A black garment, a black horse, and a black ewe are the sacrificial gift.

19.27.13.a.m: Now for the Kārīrī of the Sava: there is only the [cake] on eight potsherds for Agni, without any added deity.

19.27.14.a.s: tasyopahomā vātanāmāni yābhiḥ piṇḍīrābadhnāti juhoti yābhyāṃ ca dhūmamanumantrayate
19.27.14.a.d: तस्योपहोमा वातनामानि याभिः पिण्डीराबध्नाति जुहोति याभ्यां च धूममनुमन्त्रयते
19.27.14.a.m: Its supplementary oblations are the wind-names, those with which he ties up the balls or offers them, and the two with which he addresses the smoke.

19.27.15.a.m: As before, he puts on the fire [the cake] of three parts.

19.27.16.a.m: The oblation is for Indra and Viṣṇu.

19.27.17.a.m: With 'O Agni, may he surpass...' [TS 4.7.13.1], he inserts two dhāyyā verses in the uṣṇih and kakubh metres.

19.27.18.a.s: agne trī te vājinā trī ṣadhastheti trivatyā paridadhāti
19.27.18.a.d: अग्ने त्री ते वाजिना त्री षधस्थेति त्रिवत्या परिदधाति
19.27.18.a.m: With the verse containing the word 'three', 'Three are your fleet runners, O Agni, three are your seats...' [TS 4.7.13.3], he encloses [with the concluding verse].

19.27.19.a.m: 'Together in your work...', 'You both have conquered...' [TS 3.2.10.1] are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

19.27.21.a.m: Gold, a tārpya cloth, and a milch cow are the sacrificial gift.

19.27.22.a.m: When a kṣatriya is born, he should offer a boiled-grain oblation to Indra and Bṛhaspati.

19.27.23.a.m: A golden garland is the sacrificial gift, the sacrificial gift.

20.1.1.a.m: A universal king should sacrifice with the horse sacrifice (aśvamedha),

20.1.2.a.m: The lunar asterism is Citrā, which has an auspicious name.

20.1.3.a.m: He selects the sacrificial ground where to the east there are pleasant waters, easily accessible for bathing, and not drying up.

20.1.4.a.m: On the full-moon day of the month Caitra, he sacrifices with the sāṃgrahaṇī offering.

20.1.4.b.m: On the new-moon day that follows it, [he sacrifices] with the saṃjñānī offering.

20.1.5.a.s: vaiśākhyāṃ paruṇamāsyāṃ prājāpatyamṛṣabhaṃ tūparaṃ sarvarūpaṃ sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhya ālabhate
20.1.5.a.d: वैशाख्यां परुणमास्यां प्राजापत्यमृषभं तूपरं सर्वरूपं सर्वेभ्यः कामेभ्य आलभते
20.1.5.a.m: On the full-moon day of the month Vaiśākha, he immolates a hornless bull of all colors dedicated to Prajāpati, for [the attainment of] all desires.

20.1.6.a.m: On the new-moon day that follows it, they convey the chief officiating priests without [them walking on] foot.

20.1.7.a.m: Day by day they convey the others up to [the invocation of] the Subrahmaṇyā.

20.1.8.a.m: Having performed the new-moon sacrifice, he proceeds to the sacrificial ground.

20.1.13.a.m: He puts on an unwashed garment.

20.1.15.a.m: Those who are friendly keep watch over him.

20.1.16.a.m: For him who is restraining his speech, they offer the agnihotra this night.

20.1.17.a.s: draṣṭre nama upadraṣṭre namo 'nudraṣṭre namaḥ khyātre nama upakhyātre namo 'nukhyātre namaḥ śṛṇvate nama upaśṛṇvate namaḥ sate namo 'sate namo jātāya namo janiṣyamāṇāya namo bhūtāya namo bhaviṣyate namaścakṣuṣe namaḥ śrotrāya namo manase namo vāce namo brahmaṇe namastapase namaḥ śāntāya nama ityekaviṃśatyā namaskārairudyantamādityamupatiṣṭhate
20.1.17.a.d: द्रष्ट्रे नम उपद्रष्ट्रे नमो ऽनुद्रष्ट्रे नमः ख्यात्रे नम उपख्यात्रे नमो ऽनुख्यात्रे नमः शृण्वते नम उपशृण्वते नमः सते नमो ऽसते नमो जाताय नमो जनिष्यमाणाय नमो भूताय नमो भविष्यते नमश्चक्षुषे नमः श्रोत्राय नमो मनसे नमो वाचे नमो ब्रह्मणे नमस्तपसे नमः शान्ताय नम इत्येकविंशत्या नमस्कारैरुद्यन्तमादित्यमुपतिष्ठते
20.1.17.a.m: With twenty-one obeisances: 'Homage to the beholder, homage to the onlooker, homage to the watcher; homage to the proclaimer, homage to the notifier, homage to the reporter; homage to the listener, homage to the overhearer; homage to what is, homage to what is not; homage to what is born, homage to what will be born; homage to what has become, homage to what will become; homage to the eye, homage to the ear, homage to the mind, homage to speech, homage to the brahma, homage to austerity, homage to the pacified, homage!', he worships the rising sun,

20.2.1.a.m: and with 'Homage to Agni, dweller on the earth...' [TS 4.4.10.1], according to the characteristic marks.

20.2.2.a.s: ye te panthānaḥ savitariti pūrvayā dvārā prāgvaṃśaṃ praviśyāhavanīye vaitasamidhmamabhyādhāyaikādaśa pūrṇāhutīrjuhoti /
20.2.2.a.d: ये ते पन्थानः सवितरिति पूर्वया द्वारा प्राग्वंशं प्रविश्याहवनीये वैतसमिध्ममभ्याधायैकादश पूर्णाहुतीर्जुहोति ।
20.2.2.a.m: Having entered the hall with east-pointing beams by the eastern door with 'Whatever paths are yours, O Savitṛ...' [TS 1.2.2.1], and having placed reed firewood on the āhavanīya fire, he offers eleven full oblations:

20.2.2.b.m: eight with 'The golden germ arose in the beginning...' [TS 4.1.8.3–4 / 4.2.8.2],

20.2.2.c.m: and three with 'O gods, step out among the gods...' [TS 1.7.11.1].

20.2.3.a.m: Waters are collected into four vessels from the cardinal directions.

20.2.4.a.m: In them he cooks the boiled rice for the priests (brahmaudana).

20.2.5.a.s: pātryāṃ rājataṃ rukmaṃ nidhāya tasminbrahmaudanamuddhṛtya prabhūtena sarpiṣopasicya sauvarṇaṃ rukmamupariṣṭātkṛtvā karṣannanucchindaṃścaturbhya ārṣeyebhyo manartvigbhya upohati
20.2.5.a.d: पात्र्यां राजतं रुक्मं निधाय तस्मिन्ब्रह्मौदनमुद्धृत्य प्रभूतेन सर्पिषोपसिच्य सौवर्णं रुक्ममुपरिष्टात्कृत्वा कर्षन्ननुच्छिन्दंश्चतुर्भ्य आर्षेयेभ्यो मनर्त्विग्भ्य उपोहति
20.2.5.a.m: Having placed a silver plate in a vessel, having dished out the brahmaudana into it, having poured abundant melted butter over it, and having placed a golden plate over it, drawing it along without cutting into it, he serves it to four great officiating priests of ṛṣi descent.

20.2.6.a.m: To those who have eaten he gives four golden neck-ornaments worth a thousand [cows], four mule-drawn chariots, and these two plates.

20.2.7.a.m: The halter is twelve cubits or thirteen cubits long, made of darbha grass or of muñja grass.

20.2.8.a.m: He anoints it with the residue of the brahmaudana.

20.2.9.a.m: They teach the marks of the horse:

20.2.9.b.d: कृष्णः श्वेतः पिशङ्गः सारङ्गो ऽरुणपिशङ्गो वा
20.2.9.b.m: black, white, tawny, speckled, or reddish-tawny;

20.2.10.a.m: or if a white one has a little black, he should immolate that one.

20.2.10.b.s: mātṛmantaṃ prtṛmantaṃ pṛṣṭhe vahe ca dāntaṃ somapaṃ somapayoḥ putram
20.2.10.b.d: मातृमन्तं प्र्तृमन्तं पृष्ठे वहे च दान्तं सोमपं सोमपयोः पुत्रम्
20.2.10.b.m: [It should be] with a known mother, with a known father, trained to the back and to the draught, soma-drinking, the offspring of two soma-drinkers.

20.2.11.a.s: vijñāyata eṣa vai somapo yaṃ śiśuṃ jātaṃ purā tṛṇādyātsomaṃ pāyayanti /
20.2.11.a.d: विज्ञायत एष वै सोमपो यं शिशुं जातं पुरा तृणाद्यात्सोमं पाययन्ति ।
20.2.11.a.m: It is known [from the śruti]: 'This one is indeed a soma-drinker whom, when born as a foal, they make drink soma before he eats grass.'

20.2.11.b.s: etau vai samapau yau śiśū jātau purā tṛṇādyātsomaṃ pāyayantīti
20.2.11.b.d: एतौ वै समपौ यौ शिशू जातौ पुरा तृणाद्यात्सोमं पाययन्तीति
20.2.11.b.m: 'These two are indeed soma-drinkers whom, when born as foals, they make drink soma before they eat grass.'

20.2.12.a.m: He entrusts the adhvaryu with the kingdom:

20.3.1.a.m: 'O Brahmins and kings, this adhvaryu is your king.

20.3.1.b.m: Whatever reverence is mine, that belongs to you toward him.

20.3.1.c.m: Whatever he does for you, let that be done for you.'

20.3.2.a.m: For the duration of the sacrifice, the adhvaryu is king.

20.3.3.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti raśanāmādāyemāmagṛbhṇanraśanāmṛtasyetyabhimantrya brahmannaśvaṃ medhyaṃ bhantsyāmi devebhyo medhāya prajāpataye tena rādhyāsamiti brahmāṇamāmantrayate
20.3.3.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति रशनामादायेमामगृभ्णन्रशनामृतस्येत्यभिमन्त्र्य ब्रह्मन्नश्वं मेध्यं भन्त्स्यामि देवेभ्यो मेधाय प्रजापतये तेन राध्यासमिति ब्रह्माणमामन्त्रयते
20.3.3.a.m: Taking the halter with 'At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...', consecrating it with 'They took this halter of the truth...', he addresses the brahman priest: 'O brahman, I shall bind the sacrificial horse for the gods, for the sacrifice, for Prajāpati; may I succeed thereby.'

20.3.4.a.s: taṃ badhāna devebhyo medhāya prajāpataye tena rādhnuhīti pratyāha
20.3.4.a.d: तं बधान देवेभ्यो मेधाय प्रजापतये तेन राध्नुहीति प्रत्याह
20.3.4.a.m: He replies: 'Bind it for the gods, for the sacrifice, for Prajāpati; succeed thereby.'

20.3.5.a.m: He halters the horse with 'You are the halter...'

20.3.6.a.m: They bring a four-eyed dog bound with a cord around both sides.

20.3.7.a.m: The son of the father's younger sister leads it in front;

20.3.7.b.m: the son of the mother's younger sister [leads it] behind.

20.3.9.a.m: The son of an unchaste woman, having wrapped his knee with embroidered cloth, follows behind.

20.3.10.a.m: They make the horse and the dog plunge into the water.

20.3.11.a.d: यत्र शुनो ऽप्रतिष्ठा तदध्वर्युः प्रसौति जहीति
20.3.11.a.m: Where the dog has no foothold, there the adhvaryu gives the impulse: 'Kill [it]!'

20.3.12.a.s: yo arvantamiti saidhrakeṇa musalena pauṃścaleyaḥ śunaḥ prahanti
20.3.12.a.d: यो अर्वन्तमिति सैध्रकेण मुसलेन पौंश्चलेयः शुनः प्रहन्ति
20.3.12.a.m: With 'He who [seeks to kill] the steed...' [TS 7.5.9.2], the son of an unchaste woman strikes down the dog with the sidhraka pestle.

20.3.13.a.m: He throws it under the feet of the horse with 'Away is the mortal, away is the white one!' [TS 7.5.9.2]

20.3.14.a.s: dakṣiṇāpaplāvyāhaṃ ca tvaṃ ca vṛtrahanniti brahmā yajamānasya hastaṃ gṛhṇāti
20.3.14.a.d: दक्षिणापप्लाव्याहं च त्वं च वृत्रहन्निति ब्रह्मा यजमानस्य हस्तं गृह्णाति
20.3.14.a.m: Having caused the sacrificer to step towards the south, the Brahman takes the sacrificer's hand with: 'Both I and thou, O slayer of Vṛtra…'

20.3.15.a.m: The adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite: 'With skill, O Indra, thou becamest…'

20.3.16.a.m: They bring an extraction-pipe made of reed, tied with three straps.

20.3.17.a.m: To it a moist reed branch is bound.

20.3.18.a.m: Two hundred hold it on the south;

20.3.19.a.m: With it they sweep over the horse from east to west.

20.4.1.a.s: śatena rājaputraiḥ sahādhvaryuḥ purastātpratyaṅ tiṣṭhanprokṣatyanenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyaṃ rājā vṛtraṃ vadhyāditi
20.4.1.a.d: शतेन राजपुत्रैः सहाध्वर्युः पुरस्तात्प्रत्यङ् तिष्ठन्प्रोक्षत्यनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायं राजा वृत्रं वध्यादिति
20.4.1.a.m: Standing to the east and facing west together with a hundred princes, the adhvaryu sprinkles [it], saying: “Having sacrificed with this horse fit for sacrifice, may this king slay Vṛtra!”

20.4.2.a.s: śtenārājabhirugraiḥ saha brahmā dakṣiṇata udaṅ tiṣṭhanprokṣatyanenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyaṃ rājāpratidhṛṣyo 'stviti
20.4.2.a.d: श्तेनाराजभिरुग्रैः सह ब्रह्मा दक्षिणत उदङ् तिष्ठन्प्रोक्षत्यनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायं राजाप्रतिधृष्यो ऽस्त्विति
20.4.2.a.m: Standing to the south and facing north together with a hundred fierce non-royal men, the brahman sprinkles [it], saying: “Having sacrificed with this horse fit for sacrifice, may this king be unassailable!”

20.4.3.a.s: śatena sūtagrāmaṇibhiḥ saha hotā paścātprāṅ tiṣṭhanprokṣatyanenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyaṃ rājāsyai viśo bahugvai bahvaśvāyai bahvajāvikāyai bahuvrīhiyavāyai bahumāṣatilāyai bahuhiraṇyāyai bahuhastikāyai bahudāsapuruṣāyai rayimatyai puṣṭimatyai bahurāyaspoṣāyai rājāstviti
20.4.3.a.d: शतेन सूतग्रामणिभिः सह होता पश्चात्प्राङ् तिष्ठन्प्रोक्षत्यनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायं राजास्यै विशो बहुग्वै बह्वश्वायै बह्वजाविकायै बहुव्रीहियवायै बहुमाषतिलायै बहुहिरण्यायै बहुहस्तिकायै बहुदासपुरुषायै रयिमत्यै पुष्टिमत्यै बहुरायस्पोषायै राजास्त्विति
20.4.3.a.m: Standing to the west and facing east together with a hundred heralds and village chiefs, the hotṛ sprinkles [it], saying: “Having sacrificed with this horse fit for sacrifice, may this king be king of this subject folk that has many cows, many horses, many goats and sheep, many grains of rice and barley, many beans and sesamums, much gold, many elephants, many slaves and men, is rich in wealth, rich in nourishment, and has much increase of wealth!”

20.4.4.a.s: śatena kṣattṛsaṃgrahītṛbhiḥ sahodgātottarato dakṣiṇā tiṣṭhanprokṣatyanenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyaṃ rājā sarvamāyuretviti
20.4.4.a.d: शतेन क्षत्तृसंग्रहीतृभिः सहोद्गातोत्तरतो दक्षिणा तिष्ठन्प्रोक्षत्यनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायं राजा सर्वमायुरेत्विति
20.4.4.a.m: Standing to the north and facing south together with a hundred chamberlains and charioteers, the udgātṛ sprinkles [it], saying: “Having sacrificed with this horse fit for sacrifice, may this king attain a full lifespan!”

20.4.5.a.s: atraitamaiṣīkamapaplāvyānudakamaśvamākramayyāntarā sthānamākramaṇaṃ cedaṃ viṣṇuḥ pra tadviṣṇurdivo vā viṣṇavityaśvasya pade tisrovaiṣṇavīrhutvāśvasya stokānanumantrayate 'gnaye svāhā somāya svāheti
20.4.5.a.d: अत्रैतमैषीकमपप्लाव्यानुदकमश्वमाक्रमय्यान्तरा स्थानमाक्रमणं चेदं विष्णुः प्र तद्विष्णुर्दिवो वा विष्णवित्यश्वस्य पदे तिस्रोवैष्णवीर्हुत्वाश्वस्य स्तोकाननुमन्त्रयते ऽग्नये स्वाहा सोमाय स्वाहेति
20.4.5.a.m: Thereupon, having floated away that reed broom and made the horse step into waterless [ground], between the post and the stepping-place, having offered three [libations] to Viṣṇu with: “This Viṣṇu...”, “Forth this Viṣṇu...”, or “From the sky, O Viṣṇu...”, into the footprint of the horse, he accompanies with a mantra the drops of water from the horse, saying: “To Agni, svāhā! To Soma, svāhā!”

20.4.6.a.m: He repeats this section a hundred times, [making] an offering at every tenth;

20.5.1.a.m: Then he sprinkles it in each direction:

20.5.2.a.s: prajāpataye tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmīti purastātpratyaṅ tiṣṭhan
20.5.2.a.d: प्रजापतये त्वा जुष्टं प्रोक्षामीति पुरस्तात्प्रत्यङ् तिष्ठन्
20.5.2.a.m: Standing to the east facing west, with: “To Prajāpati, acceptable to you, I sprinkle you”;

20.5.3.a.m: to the south facing north, with: “To Indra and Agni, to you”;

20.5.4.a.m: to the west facing east, with: “To Vāyu, to you”;

20.5.5.a.m: to the north facing south, with: “To the All-gods, to you”;

20.5.6.a.m: downwards, with: “To the gods, to you”;

20.5.7.a.m: upwards, with: “To all the gods, to you”;

20.5.8.a.s: pṛthivyai tvāntarikṣāya tvā dive tveti śeṣam
20.5.8.a.d: पृथिव्यै त्वान्तरिक्षाय त्वा दिवे त्वेति शेषम्
20.5.8.a.m: the remainder with: “To earth, to you; to the atmosphere, to you; to heaven, to you.”

20.5.9.a.s: vibhūrmātrā prabhūḥ pitretyaśvasya dakṣiṇe karṇe yajamānamaśvanāmāni vācayitvāgnaye svāhā svāhendrāgnibhyāmiti pūrvahomānhutvā bhūrasi bhuve tvā bhavyāya tvā bhaviṣyate tvetyaśvamutsṛjya devā āśāpālā iti ratnibhyaḥ paridadāti
20.5.9.a.d: विभूर्मात्रा प्रभूः पित्रेत्यश्वस्य दक्षिणे कर्णे यजमानमश्वनामानि वाचयित्वाग्नये स्वाहा स्वाहेन्द्राग्निभ्यामिति पूर्वहोमान्हुत्वा भूरसि भुवे त्वा भव्याय त्वा भविष्यते त्वेत्यश्वमुत्सृज्य देवा आशापाला इति रत्निभ्यः परिददाति
20.5.9.a.m: Having made the sacrificer recite the names of the horse into the right ear of the horse with: “Extensive through the mother, powerful through the father...”, having offered the preliminary offerings with: “To Agni, svāhā! Svāhā to Indra and Agni...”, having released the horse with: “You are being, to being, to you; to that which has been, to you; to that which shall be, to you”, he delivers it over to the guardians with: “O gods, region-protectors...”.

20.5.11.a.m: They follow the horse without turning [it] back.

20.5.13.a.s: śataṃ talpyā rājaputrāḥ saṃnaddhāḥ saṃnaddhasārathinaḥ śatamugrā arājānaḥ saṃnaddhāḥ saṃnaddhasārathinaḥ śataṃ vaiśyā vipathinaḥ śataṃ śūdrā varūthinaḥ
20.5.13.a.d: शतं तल्प्या राजपुत्राः संनद्धाः संनद्धसारथिनः शतमुग्रा अराजानः संनद्धाः संनद्धसारथिनः शतं वैश्या विपथिनः शतं शूद्रा वरूथिनः
20.5.13.a.m: A hundred princes of the royal couch in armor, with armored charioteers; a hundred fierce non-royal men in armor, with armored charioteers; a hundred Vaiśyas in carts; a hundred Śūdras with shields.

20.5.14.a.m: They are the protectors of the horse.

20.5.15.a.m: Whichever brahmin family they approach, they should ask them: “How much of the horse sacrifice do you know?”

20.5.16.a.s: yo na vidyāttaṃ jitvā tasya gṛhātkhādaṃ pānaṃ copanivapeyuḥ
20.5.16.a.d: यो न विद्यात्तं जित्वा तस्य गृहात्खादं पानं चोपनिवपेयुः
20.5.16.a.m: Whichever does not know, having conquered him, they should take food and drink from his house.

20.5.17.a.m: Whatever cooked food belongs to non-brahmins, that is their food.

20.5.18.a.m: The dwelling is in the house of a chariot-maker.

20.5.19.a.s: iha dhṛtiḥ svāheti sāyamaśvasya caturṣu patsu catasro dhṛtīrjuhoti
20.5.19.a.d: इह धृतिः स्वाहेति सायमश्वस्य चतुर्षु पत्सु चतस्रो धृतीर्जुहोति
20.5.19.a.m: In the evening, with: “Here is stability, svāhā!”, he offers four stability offerings at the four feet of the horse.

20.6.1.a.m: In the morning, he portions out [an oblation] on eight potsherds to Savitṛ.

20.6.2.a.s: tasya purastātsviṣṭakṛta āyanāya svāhā prāyaṇāya svāhetyuddrāvāñjuhoti
20.6.2.a.d: तस्य पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृत आयनाय स्वाहा प्रायणाय स्वाहेत्युद्द्रावाञ्जुहोति
20.6.2.a.m: Before its Sviṣṭakṛt [offering], he offers the flow-offerings with: “To going, svāhā! To departure, svāhā!”

20.6.3.a.m: The horse's movements with: “To the sound īṃ, svāhā! To that which has made the sound īṃ, svāhā!”

20.6.4.a.s: añjyetāya svāhā kṛṣṇāya svāhā śvetāya svāhetyaṣṭācatvāriṃśatamaśvarūpāṇi /
20.6.4.a.d: अञ्ज्येताय स्वाहा कृष्णाय स्वाहा श्वेताय स्वाहेत्यष्टाचत्वारिंशतमश्वरूपाणि ।
20.6.4.a.m: The forty-eight forms of the horse with: “To the marked-colored, svāhā! To the black, svāhā! To the white, svāhā!”;

20.6.5.a.s: atra brāhmaṇo vīṇāgāthī gāyatītyadadā ityayajathā ityapaca iti tisraḥ
20.6.5.a.d: अत्र ब्राह्मणो वीणागाथी गायतीत्यददा इत्ययजथा इत्यपच इति तिस्रः
20.6.5.a.m: Here a brahmin lute-player sings three [verses]: “You gave...”, “You sacrificed...”, “You cooked...”.

20.6.6.a.m: At midday, [an oblation] on eleven potsherds to Savitṛ the Impeller;

20.6.6.b.m: in the afternoon, [an oblation] on twelve potsherds to Savitṛ the Enlivener.

20.6.7.a.s: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ hotā hiraṇyakaśipāvupaviśati pāriplavaṃ bhauvanyavaṃ cācikhyāsan
20.6.7.a.d: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं होता हिरण्यकशिपावुपविशति पारिप्लवं भौवन्यवं चाचिख्यासन्
20.6.7.a.m: To the south of the āhavanīya, the hotṛ sits down on a gold cushion wishing to narrate the cyclical tale and the genealogy of Bhuvana's descendants.

20.6.8.a.m: To the south of him, on two gold cushions, the brahman and the sacrificer [sit].

20.6.9.a.m: To the east, the adhvaryu on a golden grass mat.

20.6.10.a.m: To the south, the lute-playing troop sit down nearby.

20.6.11.a.m: When they are seated, the hotṛ addresses the adhvaryu: “O adhvaryu!”

20.6.13.a.s: saṃsthitayoradhvaryuḥ saṃpreṣyati vīṇāgṇakinaḥ pūrvaiḥ saha sukṛdbhī rājbhirimaṃ yajamānaṃ saṃgāyateti
20.6.13.a.d: संस्थितयोरध्वर्युः संप्रेष्यति वीणाग्णकिनः पूर्वैः सह सुकृद्भी राज्भिरिमं यजमानं संगायतेति
20.6.13.a.m: When the two [rites] are concluded, the adhvaryu gives the command: “Lute-players, sing along of this sacrificer together with the former kings of good deeds!”

20.6.14.a.s: sāyaṃ dhṛtiṣu hūyamānāsu rājanyo vīṇāgāthī gāyatītyajinā ityayudhyataḥ ityamuṃ saṃgrāmamahanniti tisraḥ
20.6.14.a.d: सायं धृतिषु हूयमानासु राजन्यो वीणागाथी गायतीत्यजिना इत्ययुध्यतः इत्यमुं संग्राममहन्निति तिस्रः
20.6.14.a.m: In the evening, while the stability offerings are being offered, a noble lute-player sings three [verses]: “You conquered...”, “You fought...”, “You won this battle...”.

20.7.1.a.m: In the evening and morning, two brahmin lute-players should sing.

20.7.2.a.m: In this way, these rites beginning with the Savitṛ rites are performed for a year.

20.7.3.a.m: Or he offers the horse's movements only once.

20.7.4.a.m: This year consists of thirty-day months.

20.7.5.a.m: When the offerings are completed, he gives a hundred [cows] and a cart with a draft animal to the two lute-players;

20.7.6.a.m: or two hundred and two carts with draft animals, according to some.

20.7.7.a.m: After the eleventh month, they tie the horse in a pen made of aśvattha wood.

20.7.8.a.m: They bring fodder to it when tied.

20.7.9.a.m: If illness should befall the horse, he should portion out [an oblation] on eight potsherds to Agni, a caru to Soma, and [an oblation] on eight potsherds to Savitṛ.

20.7.10.a.m: A caru to Pūṣan if it is lame.

20.7.11.a.m: [He offers] a caru to Rudra if a great deity should afflict [the horse].

20.7.12.a.m: He should offer a [cake] on twelve potsherds to Agni Vaiśvānara at a deer-mound if it should not return.

20.7.13.a.d: यद्यधीयादग्नये ऽंहोमुचे ऽष्टाकपालः सौर्यं पयो वायव्य आज्यभागः
20.7.13.a.m: If it should mate [with a mare], [there is] a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Aṃhomuc, milk to Sūrya, [and] a portion of clarified butter to Vāyu.

20.7.14.a.m: If it should mate with a mare, [he offers] a caru to Prajāpati or a [cake] on twelve potsherds.

20.7.15.a.m: If it should perish, [he offers] a caru to Vāyu.

20.7.16.a.m: If an invading army should capture it, [he offers a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra the Conqueror.

20.7.17.a.m: If they carry it off by force, [he offers a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra the Overcomer.

20.7.18.a.m: If it should go blind, [he offers] a caru to Sūrya or a [cake] on one potsherd.

20.7.19.a.m: If it should fall into a pit, [he offers] a caru to Viṣṇu.

20.7.20.a.s: yadyavijñātena yakṣmaṇā mriyeta prājāpatyaṃ caruṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vā
20.7.20.a.d: यद्यविज्ञातेन यक्ष्मणा म्रियेत प्राजापत्यं चरुं द्वादशकपालं वा
20.7.20.a.m: If it should die of an unknown disease, [he offers] a caru to Prajāpati or a [cake] on twelve potsherds.

20.8.1.a.m: If enemies should capture the horse, his sacrifice would be destroyed.

20.8.2.a.m: Then, having brought another [horse], they should sprinkle it.

20.8.3.a.m: On the last new-moon day of this year, he procures the ukhā pot.

20.8.4.a.m: The consecratory offering is the traidhātavīyā.

20.8.5.a.d: आकूत्यै प्रयुजे ऽग्नये स्वाहेति चत्वार्यौद्ग्रहणानि जुहोति
20.8.5.a.m: With 'To intention, to impulse, to Agni svāhā', he offers the four audgrahaṇa libations.

20.8.6.a.m: With 'Svāhā to the thought, to what has been thought svāhā', [he offers] three vaiśvadeva libations.

20.8.7.a.m: This is an extended time for the consecration offerings.

20.8.8.a.m: For seven days, day after day, he performs [the offerings] with the subsequent audgrahaṇa and vaiśvadeva libations.

20.8.9.a.m: On the last day, he offers six audgrahaṇa libations;

20.8.9.b.m: with 'To all svāhā', the last full-offering.

20.8.10.a.m: For six days he performs [the rite] with [an offering] to Agni-and-Viṣṇu.

20.8.11.a.m: On the seventh day, [there is] the āgnikī [iṣṭi] with three oblations—such is the Vājasaneyaka [view].

20.8.12.a.m: With the season-consecration mantras beginning with 'Bhūḥ, for the ritual of the gods', he addresses [the sacrificer] mounting the black antelope skin.

20.8.13.a.s: ā brahmanbrāhmaṇo brahmavarcasī jāyatāṃ jajñi bījamiti jātamukhyamupatiṣṭhate
20.8.13.a.d: आ ब्रह्मन्ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चसी जायतां जज्ञि बीजमिति जातमुख्यमुपतिष्ठते
20.8.13.a.m: With 'May a brāhmaṇa be born in the sacred power, radiant with sacred knowledge! A seed born...', he attends the [fire] born in the ukhā pot.

20.8.14.a.s: visṛṣṭavāci yajamāne saṃpreṣyati vīṇāgaṇakino devairimaṃ yajamānaṃ saṃgāyateti
20.8.14.a.d: विसृष्टवाचि यजमाने संप्रेष्यति वीणागणकिनो देवैरिमं यजमानं संगायतेति
20.8.14.a.m: When the sacrificer has released his speech, he calls: 'Lute-players, sing of this sacrificer together with the gods!'

20.8.16.a.m: 'Together with Prajāpati during the pressing days, the avabhṛtha, the concluding offering, the anubandhyā, and the udavasānīyā'—

20.9.1.a.m: At the time of the altar ground, the altar ground is twice as large;

20.9.1.b.m: the fire-altar is thrice as large, or twenty-one-fold.

20.9.2.a.s: vaiśvānareṇa pracaryāgnaye gāyatrāyeti daśahaviṣaṃ sarvapṛṣṭhāṃ nirvapati
20.9.2.a.d: वैश्वानरेण प्रचर्याग्नये गायत्रायेति दशहविषं सर्वपृष्ठां निर्वपति
20.9.2.a.m: Having performed [the rite] with the vaiśvānara [cake], he offers the sarvapṛṣṭhā [iṣṭi] of ten oblations, beginning with '[To Agni] Gāyatra'.

20.9.3.a.m: The invitatory and consecratory verses are according to their characteristic marks: 'The fuel of the directions...', 'According to our wish...'

20.9.4.a.s: kastvā yunakti sa tvā yunaktviti paridhīnyunakti
20.9.4.a.d: कस्त्वा युनक्ति स त्वा युनक्त्विति परिधीन्युनक्ति
20.9.4.a.m: With 'Who yokes thee? May he yoke thee', he yokes the enclosing sticks.

20.9.5.a.s: asya yajñasyarddhyai mahyaṃ saṃnatyā iti sarvatrānuṣajati
20.9.5.a.d: अस्य यज्ञस्यर्द्ध्यै मह्यं संनत्या इति सर्वत्रानुषजति
20.9.5.a.m: He attaches everywhere [the words]: 'For the prosperity of this sacrifice, for submission to me.'

20.9.6.a.m: On the two cart-transporters of the havirdhāna [hall], he erects the central post facing the fire, made of rājjuda-wood, twenty-one cubits long.

20.9.7.b.m: three of bilva-wood to the south;

20.9.7.d.m: three of khadira-wood to the south;

20.9.7.f.m: three of palāśa-wood to the south;

20.9.8.a.m: Some say the khadira or the palāśa [posts] are at the ends.

20.9.9.a.m: There is a Brāhmaṇa passage of the Kālabavins: 'They erect eleven sets of eleven [posts] facing east.'

20.9.10.a.m: Fourfold waters are fetched from the directions.

20.9.11.a.m: From them he draws the vasatīvarī waters.

20.9.12.a.m: On the morrow, the first of the two Gautama-catuṣṭomas, possessing the Rathantara-sāman, is extended.

20.9.13.a.m: At the time of the animal sacrifice, he brings forward the pressing animal sacred to Agni,

20.9.14.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle yadabrāhmaṇānāṃ dikṣu vittaṃ tattryahe samaśaḥ prativibhajyānvahaṃ dadāti
20.9.14.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले यदब्राह्मणानां दिक्षु वित्तं तत्त्र्यहे समशः प्रतिविभज्यान्वहं ददाति
20.9.14.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gift, dividing equally over the three days whatever property belongs to non-brāhmaṇas in the directions, he gives it day after day:

20.10.1.a.m: the eastern direction to the adhvaryu;

20.10.1.e.m: whatever is other than the earth and human beings;

20.10.2.a.m: He gives the chief queen (mahiṣī) to the brahman;

20.10.2.d.m: [and] the pālākalī to the adhvaryu's [assistants]—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

20.10.3.a.m: The day concludes ending with the Patnīsaṃyājas.

20.10.4.a.m: When the day is concluded, around the āhavanīya they set up thirty-six wooden stands made of aśvattha wood.

20.10.5.a.s: astamita āditye ṣaṭtriṃśatamadhvaryava upatalpānadhiruhya khādiraiḥ sruvaiḥ sarvāṃ rātrimannahomāñjuhvati /
20.10.5.a.d: अस्तमित आदित्ये षट्त्रिंशतमध्वर्यव उपतल्पानधिरुह्य खादिरैः स्रुवैः सर्वां रात्रिमन्नहोमाञ्जुह्वति ।
20.10.5.a.m: When the sun has set, thirty-six adhvaryus, having climbed upon the stands, offer the food offerings throughout the whole night with khadira dipping spoons:

20.10.5.b.m: clarified butter, honey, husked rice, flattened rice, parched grains, barley porridge, roasted grain, groats, lentils, and millet groats.

20.10.6.b.m: he offers with clarified butter, he offers with parched grains, he offers with roasted grain, he offers with groats.

20.10.7.a.m: Of these anuvākas beginning with 'To one, svāhā', [he offers] the odd ones with clarified butter, and the even ones with food.

20.10.8.a.s: atra prayuktānāṃ prayokṣyamāṇānāṃ ca mantrāṇāṃ prayogameke samāmananti
20.10.8.a.d: अत्र प्रयुक्तानां प्रयोक्ष्यमाणानां च मन्त्राणां प्रयोगमेके समामनन्ति
20.10.8.a.m: Some teach here the recitation of the formulas that have been employed and that are to be employed:

20.11.1.a.m: the horse names with 'Vibhū through the mother, prabhū through the father';

20.11.2.a.m: the uddrāva offerings with 'To coming, svāhā! To departing, svāhā!';

20.11.3.a.m: the preliminary offerings with 'To Agni, svāhā! To Soma, svāhā!';

20.11.4.a.s: pṛthivyai svāhāntarikṣāya svāhetyetaṃ hutvāgnaye svāhā somāya svāheti pūrvadīkṣāḥ
20.11.4.a.d: पृथिव्यै स्वाहान्तरिक्षाय स्वाहेत्येतं हुत्वाग्नये स्वाहा सोमाय स्वाहेति पूर्वदीक्षाः
20.11.4.a.m: having offered this [anuvāka] 'To the earth, svāhā! To the intermediate space, svāhā!', the prior consecration offerings with 'To Agni, svāhā! To Soma, svāhā!';

20.11.5.a.m: the twenty-one-part consecration offering with 'To the earth, svāhā! To the intermediate space, svāhā!';

20.11.6.a.m: the seasonal consecration offerings with 'Bhuvas! For the rite of the gods';

20.11.7.a.s: agnaye svāhā vāyave svāhetyetaṃ hutvārvāṅyajñaḥ saṃ krāmatvityāptīḥ
20.11.7.a.d: अग्नये स्वाहा वायवे स्वाहेत्येतं हुत्वार्वाङ्यज्ञः सं क्रामत्वित्याप्तीः
20.11.7.a.m: having offered this [anuvāka] 'To Agni, svāhā! To Vāyu, svāhā!', the attainment offerings with 'May the sacrifice turn towards us';

20.11.8.a.m: the completion offerings with 'Past, present, future';

20.11.9.a.m: the ābhū offerings with 'May homes belong to me';

20.11.10.a.m: the anubhū offerings with 'Heat accompanied Agni';

20.11.11.a.m: the All-Gods formulas taken all together with 'Svāhā to the over-reflection, svāhā to the thought';

20.11.12.a.m: the limb offerings with 'To the teeth, svāhā! To the jaws, svāhā!';

20.11.13.a.s: añjyetāya svāhā kṛṣṇāya svāhā śvetāya svāhetyaśvarūpāṇi
20.11.13.a.d: अञ्ज्येताय स्वाहा कृष्णाय स्वाहा श्वेताय स्वाहेत्यश्वरूपाणि
20.11.13.a.m: the horse-color offerings with 'To the spotted-marked, svāhā! To the black, svāhā! To the white, svāhā!';

20.11.14.a.m: the plant offerings with 'To the herbs, svāhā! To the roots, svāhā!';

20.11.15.a.m: the tree offerings with 'To the lordly trees, svāhā!';

20.11.16.a.m: the apāvya offerings with 'May the ram protect you with cooked meats';

20.11.17.a.m: the water offerings with 'To the well-waters, svāhā! To the waters, svāhā!';

20.11.18.a.s: ambhobhyaḥ svāhā nabhobhyaḥ svāhā mahobhyaḥ svāhetyambhāṃsi nabhāṃsi mahāṃsi
20.11.18.a.d: अम्भोभ्यः स्वाहा नभोभ्यः स्वाहा महोभ्यः स्वाहेत्यम्भांसि नभांसि महांसि
20.11.18.a.m: the waters, skies, and lights with 'To the waters, svāhā! To the skies, svāhā! To the lights, svāhā!';

20.12.1.a.m: the barley offerings with 'Homage to the King, homage to Varuṇa';

20.12.2.a.m: the cow offerings with 'May the wind blow beneficent upon the cows';

20.12.3.a.m: the continuity offerings with 'To the in-breath, svāhā! To the out-breath, svāhā!';

20.12.4.a.m: the release offerings with 'To the bound, svāhā! To the unbound, svāhā!';

20.12.5.a.s: pṛthivyai svāhāntarikṣāya svāhetyetaṃ hutvā datvate svāhādantakāya svāheti śarīrahomān
20.12.5.a.d: पृथिव्यै स्वाहान्तरिक्षाय स्वाहेत्येतं हुत्वा दत्वते स्वाहादन्तकाय स्वाहेति शरीरहोमान्
20.12.5.a.m: having offered this [anuvāka] 'To the earth, svāhā! To the intermediate space, svāhā!', the body offerings with 'To the toothed, svāhā! To the toothless, svāhā!';

20.12.6.a.s: yaḥ prāṇato ya ātmadā iti mahimānau
20.12.6.a.d: यः प्राणतो य आत्मदा इति महिमानौ
20.12.6.a.m: the two mahiman offerings with 'He who by breath' and 'He who is the soul-giver';

20.12.7.a.s: ā brahmanbrāhmaṇo brahmavarcasī jāyatāmiti samastāni brahmavarcasāni
20.12.7.a.d: आ ब्रह्मन्ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चसी जायतामिति समस्तानि ब्रह्मवर्चसानि
20.12.7.a.m: the priestly-splendor formulas taken all together with 'O Brahman, may a brāhmaṇa be born endowed with priestly splendor';

20.12.8.a.s: jajñi bījamityetaṃ hutvāgnaye samanamatpṛthivyai samanamaditi saṃnatihomān
20.12.8.a.d: जज्ञि बीजमित्येतं हुत्वाग्नये समनमत्पृथिव्यै समनमदिति संनतिहोमान्
20.12.8.a.m: having offered this [anuvāka] 'The seed has been born', the obedience offerings with 'It bowed to Agni; it bowed to the earth';

20.12.9.a.s: bhūtāya svāhā bhaviṣyate svāheti bhūtābhavyau homau
20.12.9.a.d: भूताय स्वाहा भविष्यते स्वाहेति भूताभव्यौ होमौ
20.12.9.a.m: the two offerings for what was and what will be with 'To that which has been, svāhā! To that which shall be, svāhā!';

20.12.10.a.s: yadakrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamāna ityaśvastomīyaṃ hutvaikasmai svāhetyetānanuvākānpunaḥpunarabhyāsaṃ rātriśeṣaṃ hutvoṣase svāhetyuṣasi /
20.12.10.a.d: यदक्रन्दः प्रथमं जायमान इत्यश्वस्तोमीयं हुत्वैकस्मै स्वाहेत्येताननुवाकान्पुनःपुनरभ्यासं रात्रिशेषं हुत्वोषसे स्वाहेत्युषसि ।
20.12.10.a.m: having offered the horse-praise offering with 'When first being born you neighed', and having offered repeatedly for the remainder of the night these anuvākas beginning with 'To one, svāhā', [he offers] at dawn with 'To the dawn, svāhā!';

20.12.10.b.m: while it is dawning, with 'To the brightening [dawn], svāhā!';

20.12.10.c.m: when it has dawned, with 'To the dawn break, svāhā!';

20.12.10.d.m: just before sunrise, with 'To that which is about to rise, svāhā!';

20.12.10.f.s: uditāya svāhā suvargāya svāhā lokāya svāhetyudite hutvā prajñātānannapariśeṣānnidadhāti
20.12.10.f.d: उदिताय स्वाहा सुवर्गाय स्वाहा लोकाय स्वाहेत्युदिते हुत्वा प्रज्ञातानन्नपरिशेषान्निदधाति
20.12.10.f.m: and when it has risen, having offered with 'To the risen [sun], svāhā! To the heavenly, svāhā! To the world, svāhā!', he sets down in a known place the remnants of the food.

20.13.1.a.m: The twenty-one-fold Ukthya with the Mahānāmnī sāmans proceeds.

20.13.2.a.s: antareṇāgrayaṇokthyau somamabhiṣutya yaḥ prāṇato ya ātmadā iti mahimānau gṛhṇāti /
20.13.2.a.d: अन्तरेणाग्रयणोक्थ्यौ सोममभिषुत्य यः प्राणतो य आत्मदा इति महिमानौ गृह्णाति ।
20.13.2.a.m: Between the Āgrayaṇa and Ukthya [grahas], having pressed the soma, he draws the two Mahiman grahas with 'He who by breath' and 'He who is the soul-giver':

20.13.2.b.m: the first with a silver [cup], the second with a golden one.

20.13.3.a.m: He sets down the first with 'The sun is your greatness';

20.13.3.b.m: the second with 'The moon is your greatness'.

20.13.4.a.s: āyuryajñasya pavate madhu priyaṃ pitā devānāṃ janitā vibhāvasuḥ /
20.13.4.a.d: आयुर्यज्ञस्य पवते मधु प्रियं पिता देवानां जनिता विभावसुः ।
20.13.4.a.m: “The dear sweet life of the sacrifice purifies itself, the father of the gods, the creator, shining brightly...”

20.13.4.b.s: dadhāti ratnaṃ svadhayorapīcyaṃ madhintamo matsara indriyo rasa ityaśvasya grīvāsu sauvarṇaniṣkaṃ pratimucyāgniste vājinyuṅṅanu tvārabha iti vāladhāvaśvamanvārabhya bahiṣpavamānaṃ sarpantyagnirmūrdheti
20.13.4.b.d: दधाति रत्नं स्वधयोरपीच्यं मधिन्तमो मत्सर इन्द्रियो रस इत्यश्वस्य ग्रीवासु सौवर्णनिष्कं प्रतिमुच्याग्निस्ते वाजिन्युङ्ङनु त्वारभ इति वालधावश्वमन्वारभ्य बहिष्पवमानं सर्पन्त्यग्निर्मूर्धेति
20.13.4.b.m: 'He places the secret gem in the two self-powers, the most intoxicating, exhilarating, vigorous sap'—having fastened a golden breast-ornament onto the neck of the horse with this [verse], and having touched the horse along its tail with 'May Agni, your courser, be yoked; I take hold behind you', they glide to the Bahiṣpavamāna [chant] with 'Agni is the head'.

20.13.5.a.m: Excluding the udgātṛ, he chooses the horse for the udgītha.

20.13.6.a.m: They shut in mares near him.

20.13.7.a.m: When he whickers towards them, that is the udgītha;

20.13.7.b.m: when they whicker back in response, that is the upagītha.

20.13.8.a.s: udagāsīdaśvo medhyo yajñiya iti śatena śatapalena ca niṣkeṇodgātāramupaśikṣyemāṃ devatāmudgāyantīmanūdgāyeti saṃpreṣyati
20.13.8.a.d: उदगासीदश्वो मेध्यो यज्ञिय इति शतेन शतपलेन च निष्केणोद्गातारमुपशिक्ष्येमां देवतामुद्गायन्तीमनूद्गायेति संप्रेष्यति
20.13.8.a.m: Having appeased the udgātṛ with a hundred [cows] and an ornament weighing a hundred palas, saying: 'The sacrificial, sacred horse has sung the udgītha', he gives the ritual call: 'Sing the udgītha after this singing deity!'

20.13.9.a.m: With that gold he undertakes the chant;

20.13.11.a.s: namo rajñe namo varuṇāyeti vetasaśākhayāśvatūparagomṛgānagniṣṭha upākaroti yeṣāṃ cānādiṣṭo deśaḥ
20.13.11.a.d: नमो रज्ञे नमो वरुणायेति वेतसशाखयाश्वतूपरगोमृगानग्निष्ठ उपाकरोति येषां चानादिष्टो देशः
20.13.11.a.m: With a branch of reed, with 'Homage to the King, homage to Varuṇa', he assigns at the post closest to the fire the horse, the hornless goat, and the gomṛga, and those [animals] whose place is not specified;

20.13.12.a.m: with plakṣa branches, the other animals fastened to the horse:

20.13.12.b.m: in front, on the forehead, the black-necked one for Agni;

20.13.12.d.m: one sacred to Indra and Pūṣan above on the neck;

20.13.12.e.m: two black-necked ones sacred to Agni to the forelegs;

20.13.12.f.m: two hairy-thighed ones sacred to Tvaṣṭṛ to the thighs;

20.13.12.g.m: two white-backed ones sacred to Bṛhaspati along the back;

20.13.12.h.m: two, one white and one black, sacred to Sūrya and Yama, to the sides;

20.13.12.i.m: one with a speckled belly for Dhātṛ underneath;

20.13.12.j.m: [and] a white one sacred to Sūrya to the tail.

20.13.13.a.m: At [the posts] other than the central post, there are groups of eighteen [victims].

20.14.1.a.s: rohito dhūmrarohita iti navanava prativibhajyaindrāgnadaśamāneke samāmananti
20.14.1.a.d: रोहितो धूम्ररोहित इति नवनव प्रतिविभज्यैन्द्राग्नदशमानेके समामनन्ति
20.14.1.a.m: Some hand down [these] dividing them into nine each, [beginning with] 'the reddish, the smoky-reddish', with one sacred to Indra and Agni as the tenth;

20.14.3.a.m: They hold them in the intervals between the sacrificial posts.

20.14.4.a.s: indrāya rājñe sūkara ityekādaśa daśata ālabhyante
20.14.4.a.d: इन्द्राय राज्ञे सूकर इत्येकादश दशत आलभ्यन्ते
20.14.4.a.m: Eleven sets of ten are seized, [beginning with] 'A hog for King Indra'.

20.14.6.e.m: leprous-spotted ones belong to the stars: these are the groups of fifteen.

20.14.10.a.m: He seizes first-borns for Agni Anīkavat;

20.14.10.b.m: those born in the same year for the Sāṃtapana Maruts;

20.14.10.d.m: intermingled ones for the Krīḍin Maruts;

20.14.10.e.m: subsequently produced ones for the Svatavat Maruts.

20.14.13.a.m: For the ancestors accompanied by Soma, brown ones with a smoky tinge;

20.14.13.b.m: for the ancestors seated on the sacrificial grass, smoky ones with a brown tinge;

20.14.13.c.m: for the ancestors consumed by fire, smoky ones; reddish ones sacred to Tryambaka.

20.15.3.e.m: white ones sacred to Sūrya: these are the Cāturmāsya animals.

20.15.4.a.m: They seize two sets of eleven:

20.15.4.b.m: the standard ones and the Aśvamedha ones.

20.15.5.a.m: The Aśvamedha ones [are those beginning with] 'for Agni Anīkavat'.

20.15.5.b.m: “To King Soma”, these are the pairs [of formulas].

20.15.6.a.m: When it is brought near, he offers with: “To the one brought near, svāhā!”

20.15.6.b.m: With the formula 'Svāhā to the one who has been seized', he offers when [the horse] has been tied to the post.

20.15.7.b.m: the chief queen (mahiṣī), the favorite wife (vāvātā), and the discarded wife (parivṛktī).

20.15.8.a.m: Each one has one hundred female attendants:

20.15.8.b.m: princesses, wives of nobles, of non-kings, and of heralds and village headmen.

20.15.9.a.m: There are a thousand beads each, made of gold, silver, and sea-shells.

20.15.10.b.m: With 'Bhūḥ', the chief queen weaves the golden beads forward from the shoulder-yoke.

20.15.10.c.m: With 'Bhuvaḥ', the favorite wife weaves the silver beads back from the shoulder-yoke and forward from the hips.

20.15.10.d.m: With 'Suvaḥ', the discarded wife weaves the sea-shell beads back from the hips.

20.15.11.a.m: Maidens tie shell beads into the hair so that they do not slip off;

20.15.12.a.m: Then they anoint its various body parts with clarified butter.

20.15.12.b.m: The chief queen [anoints] with guggulu-ointment, with the formula 'May the Vasus anoint you with the Gāyatrī meter!'

20.15.12.c.m: The favorite wife [anoints] with kāsāmba-ointment, with 'May the Rudras [anoint you with the Triṣṭubh meter]!'

20.15.12.d.m: The discarded wife [anoints] with mustā-ointment, with 'May the Ādityas [anoint you with the Jagatī meter]!'

20.15.13.a.m: 'Fragrant with guggulu-ointment, the horse has been brought forward for the sacrifice.

20.15.13.b.m: About to be sent forth to the gods, O courser, bestowing splendor, become a conqueror of the world! //'

20.15.13.c.m: 'Fragrant with kāsāmba-ointment, the horse has been brought forward for the sacrifice.

20.15.13.d.m: About to be sent forth to the gods, O courser, bestowing splendor, become a conqueror of the world! //'

20.15.13.e.m: 'Fragrant with mustā-ointment, the horse has been brought forward for the sacrifice.

20.15.13.f.m: About to be sent forth to the gods, O courser, bestowing splendor, become a conqueror of the world!'—with these formulas respectively [they also anoint him].

20.16.1.a.m: With 'They yoke the tawny steed...', he yokes this horse to the right yoke-pin.

20.16.2.a.m: With 'They yoke his desirable [steeds]...', [he yokes] the two side-horses.

20.16.3.a.m: With 'Making a banner for the bannerless...', he fastens the flag to the chariot.

20.16.4.a.m: With 'Like a storm cloud...', he puts on the coat of mail.

20.16.5.a.m: With 'With the bow may we win cattle...', he takes up the bow.

20.16.6.a.m: With 'As if about to speak...', he touches the bowstring.

20.16.7.a.m: With 'These two arriving together...', he touches the two notches of the bow.

20.16.8.a.s: bahvīnāṃ pitā bahurasya putra iti pṛṣṭha iṣudhiṃ ninahyati
20.16.8.a.d: बह्वीनां पिता बहुरस्य पुत्र इति पृष्ठ इषुधिं निनह्यति
20.16.8.a.m: With 'Father of many, many are his sons...', he ties the quiver to his back.

20.16.9.a.m: With 'Standing in the chariot, he guides the coursers...', he addresses the charioteer with a mantra.

20.16.10.a.m: With 'Loud cries they make, raising their hoofs...', [he addresses] the horses.

20.16.11.a.s: svāduṣaṃsadaḥ pitaro vayodhā iti tisṛbhiḥ pitṝnupatiṣṭhate
20.16.11.a.d: स्वादुषंसदः पितरो वयोधा इति तिसृभिः पितॄनुपतिष्ठते
20.16.11.a.m: With the three verses beginning 'Sweet-assemblied, the fathers, granting vigor...', he pays homage to the fathers.

20.16.12.a.s: ṛjīte pari vṛṅgdhi na ityātmānaṃ pratyabhimṛśyā jaṅghantītyaśvājanimādāyāhiriva bhogairiti hastaghnamabhimantrayate
20.16.12.a.d: ऋजीते परि वृङ्ग्धि न इत्यात्मानं प्रत्यभिमृश्या जङ्घन्तीत्यश्वाजनिमादायाहिरिव भोगैरिति हस्तघ्नमभिमन्त्रयते
20.16.12.a.m: Having touched himself with 'O swift one, spare us!', and having taken up the horsewhip with 'Striking repeatedly...', he addresses the arm-guard with 'Like a serpent with its coils...'.

20.16.13.a.s: vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyā iti pañcabhī ratham
20.16.13.a.d: वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूया इति पञ्चभी रथम्
20.16.13.a.m: With the five verses beginning 'O tree, may you have strong limbs...', [he addresses] the chariot.

20.16.14.a.m: With 'O drum, turn these back, possessing a banner...', they beat the war drums.

20.16.15.a.s: ākrānvājī kramairatyakramīdvājītyudagudakāntamabhiprayāya ye te panthānaḥ savitarityadhvaryuryajamānaṃ vācayati
20.16.15.a.d: आक्रान्वाजी क्रमैरत्यक्रमीद्वाजीत्युदगुदकान्तमभिप्रयाय ये ते पन्थानः सवितरित्यध्वर्युर्यजमानं वाचयति
20.16.15.a.m: With 'The courser has strode forward; with his strides the courser has surpassed...', having driven out northwards to the edge of the water, the adhvaryu causes the sacrificer to recite: 'Whatever paths are yours, O Savitṛ...'.

20.16.16.a.s: svayaṃ vājinnapo 'vajighretyapo 'śvamavaghrāpya yadvāto apo agamaditi pradakṣiṇamāvartayati
20.16.16.a.d: स्वयं वाजिन्नपो ऽवजिघ्रेत्यपो ऽश्वमवघ्राप्य यद्वातो अपो अगमदिति प्रदक्षिणमावर्तयति
20.16.16.a.m: Having made the horse sniff the water with 'Yourself, O courser, sniff the water!', he turns it around clockwise with 'When the wind went to the waters...'.

20.16.17.a.m: He halts where he set out from.

20.16.18.a.s: vi te muñcāmītyetamaśvaṃ vimucya rathavāhanaṃ havirasya nāmeti rathavāhane rathamatyādhāya dyauste pṛṣṭhamityaśvasya pṛṣṭhaṃ saṃmārṣṭi
20.16.18.a.d: वि ते मुञ्चामीत्येतमश्वं विमुच्य रथवाहनं हविरस्य नामेति रथवाहने रथमत्याधाय द्यौस्ते पृष्ठमित्यश्वस्य पृष्ठं संमार्ष्टि
20.16.18.a.m: Having unyoked this horse with 'I unyoke you...', and having placed the chariot onto the chariot-stand with 'Chariot-stand, oblation is its name...', he strokes the horse's back with 'Heaven is your back...'.

20.16.19.a.m: With 'O grain! O barley! Mine is the fame!', the wives scatter food-remnants before the horse.

20.16.20.a.m: Whichever [wife's food] it eats when scattered down, to hers belong the offspring and the kingdom.

20.17.1.a.s: ākrānvājī kramairatyakramīdvājī dyauste pṛṣṭhamityaśvamabhimantrya yathopākṛtaṃ niyujya prokṣyopapāyayati
20.17.1.a.d: आक्रान्वाजी क्रमैरत्यक्रमीद्वाजी द्यौस्ते पृष्ठमित्यश्वमभिमन्त्र्य यथोपाकृतं नियुज्य प्रोक्ष्योपपाययति
20.17.1.a.m: Having addressed the horse with 'The courser has strode forward; with his strides the courser has surpassed...' and 'Heaven is your back...', having tied him as he was brought forward, and having sprinkled him, he gives him water to drink.

20.17.2.a.m: If he does not drink when given water, he should make him drink with 'Agni was the animal...'.

20.17.3.a.m: The āprī verses of the horse are those beginning with 'Kindled, anointing the chamber of prayers...'.

20.17.4.a.d: मेषस्त्वा पचतैरवत्विति पर्यग्नौ क्रियमाणे ऽपाव्यानि जुहोति
20.17.4.a.m: While the fire is being carried around [the victims], he offers the apāvya oblations with 'May the ram protect you with cooked offerings...'.

20.17.5.a.m: After carrying the fire around them, they release the wild animals,

20.17.7.a.m: A goat is led in front of the horse.

20.17.8.a.s: vetasaśākhāyāṃ tārpyaṃ kṛttyadhīvāsaṃ hiraṇyakaśipu cāstīrya sauvarṇaṃ rukmamupariṣṭātkṛtvā tasminnaśvatūparagomṛgānnighnanti /
20.17.8.a.d: वेतसशाखायां तार्प्यं कृत्त्यधीवासं हिरण्यकशिपु चास्तीर्य सौवर्णं रुक्ममुपरिष्टात्कृत्वा तस्मिन्नश्वतूपरगोमृगान्निघ्नन्ति ।
20.17.8.a.m: Having spread out a reed mat, a cloth of tārpya, a garment of hide, and a gold cushion, and having placed a golden plate above, upon it they suffocate the horse, the hornless goat, and the gomṛga.

20.17.8.b.m: On plakṣa branches [they suffocate] the other animal victims.

20.17.9.a.m: They suffocate the horse with a dark linen garment,

20.17.9.b.m: and the other victims with cords.

20.17.10.a.s: prāṇāya svāhā vyānāya svaheti saṃjñapyamāne paśāvāhutī juhoti /
20.17.10.a.d: प्राणाय स्वाहा व्यानाय स्वहेति संज्ञप्यमाने पशावाहुती जुहोति ।
20.17.10.a.m: While the animal is being suffocated, he offers two oblations with 'Svāhā to prāṇa! Svāhā to vyāna!'—

20.17.11.a.m: The prastotṛ waits upon [the horse] with the Yāma sāman.

20.17.12.a.m: With 'O mother! O little mother! O dear mother!', the pratiprasthātṛ brings up the wives.

20.17.13.a.s: tā dakṣiṇānkeśapakṣānudgrathya savyānprasrasya dakṣiṇānūrūnāghnānāḥ sigbhirabhidhūnvatyastriḥ pradakṣiṇamaśvaṃ pariyantyavantī stheti
20.17.13.a.d: ता दक्षिणान्केशपक्षानुद्ग्रथ्य सव्यान्प्रस्रस्य दक्षिणानूरूनाघ्नानाः सिग्भिरभिधून्वत्यस्त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमश्वं परियन्त्यवन्ती स्थेति
20.17.13.a.m: Having tied up the locks of hair on their right sides and let down those on their left, beating their right thighs and fanning [the horse] with the skirts of their garments, they walk clockwise three times around the horse, reciting: 'You are helpers...'.

20.17.14.a.m: Having tied up the left locks and let down the right, beating their left thighs, not fanning, they walk three times counter-clockwise around [the horse].

20.17.17.a.m: With 'O mother, little mother, mother!' the chief queen, having lain down beside the horse,

20.18.1.a.s: gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ havāmaha ityabhimantryāhaṃ syāṃ tvaṃ syāḥ surāyāḥ kulajaḥ syāttatremāṃścaturaḥ pado vyatiṣajya śayāvahā iti pado vyatiṣajate
20.18.1.a.d: गणानां त्वा गणपतिं हवामह इत्यभिमन्त्र्याहं स्यां त्वं स्याः सुरायाः कुलजः स्यात्तत्रेमांश्चतुरः पदो व्यतिषज्य शयावहा इति पदो व्यतिषजते
20.18.1.a.m: having addressed it with 'We invoke you, the lord of hosts,' [and saying] 'May I be, may you be, may he be born of good family from the liquor; there, having intertwined these four legs, let us two lie,' intertwines her legs [with its legs].

20.18.2.a.s: tau saha caturaḥ padaḥ saṃ pra sārayāvahā iti padaḥ saṃprasārayate
20.18.2.a.d: तौ सह चतुरः पदः सं प्र सारयावहा इति पदः संप्रसारयते
20.18.2.a.m: [Saying] 'Let us two together stretch out the four legs,' she stretches out her legs.

20.18.3.a.s: subhage kāmpīlavāsinīti kṣaumeṇa vāsasādhvaryurmahiṣīmaśvaṃ ca pracchādya vṛṣā vāmityabhimantrayate
20.18.3.a.d: सुभगे काम्पीलवासिनीति क्षौमेण वाससाध्वर्युर्महिषीमश्वं च प्रच्छाद्य वृषा वामित्यभिमन्त्रयते
20.18.3.a.m: With 'O auspicious one, dwelling in Kāmpīla!' the adhvaryu, having covered the chief queen and the horse with a linen garment, addresses [them] with 'You two are stallions.'

20.18.4.a.s: utsakthyorgṛdaṃ dhehīti prajananena prajananaṃ saṃdhāyāmbe ambālyambika iti mahiṣyaśvaṃ garhate
20.18.4.a.d: उत्सक्थ्योर्गृदं धेहीति प्रजननेन प्रजननं संधायाम्बे अम्बाल्यम्बिक इति महिष्यश्वं गर्हते
20.18.4.a.m: Joining the generative organ to the generative organ with 'Place the organ between the thighs,' the chief queen reproaches the horse with 'O mother, little mother, mother!'

20.18.5.a.m: The wives taunt [her] with 'Raise her up!'

20.18.6.b.m: three times the wives taunt, each time with the subsequent verse.

20.18.7.a.s: dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣamiti sarvāḥ surabhimatīmṛcamantato japitvāpohiṣṭhīyābhirmārjayitvā gāyatrī triṣṭubiti dvābhyāṃ sauvarṇībhiḥ sūcībhirmahiṣyaśvasyāsipathānkalpayati prākkroḍāt /
20.18.7.a.d: दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषमिति सर्वाः सुरभिमतीमृचमन्ततो जपित्वापोहिष्ठीयाभिर्मार्जयित्वा गायत्री त्रिष्टुबिति द्वाभ्यां सौवर्णीभिः सूचीभिर्महिष्यश्वस्यासिपथान्कल्पयति प्राक्क्रोडात् ।
20.18.7.a.m: All of them, having murmured at the end the fragrant verse, 'I have sung the praise of Dadhikrāvan,' and having purified themselves with the verses to the waters, 'You waters are indeed healing,' the chief queen with two golden needles marks the knife-paths of the horse with 'The gāyatrī, the triṣṭubh,' forward from the chest;

20.18.7.b.m: likewise the favorite wife with the two subsequent silver ones, backward from the chest and forward from the navel;

20.18.7.c.m: likewise the discarded wife with the two subsequent copper or lead ones, the rest.

20.18.8.a.m: Silently they mark the knife-paths of the hornless goat and the wild ox.

20.18.9.a.s: kastvā chyati kastvā vi śāstītyaśvasya tvacamācchyati
20.18.9.a.d: कस्त्वा छ्यति कस्त्वा वि शास्तीत्यश्वस्य त्वचमाच्छ्यति
20.18.9.a.m: With 'Who cuts you? Who carves you?' he slits the skin of the horse.

20.18.13.a.m: Cutting off the ear, he binds it with the three limbs.

20.18.15.a.m: When the omenta are cooked, to the north, above the fire, he places the omenta of the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox on a branch of reed;

20.19.1.a.m: to the south, on branches of plakṣa, those of the other animals.

20.19.2.a.s: pūrvau parivapyamahimānau hutvāśvatūparagomṛgāṇāṃ vapāḥ samavadāya saṃpreṣyati
20.19.2.a.d: पूर्वौ परिवप्यमहिमानौ हुत्वाश्वतूपरगोमृगाणां वपाः समवदाय संप्रेष्यति
20.19.2.a.m: Having offered the two prior mahiman oblations connected with the omenta, having cut off portions together from the omenta of the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox, he calls out:

20.19.3.a.d: प्रजापतये ऽश्वस्य तूपरस्य गोमृगस्य वपानां मेदसामनुब्रूहि ।
20.19.3.a.m: 'Recite for Prajāpati [the invitatory verse] for the omenta and the fat of the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox.'

20.19.3.b.s: prajāpataye 'śvasya tūparasya gomṛgasya vapānāṃ medasāṃ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau /
20.19.3.b.d: प्रजापतये ऽश्वस्य तूपरस्य गोमृगस्य वपानां मेदसां प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ ।
20.19.3.b.m: 'Prompt for Prajāpati [the consecratory verse] for the omenta and the fat of the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox'—these are the two ritual calls;

20.19.3.c.m: or 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for the omenta and the fat of the candra and the omentum,' 'Prompt [the consecratory verse] for the omenta and the fat of the candra and the omentum.'

20.19.4.a.m: Having cut off portions together from the omenta of the others, he calls out:

20.19.5.a.s: viśvebhyo devebhya usrāṇāṃ chāgānāṃ meṣāṇāṃ vapānāṃ medasāmanubrūhi /
20.19.5.a.d: विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्य उस्राणां छागानां मेषाणां वपानां मेदसामनुब्रूहि ।
20.19.5.a.m: 'Recite for the All-gods [the invitatory verse] for the omenta and the fat of the cows, goats, and sheep.'

20.19.5.b.s: viśvebhyo devebhya usarāṇāṃ chāgānāṃ meṣāṇāṃ vapānāṃ medasāṃ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
20.19.5.b.d: विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्य उसराणां छागानां मेषाणां वपानां मेदसां प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
20.19.5.b.m: 'Prompt for the All-gods [the consecratory verse] for the omenta and the fat of the cows, goats, and sheep'—these are the two ritual calls.

20.19.6.a.s: uttaru parivapyamahimānau hutvā cātvāle mārjayitvābhito 'gniṣṭhaṃ brahmodyāya paryupaviśete /
20.19.6.a.d: उत्तरु परिवप्यमहिमानौ हुत्वा चात्वाले मार्जयित्वाभितो ऽग्निष्ठं ब्रह्मोद्याय पर्युपविशेते ।
20.19.6.a.m: Having offered the two subsequent mahiman oblations connected with the omenta and purified themselves at the cātvāla, they sit around the post nearest the fire on either side for the brahmodya;

20.19.7.a.s: kiṃ svidāsītpūrvacittirityetasyānuvākasya pṛṣṭāni hotuḥ pratijñātāni brahmaṇaḥ
20.19.7.a.d: किं स्विदासीत्पूर्वचित्तिरित्येतस्यानुवाकस्य पृष्टानि होतुः प्रतिज्ञातानि ब्रह्मणः
20.19.7.a.m: The questions of this anuvāka, 'What was the first conception?', belong to the hotṛ, and the answers to the brahman.

20.19.8.a.m: They announce the victory northward to the brahman.

20.19.9.a.s: prajāpataye 'śvasya tūparasya gomṛgasyāsthi loma ca tiryagasaṃbhindantaḥ sūkaraviśasaṃ viśamateti saṃpraiṣavatkurvanti
20.19.9.a.d: प्रजापतये ऽश्वस्य तूपरस्य गोमृगस्यास्थि लोम च तिर्यगसंभिन्दन्तः सूकरविशसं विशमतेति संप्रैषवत्कुर्वन्ति
20.19.9.a.m: With the ritual call: 'For Prajāpati, dismember the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox, according to the dismemberment of a boar, without cutting transversely across the bone and hair,' they act accordingly.

20.19.10.a.m: He deposits the blood of the horse for the sake of the sviṣṭakṛt.

20.19.11.a.s: śaphaṃ gomṛgakaṇṭhaṃ ca māhendrasya stotraṃ pratyabhiṣiñcati
20.19.11.a.d: शफं गोमृगकण्ठं च माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रं प्रत्यभिषिञ्चति
20.19.11.a.m: He sprinkles the hoof and the neck of the wild ox towards the chant for Mahendra.

20.19.12.a.s: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti ṣaṭ prājāpatyāḥ purastādabhiṣekasya juhoti /
20.19.12.a.d: हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति षट् प्राजापत्याः पुरस्तादभिषेकस्य जुहोति ।
20.19.12.a.m: With 'The golden germ came into being in the beginning,' he offers six oblations to Prajāpati before the consecration;

20.19.12.b.s: ayaṃ puro bhuva iti ṣaṭ ca prāṇabhṛtaḥ
20.19.12.b.d: अयं पुरो भुव इति षट् च प्राणभृतः
20.19.12.b.m: and the six prāṇabhṛt oblations with 'This one in front is the earth.'

20.19.13.a.m: He is consecrated upon a tiger skin or upon a lion skin.

20.20.1.a.m: They hold a bull skin above the one being consecrated.

20.20.2.a.s: sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa iti puruṣeṇa nārāyaṇena sauvarṇena śatamānena śatakṣareṇa śatakṛṣṇalena yajamānasya śīrṣannadhinidadhāti
20.20.2.a.d: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुष इति पुरुषेण नारायणेन सौवर्णेन शतमानेन शतक्षरेण शतकृष्णलेन यजमानस्य शीर्षन्नधिनिदधाति
20.20.2.a.m: With the puruṣasūkta, 'The Puruṣa has a thousand heads,' he places on the head of the sacrificer a golden [ornament] of one hundred mānas, one hundred syllables, and one hundred kṛṣṇalas.

20.20.3.a.s: prajāpatestvā prasave pṛthivyā nābhāvantarikṣasya bāhubhyāṃ divo hastābhyāṃ prajāpatestvā parameṣṭhinaḥ svārājyenābhiṣiñcāmīti mahimnoḥ saṃsrāveṇābhiṣiñcati
20.20.3.a.d: प्रजापतेस्त्वा प्रसवे पृथिव्या नाभावन्तरिक्षस्य बाहुभ्यां दिवो हस्ताभ्यां प्रजापतेस्त्वा परमेष्ठिनः स्वाराज्येनाभिषिञ्चामीति महिम्नोः संस्रावेणाभिषिञ्चति
20.20.3.a.m: With 'At the impulse of Prajāpati, on the navel of the earth, with the arms of the intermediate space, with the hands of heaven, I consecrate you with the sovereignty of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin,' he sprinkles [him] with the residue of the two mahiman draughts.

20.20.4.a.m: 'He sprinkles with the vāyavya cups,' say some.

20.20.5.a.m: He offers oblations over the one being consecrated with the names of the months, 'Madhu and Mādhava.'

20.20.6.a.m: Six to the seasons with 'Svāhā to spring! Svāhā to summer!'

20.20.7.a.s: vi na indra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ /
20.20.7.a.d: वि न इन्द्र मृधो जहि नीचा यच्छ पृतन्यतः ।
20.20.7.a.m: 'Smite away our foes, O Indra, strike down those who fight us;

20.20.7.b.m: Whoever assails us, send him down into darkness.

20.20.7.c.s: vi rakṣo vi mṛdho nuda vi vṛtrasya hanū ruja /
20.20.7.c.d: वि रक्षो वि मृधो नुद वि वृत्रस्य हनू रुज ।
20.20.7.c.m: Drive away the demon, drive away the foes, break the jaws of Vṛtra;

20.20.7.d.s: vi manyumindra vṛtrahannamitrasyābhidāsata iti vaimṛdhībhyāmā yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe
20.20.7.d.d: वि मन्युमिन्द्र वृत्रहन्नमित्रस्याभिदासत इति वैमृधीभ्यामा यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे
20.20.7.d.m: Smite the fury of the hostile foe who assails us, O Indra, killer of Vṛtra'—with these two vaimṛdha verses, the sacrificer wipes his face.

20.20.8.a.s: ūrdhvā asya samidho bhavantīti prājāpatyābhirāprībhirabhiṣicyamānasya hastaṃ gṛhṇāti
20.20.8.a.d: ऊर्ध्वा अस्य समिधो भवन्तीति प्राजापत्याभिराप्रीभिरभिषिच्यमानस्य हस्तं गृह्णाति
20.20.8.a.m: With 'Upright stand his kindling-sticks,' [and] with the Āprī verses to Prajāpati, he takes the hand of the one being consecrated.

20.20.9.b.s: prajāpatiṃ prathamaṃ yajñiyānāṃ devānāmagre yajataṃ yajadhvam /
20.20.9.b.d: प्रजापतिं प्रथमं यज्ञियानां देवानामग्रे यजतं यजध्वम् ।
20.20.9.b.m: Worship Prajāpati, first among those worthy of sacrifice, venerable at the head of the gods;

20.20.9.c.s: sa no dadātu draviṇaṃ suvīryaṃ rāyaspoṣaṃ vi ṣyatu nābhimasme //
20.20.9.c.d: स नो ददातु द्रविणं सुवीर्यं रायस्पोषं वि ष्यतु नाभिमस्मे ॥
20.20.9.c.m: May he give us wealth and good heroes; may he open the navel of the increase of riches unto us.

20.20.9.d.s: taveme lokāḥ pradiśo diśaśca parāvato nivata udvataśca /
20.20.9.d.d: तवेमे लोकाः प्रदिशो दिशश्च परावतो निवत उद्वतश्च ।
20.20.9.d.m: Yours are these worlds, intermediate regions, and quarters, the far distances, the depths, and the heights;

20.20.9.e.s: prajāpate viśvasṛjjīvadhanya idaṃ no deva pratiharya havyamiti ṣaṭ prājāpatyā upariṣṭādabhiṣekasya juhoti
20.20.9.e.d: प्रजापते विश्वसृज्जीवधन्य इदं नो देव प्रतिहर्य हव्यमिति षट् प्राजापत्या उपरिष्टादभिषेकस्य जुहोति
20.20.9.e.m: O Prajāpati, creator of all, rich in life, accept this our oblation, O god'—with these he offers six oblations to Prajāpati after the consecration;

20.20.10.a.m: and six apānabhṛt oblations with 'The eastern quarter of quarters.'

20.20.11.a.m: Here the sacrificer strides the viṣṇukrama strides in the jāgata meter.

20.21.1.a.s: paśukāla uttarata upariṣṭādagnervaitase kaṭe 'śvaṃ prāñcaṃ yathāṅgaṃ cinoti
20.21.1.a.d: पशुकाल उत्तरत उपरिष्टादग्नेर्वैतसे कटे ऽश्वं प्राञ्चं यथाङ्गं चिनोति
20.21.1.a.m: At the time of the animal sacrifice, to the north, above the fire, on a reed mat, he arranges the horse facing east, limb by limb.

20.21.2.a.m: In the same manner [he arranges] the hornless goat in front, facing west.

20.21.2.b.m: [He arranges] the wild ox (gomṛga) behind, facing east.

20.21.3.a.m: To the south, on branches of the plakṣa tree, he deposits the other animals.

20.21.5.a.m: He modifies the two endings with the word 'haviṣaḥ'.

20.21.6.a.s: ākrānvājī kramairatyakramīdvājī dyauste pṛṣṭhamiti vaitasena kaṭenāśvatūparagomṛgānsarvahutānhutveluvardāya svāhā balivardāya svāhetyaśvamabhijuhoti
20.21.6.a.d: आक्रान्वाजी क्रमैरत्यक्रमीद्वाजी द्यौस्ते पृष्ठमिति वैतसेन कटेनाश्वतूपरगोमृगान्सर्वहुतान्हुत्वेलुवर्दाय स्वाहा बलिवर्दाय स्वाहेत्यश्वमभिजुहोति
20.21.6.a.m: Having offered the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox completely with the reed mat, with the verses 'ākrānvājī', 'kramairatyakramīdvājī', and 'dyauste pṛṣṭham', he offers over the horse with 'iluvardāya svāhā balivardāya svāhā'.

20.21.7.a.m: At this point he throws the mat after [into the fire].

20.21.8.a.s: ye 'śvasya hutasya gandhamājighranti sarve te puṇyalokā bhavantīti vijñāyate
20.21.8.a.d: ये ऽश्वस्य हुतस्य गन्धमाजिघ्रन्ति सर्वे ते पुण्यलोका भवन्तीति विज्ञायते
20.21.8.a.m: 'All those who inhale the odor of the offered horse attain the world of merit'—so it is known.

20.21.9.a.s: haviṣā pracaryājyamavadānaṃ kṛtvā sogāndaṃṣṭrābhyāṃ maṇḍūkāñjambhyebhirityetaiścaturdaśabhiranuvākaiḥ pratimantraṃ śarīrahomāñjuhoti
20.21.9.a.d: हविषा प्रचर्याज्यमवदानं कृत्वा सोगान्दंष्ट्राभ्यां मण्डूकाञ्जम्भ्येभिरित्येतैश्चतुर्दशभिरनुवाकैः प्रतिमन्त्रं शरीरहोमाञ्जुहोति
20.21.9.a.m: Having performed the rites with the oblation and taken the portions of clarified butter, he offers the bodily oblations mantra by mantra with these fourteen sections: 'sogāndaṃṣṭrābhyāṃ maṇḍūkāñjambhyebhiḥ'.

20.21.10.a.m: [He offers] the divākīrtya section as the fifteenth.

20.21.10.b.m: [He offers] the araṇye'nuvākya section as the sixteenth.

20.21.10.c.m: [He offers] this seventeenth section, 'dyauste pṛṣṭham', with clarified butter alone.
