20.21.11.a.m: With these three sections, beginning with 'yadakrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamānaḥ', he offers thirty-six aśvastomīya oblations.

20.21.14.a.s: imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhemeti dvipadāḥ
20.21.14.a.d: इमा नु कं भुवना सीषधेमेति द्विपदाः
20.21.14.a.m: The two-verse stanzas begin with 'imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhema'.

20.21.15.a.d: अन्ततो ऽश्वस्य लोहितेन शृतेन स्विष्टकृतं यजति
20.21.15.a.m: Finally he sacrifices to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt with the cooked blood of the horse.

20.22.1.a.m: He offers the first oblation with the throat of the wild ox.

20.22.1.c.m: [He offers] the third with a vessel made of iron.

20.22.2.a.m: The day concludes with the patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

20.22.3.a.d: श्वो भूते प्रतायते सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रो बृहत्सामा
20.22.3.a.m: On the next day, an Atirātra sacrifice comprising all stomas and having the Bṛhatsāman is performed.

20.22.4.a.m: At the time of the animal sacrifice, they seize eleven bovine victims, either dedicated to Prajāpati or dedicated to the Viśvedevas.

20.22.4.b.s: prājāpatyamṛṣabhaṃ tūparaṃ sarvarūpaṃ sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyo dvādaśamupālambhyam
20.22.4.b.d: प्राजापत्यमृषभं तूपरं सर्वरूपं सर्वेभ्यः कामेभ्यो द्वादशमुपालम्भ्यम्
20.22.4.b.m: A hornless bull dedicated to Prajāpati, possessing all colors, is to be seized as the twelfth victim for the attainment of all desires.

20.22.6.a.s: avabhṛthena pracaryātreyaṃ śipiviṣṭaṃ khalatiṃ viklidhaṃ śuklaṃ piṅgākṣaṃ tilakāvalamavabhṛthamabhyavanīya tasya mūrdhañjuhoti mṛtyave svāha bhrūṇahatyāyai svāhā jumbakāya svāheti tisraḥ
20.22.6.a.d: अवभृथेन प्रचर्यात्रेयं शिपिविष्टं खलतिं विक्लिधं शुक्लं पिङ्गाक्षं तिलकावलमवभृथमभ्यवनीय तस्य मूर्धञ्जुहोति मृत्यवे स्वाह भ्रूणहत्यायै स्वाहा जुम्बकाय स्वाहेति तिस्रः
20.22.6.a.m: Having performed the purificatory bath rites, bringing down into the water of the avabhṛtha an Ātreya man who is white-spotted, bald, leprous, pale, hazel-eyed, and covered in white skin marks, he offers three oblations upon his head with: 'To Death, svāhā! To the murder of an embryo, svāhā! To Jumbaka, svāhā!'

20.22.7.a.m: He gives to him a hundred [cows] and a cart with yoked oxen.

20.22.8.a.m: Some say: two hundred [cows] and two carts with yoked oxen.

20.22.9.a.m: Together, the doers of good deeds and doers of evil deeds go up to the village holding hands.

20.22.9.b.m: 'All of them attain the world of merit'—so it is known.

20.22.10.a.m: Nine white barren cows dedicated to Sūrya are the anūbandhyā victims.

20.22.11.b.m: Reddish barren cows dedicated to Indra, white ones dedicated to the Sun, and white-backed ones dedicated to Bṛhaspati.

20.22.12.a.m: Or here he seizes victims in pairs.

20.22.13.a.s: chagalaḥ kalmāṣaḥ kikidīvirvidīgaya iti te trayastvāṣṭrāḥ
20.22.13.a.d: छगलः कल्माषः किकिदीविर्विदीगय इति ते त्रयस्त्वाष्ट्राः
20.22.13.a.m: A he-goat, a spotted animal, and a blue jay bird (kikidīvi)—these three belong to Tvaṣṭṛ.

20.22.14.a.s: pātnīvata āgneya aindrāgna āśvinaste viśālayūpa ālabhyante
20.22.14.a.d: पात्नीवत आग्नेय ऐन्द्राग्न आश्विनस्ते विशालयूप आलभ्यन्ते
20.22.14.a.m: The animal for Agni Pātnīvata, the one for Agni, the one for Indra-Agni, and the one for the Aśvins are seized at the branched sacrificial post (viśālayūpa).

20.23.1.b.s: traitānāṃ prathamajaṃ kālakābhrumaśvibhyāṃ madhyame viśālayūpa ālabhate /
20.23.1.b.d: त्रैतानां प्रथमजं कालकाभ्रुमश्विभ्यां मध्यमे विशालयूप आलभते ।
20.23.1.b.m: He seizes the firstborn of a triplet of animals, blackish-brown, for the Aśvins at the central branched sacrificial post.

20.23.1.c.m: He seizes the middleborn of these same [triplets] for Vigour at the southern post.

20.23.1.d.m: [He seizes] the lastborn for the Earth at the northern post.

20.23.2.a.d: तेषां पशुपुरोडाशानग्नये ऽंहोमुचे ऽष्टाकपाल इति दशहविषं मृगारेष्टिमनुनिर्वपति
20.23.2.a.m: Following their animal cakes, he distributes the Mṛgāreṣṭi consisting of ten oblations, beginning with 'To Agni the deliverer from distress, on eight potsherds'.

20.23.3.a.m: However, the Sviṣṭakṛt and the iḍā are common [to all].

20.23.4.a.s: agnermanve prathamasya pracetasa iti yathāliṅgaṃ yājyānuvākyāḥ
20.23.4.a.d: अग्नेर्मन्वे प्रथमस्य प्रचेतस इति यथालिङ्गं याज्यानुवाक्याः
20.23.4.a.m: The invitatory and consecratory verses correspond to the characteristic marks, beginning with 'agnermanve prathamasya pracetasaḥ'.

20.23.5.a.m: He concludes the sacrifice by departing from the sacrificial site with the Traidhātavīyā offering.

20.23.6.a.m: At it, he gives a thousand [cows as a gift].

20.23.7.a.m: Some authorities prescribe the branched sacrificial post after departing the site.

20.23.8.a.m: Regarding this they say: 'Upon completion, one should distribute twelve brahmaudana portions, or one should sacrifice with twelve iṣṭis'.

20.23.9.b.m: Upon completion, he should only distribute twelve brahmaudana portions.

20.23.9.c.m: At them, he gives twelve hundred [cows] day after day.

20.23.10.a.m: He sacrifices for a year with seasonal animal sacrifices, beginning with 'piśaṅgāstrayo vāsantāḥ'.

20.23.11.d.m: The rainy season victims are dedicated to the Maruts or to Parjanya.

20.23.11.e.m: The autumn victims are dedicated to Indra and Varuṇa.

20.23.11.f.m: The winter victims are dedicated to Indra and Bṛhaspati.

20.23.11.g.m: The cool season victims are dedicated to Indra and Viṣṇu.

20.23.12.a.s: saṃvatsarāya nivakṣasa iti dvayordvayormāsayoḥ paśubandhena yajate
20.23.12.a.d: संवत्सराय निवक्षस इति द्वयोर्द्वयोर्मासयोः पशुबन्धेन यजते
20.23.12.a.m: With the formula 'saṃvatsarāya nivakṣasaḥ', he sacrifices with an animal sacrifice every two months.

20.24.1.a.m: The Puruṣamedha is a five-day rite.

20.24.2.a.m: A Brahmin or a Rājanya may perform this sacrifice.

20.24.4.a.m: At eleven sacrificial posts, there are eleven victims for Agni-Soma.

20.24.5.a.m: The days are arranged as in the Pañcaśāradīya rite;

20.24.6.c.s: viśvāni deva savitariti tisraḥ sāvitrīrhutvā madhyame 'hanpaśūnupākaroti
20.24.6.c.d: विश्वानि देव सवितरिति तिस्रः सावित्रीर्हुत्वा मध्यमे ऽहन्पशूनुपाकरोति
20.24.6.c.m: ‘All [evils], O divine Savitṛ…’ [TS 4.1.11.1]—having offered three libations to Savitṛ with these mantras, he brings up the animal victims on the middle day.

20.24.7.a.m: Having brought forward a double set of eleven victims, [he brings forward] human beings.

20.24.8.a.m: ‘For Brahman he seizes a Brahmin…’—so it is traditionally prescribed [in the text].

20.24.9.a.m: They hold them in the intervals between the sacrificial posts.

20.24.10.a.s: upākṛtāndakṣiṇato 'vasthāya brahmā sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa iti puruṣeṇa nārāyaṇena parā cānuśaṃsati
20.24.10.a.d: उपाकृतान्दक्षिणतो ऽवस्थाय ब्रह्मा सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुष इति पुरुषेण नारायणेन परा चानुशंसति
20.24.10.a.m: Standing to the south of those brought forward, the brahman priest recites across [them] with the Puruṣanārāyaṇa hymn: ‘A thousand-headed is the Puruṣa…’ [TS 3.12.1.1].

20.24.11.a.s: paryagnikṛtānudīco nītvotsṛjyājyena taddevatā āhutīrhutvā dvayairaikādaśinaiḥ saṃsthāpayati
20.24.11.a.d: पर्यग्निकृतानुदीचो नीत्वोत्सृज्याज्येन तद्देवता आहुतीर्हुत्वा द्वयैरैकादशिनैः संस्थापयति
20.24.11.a.m: Having carried them around with fire, led them northwards, and released them, having offered oblation pours of clarified butter to their respective deities, he concludes [the rite] with the two elevenfold sets of animal victims.

20.24.12.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle yadabrāhmaṇānāṃ dikṣu vittaṃ tatsabhūmi dadāti yathāśvamedhe
20.24.12.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले यदब्राह्मणानां दिक्षु वित्तं तत्सभूमि ददाति यथाश्वमेधे
20.24.12.a.m: At the time of sacrificial gifts, whatever wealth in the cardinal directions belongs to non-Brahmins, he gives that together with the land, just as in the Aśvamedha.

20.24.13.a.m: If the sacrificer is a Brahmin, [he gives] his entire property.

20.24.14.a.m: On this very day the royal consecration takes place, just as in the Aśvamedha.

20.24.15.a.m: There are eleven barren cows to be bound after: dedicated to Sūrya, to the All-Gods, or to Prajāpati.

20.24.16.a.m: Having performed the concluding sacrifice with the Traidhātavīyā, mounted the fires separately upon the kindling sticks, and revered the sun with the Uttaranārāyaṇa hymn, he should betake himself to the wilderness.

20.24.17.a.m: Or having entered a village, he should sacrifice with the Traidhātavīyā,

20.25.1.a.s: sautrāmaṇyā maitrāvaruṇyā cāmikṣayā sākaṃprasthāyīyena pañcabilena caruṇā pañcaśāradīyeneti
20.25.1.a.d: सौत्रामण्या मैत्रावरुण्या चामिक्षया साकंप्रस्थायीयेन पञ्चबिलेन चरुणा पञ्चशारदीयेनेति
20.25.1.a.m: with the Sautrāmaṇī, with the curd mess for Mitra-Varuṇa, with the Sākaṃprasthāyīya offering, with the five-cleft mess of boiled rice, and with the Pañcaśāradīya.

20.25.2.a.m: It is stated regarding the five-cleft mess of boiled rice:

20.25.2.b.m: In clarified butter, that for Agni is placed in the eastern cleft;

20.25.2.c.m: in sour curds, that for Indra in the southern [cleft];

20.25.2.d.s: śṛte pratiduhi nītamiśre vā vaiśvadevaḥ paścime /
20.25.2.d.d: शृते प्रतिदुहि नीतमिश्रे वा वैश्वदेवः पश्चिमे ।
20.25.2.d.m: in boiled milk, in fresh milk, or in buttermilk, that for the All-Gods in the western [cleft];

20.25.2.e.m: in water, that for Mitra-Varuṇa in the northern [cleft];

20.25.2.f.m: in unboiled milk, that for Bṛhaspati in the middle [cleft].

20.25.3.a.m: The Sarvamedha is a ten-night rite.

20.25.4.a.s: rājā yajeta yaḥ kāmayeta sarvamidaṃ bhaveyamiti
20.25.4.a.d: राजा यजेत यः कामयेत सर्वमिदं भवेयमिति
20.25.4.a.m: A king who desires, ‘May I become all this,’ should sacrifice [with it].

20.25.6.a.m: The first day is an Agniṣṭud-Agniṣṭoma;

20.25.10.a.m: The fifth day is the middle day of the Aśvamedha;

20.25.10.b.m: on it he immolates the sacrificial horse.

20.25.11.a.m: The sixth day is the middle day of the Puruṣamedha;

20.25.12.b.m: on it he immolates all sacrificial victims.

20.25.14.a.m: Having chopped dry and green plants and trees, they strew them onto the āhavanīya fire.

20.25.15.a.m: At the morning pressing, when the Nārāśaṃsa goblets are set down, he offers food after food.

20.25.16.a.m: ‘For the attainment of everything, for the securing of everything,’ so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

20.25.17.a.m: In the same manner at the midday pressing and at the third pressing.

20.25.19.a.m: The ninth day is characterized by the trayastriṃśa stoma.

20.25.20.a.m: The tenth day is an Atirātra Viśvajit with all the pṛṣṭha stotras.

20.25.21.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle yadabrāhmaṇānāṃ dikṣu vittaṃ tatsabhūmi sapuruṣaṃ dadāti yathāśvamedhe yathāśvamedhe
20.25.21.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले यदब्राह्मणानां दिक्षु वित्तं तत्सभूमि सपुरुषं ददाति यथाश्वमेधे यथाश्वमेधे
20.25.21.a.m: At the time of sacrificial gifts, whatever wealth in the cardinal directions belongs to non-Brahmins, he gives that along with the land and the people, just as in the Aśvamedha, just as in the Aśvamedha.

21.1.1.a.s: dvādaśāhena praiva jāyate 'bhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
21.1.1.a.d: द्वादशाहेन प्रैव जायते ऽभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
21.1.1.a.m: Through the twelve-day rite he is indeed propagated, wins the heavenly world, and becomes established in these worlds.

21.1.4.a.m: In an Ahīna rite, non-consecrated priests sacrifice for the consecrated sacrificer;

21.1.4.b.m: in a sacrificial session, these very same are both the officiating priests and the sacrificer.

21.1.5.a.s: tasmāddvādaśāhena na yājyaṃ pāpmano vyāvṛttyā iti vijñāyate
21.1.5.a.d: तस्माद्द्वादशाहेन न याज्यं पाप्मनो व्यावृत्त्या इति विज्ञायते
21.1.5.a.m: "Therefore one should not officiate at a Dvādaśāha, to avert evil," so it is taught.

21.1.6.a.m: "He prospers who sacrifices with a Dvādaśāha;

21.1.7.a.m: he prospers who receives [gifts]," say some.

21.1.8.a.m: It speaks with reference to the officiating priests and the sacrificer:

21.1.9.c.m: what diminishes of his limbs, that he verily offers," so it is taught.

21.1.10.a.d: यो ऽतपस्वी स्यादसंश्लिष्टो ऽस्य यज्ञः स्यात् ।
21.1.10.a.m: "If he should lack austerity, his sacrifice would be disjointed.

21.1.10.c.m: Thereby he joins the sacrifice together," so it is taught.

21.1.11.a.m: One [person] may sacrifice with a Dvādaśāha,

21.1.11.b.m: or three, six, twelve, or thirteen.

21.1.12.a.m: Among these, during the Upasads they consecrate a thirteenth.

21.1.13.a.m: "Therefore, in a Dvādaśāha, there should not be a thirteenth brahman [priest]," say some.

21.1.14.a.m: Fifteen may be consecrated, having the half-month as their domain;

21.1.14.b.m: seventeen, if desiring offspring or desiring cattle;

21.1.14.c.m: twenty-one, if desiring a firm standing or desiring splendor;

21.1.14.d.m: thirty, having the month as their domain;

21.1.14.e.m: thirty-three, if desiring strength or desiring vigor;

21.1.15.a.m: "An unlimited number may be consecrated," it says finally.

21.1.16.a.s: ye 'nye saptadaśabhyo vādā ahīna eva te sthāninaḥ
21.1.16.a.d: ये ऽन्ये सप्तदशभ्यो वादा अहीन एव ते स्थानिनः
21.1.16.a.m: Statements regarding numbers other than seventeen apply only to the Ahīna.

21.1.17.a.m: Only among the seventeen is there free choice [of numbers].

21.1.18.a.m: All are entitled to the sacrificer's duties.

21.1.19.a.m: All should perform whatever duty of the sacrificer does not conflict with the priest's duty.

21.1.20.a.m: In case of conflict, the priest's duty prevails.

21.2.1.a.m: All should have performed their first sacrifice;

21.2.2.a.m: Actions serving another purpose belong to the gṛhapati alone, such as the anointing of the sacrificial post and the seasonal consecratory verse.

21.2.3.a.m: They should proceed according to the gṛhapati's rule for the sāmidhenī verses, his rule for the cuttings [of the offering], and whatever else may be of this kind.

21.2.4.a.m: "Thou, O Varuṇa" is the concluding verse for Vasiṣṭhas and Rājanyas;

21.2.6.a.m: Nārāśaṃsa is the second fore-offering for Vasiṣṭhas and Śunakas;

21.2.8.a.m: They are consecrated in winter; they conclude in spring.

21.2.9.a.s: śiśire vā etasya prayāṇaṃ vasanta utthānam
21.2.9.a.d: शिशिरे वा एतस्य प्रयाणं वसन्त उत्थानम्
21.2.9.a.m: "In winter is his departure, in spring his conclusion;

21.2.10.a.s: ṛdhnoti ya evaṃvidvāñśiśire dīkṣate vasanta uttiṣṭhata iti vijñāyate
21.2.10.a.d: ऋध्नोति य एवंविद्वाञ्शिशिरे दीक्षते वसन्त उत्तिष्ठत इति विज्ञायते
21.2.10.a.m: he prospers who, knowing thus, is consecrated in winter and concludes in spring," so it is taught.

21.2.11.a.m: When six days have dawned in the waxing half of Caitra, then they may be consecrated.

21.2.12.a.m: Intending to offer the Sāvitra libations, having churned [fire], they should combine [their fires];

21.2.13.a.m: Intending to sacrifice with five animal sacrifices, they should combine [their fires];

21.2.14.a.m: Intending to be consecrated, they should combine [their fires].

21.2.15.a.m: Their fires remain thus combined until the Udavasānīyā sacrifice.

21.2.16.a.m: The adhvaryu, having consecrated the gṛhapati, consecrates the brahman;

21.2.17.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ, having consecrated him [the adhvaryu], consecrates those of the half-share.

21.2.18.a.m: Then the neṣṭṛ, having consecrated him [the pratiprasthātṛ], consecrates those of the third-share.

21.2.19.a.m: Then the unnetṛ, having consecrated him [the neṣṭṛ], consecrates those of the quarter-share.

21.2.20.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ consecrates him [the unnetṛ];

21.3.2.a.m: Once [a priest is] consecrated, he finishes off each [action] up to the combined performance.

21.3.3.a.s: evamanupūrvā evaiṣāṃ yājamānā dharmā ye kecāvibhavinaḥ
21.3.3.a.d: एवमनुपूर्वा एवैषां याजमाना धर्मा ये केचाविभविनः
21.3.3.a.m: In this order indeed are their sacrificer's duties, whichever are not performed collectively.

21.3.4.a.m: "Because of the separation by different gotras, the invocation of ancestral sages should be repeated for those of the same gotra," is one view;

21.3.4.b.m: "Even though separated, there is only a single common performance," is another.

21.3.5.a.m: Some teach the consecration on a single day;

21.3.6.a.m: "One should be consecrated for two days, one should be consecrated for three days"—in this manner it proceeds up to twelve days.

21.3.7.a.m: When one is consecrated additionally, the entire ritual procedure along with the consecration ceremony should be repeated, according to Āśmarathya.

21.3.8.a.m: Having strewed additional fires, he should enter [the ritual] with the personal purificatory rite alone; the libations would constitute the ritual framework, according to Ālekhana.

21.3.9.a.m: They consecrate the wives only in the place of the wives.

21.3.10.a.m: The sequence of their duties is explained by the duties of the sacrificer itself.

21.3.11.a.m: The consecrated ones hold onto the adhvaryu from behind;

21.3.12.a.s: atha samanvārabdheṣu gārhapatye juhotyapaitu mṛtyuramṛtaṃ na āganvaivasvato no abhayaṃ kṛṇotu //
21.3.12.a.d: अथ समन्वारब्धेषु गार्हपत्ये जुहोत्यपैतु मृत्युरमृतं न आगन्वैवस्वतो नो अभयं कृणोतु ॥
21.3.12.a.m: Then, while they hold onto [him] together, he offers into the gārhapatya: "May death depart, may immortality come to us; may Vaivasvata make safety for us;

21.3.12.b.m: like a leaf falling from a tree, may wealth fall down to us;

21.3.12.c.m: may the lord of power be united with us, svāhā."

21.3.13.a.m: [He offers] into the other two [fires] without the wives [holding on]:

21.4.1.a.s: paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yaste sva itaro devayānāt /
21.4.1.a.d: परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पन्थां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् ।
21.4.1.a.m: "O Death, depart along the distant path which is your own, other than the path of the gods;

21.4.1.b.s: cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrāniti dakṣiṇāgnau
21.4.1.b.d: चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरानिति दक्षिणाग्नौ
21.4.1.b.m: to you who see and hear I speak: do not harm our offspring nor our heroes"—into the dakṣiṇāgni;

21.4.2.a.m: "Now indeed we have arrived at this better dwelling, which wins cattle, wins wealth, wins horses;

21.4.2.b.m: like a leaf falling from a tree, may wealth fall down to us;

21.4.2.c.m: may the lord of power be united with us, svāhā"—into the āhavanīya.

21.4.3.a.m: They remain consecrated for twelve days.

21.4.4.a.m: At a sattra they do not send out seekers of gifts.

21.4.5.a.s: prāyaṇīyayā pracarya rājānaṃ krītvopanahya nidadhāti dvādaśāhāyāptam
21.4.5.a.d: प्रायणीयया प्रचर्य राजानं क्रीत्वोपनह्य निदधाति द्वादशाहायाप्तम्
21.4.5.a.m: Having performed the prāyaṇīyā offering, having bought King [Soma], and having bundled him up, he deposits sufficient [soma] for twelve days.

21.4.6.a.m: The cow with which soma is purchased is as in the Ṣoḍaśin.

21.4.7.a.m: During the upasads of the Dvādaśāha he recites the saṃbhāra-formulas.

21.4.8.a.m: Some say he causes the sacrificer to recite them.

21.4.10.a.m: Every four days he offers with one upasad formula at a time.

21.4.11.a.m: Following the upasads, he piles the fire altar.

21.4.14.a.m: The fast-milk rations are from four teats, three teats, two teats, and one teat, for three days each.

21.4.15.a.s: ya eṣāṃ vratamicchedabhipūrayitmā dadhna ekaṃ sruvamunnayeta
21.4.15.a.d: य एषां व्रतमिच्छेदभिपूरयित्मा दध्न एकं स्रुवमुन्नयेत
21.4.15.a.m: If any of them wishes to make up his fast-milk ration, he should ladle out one sruva of curd.

21.4.16.a.m: The sadas has twenty-one roof coverings.

21.5.1.a.m: On the next day, the Jyotiṣṭoma begins.

21.5.2.a.m: The introductory Atirātra is dedicated to Vaiśvānara.

21.5.3.a.m: The ritual is the same up to the taking down of King [Soma].

21.5.4.a.m: As much as he considers sufficient for one day,

21.5.5.a.m: having tied that up in another garment and re-tied the other, he brings it down.

21.5.6.a.m: In this way the ritual framework and the yoking and unyoking of the fire altar [are done] day after day.

21.5.8.a.m: Some teach the yoking and unyoking day after day.

21.5.9.a.m: At the time of sacrificial gifts he gives twelve hundred [cows] day after day in an ahīna.

21.5.10.a.s: sattre tu dākṣiṇau homau hutvedamahaṃ māṃ kalyānyai kīrtyai svargāya lokāya dakṣiṇāṃ nayāmīti yajamānāḥ kṛṣṇājināni dhūnvanta udañco dakṣiṇāpathenātiyanti
21.5.10.a.d: सत्त्रे तु दाक्षिणौ होमौ हुत्वेदमहं मां कल्यान्यै कीर्त्यै स्वर्गाय लोकाय दक्षिणां नयामीति यजमानाः कृष्णाजिनानि धून्वन्त उदञ्चो दक्षिणापथेनातियन्ति
21.5.10.a.m: In a sattra, however, having offered the two dakṣiṇā libations, [saying,] "Here I lead myself as a sacrificial gift for good fame, for the heavenly world," the sacrificers, shaking their black-antelope skins, pass across along the path of gifts towards the north.

21.5.12.a.m: Only on the last day do they dissolve friendships,

21.5.13.a.m: and cast away the black antelope horns.

21.5.14.a.m: On the previous day itself, at the time of the yajñāyajñīya stotra, he draws the vasatīvarī waters for the following day.

21.5.15.a.s: vartamāna evātirātra uttarasmā ahne payāṃsi viśāsti
21.5.15.a.d: वर्तमान एवातिरात्र उत्तरस्मा अह्ने पयांसि विशास्ति
21.5.15.a.m: While the Atirātra is still in progress, he assigns the milk portions for the following day.

21.5.16.a.s: yatra maitrāvaruṇasyābhijānāti śvaḥsutyāmindrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somyebhyaḥ somapebhyaḥ somaṃ prabrūtātsubrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti
21.5.16.a.d: यत्र मैत्रावरुणस्याभिजानाति श्वःसुत्यामिन्द्राग्निभ्यां विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोम्येभ्यः सोमपेभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रूतात्सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति
21.5.16.a.m: When he understands the Maitrāvaruṇa’s [call]: "Announce the tomorrow's soma pressing for Indra and Agni, for all the gods, for the Brahmins who are worthy of soma and drinkers of soma; O Subrahmaṇya, call out the subrahmaṇyā recitation!"—

21.6.1.a.s: tadāgnīdhra āgnīdhrāgāraṃ praviśya saṃpreṣyati śvaḥsutyāmindrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somyebhyaḥ somapebhyaḥ somaṃ prabravīmi subrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti
21.6.1.a.d: तदाग्नीध्र आग्नीध्रागारं प्रविश्य संप्रेष्यति श्वःसुत्यामिन्द्राग्निभ्यां विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोम्येभ्यः सोमपेभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रवीमि सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति
21.6.1.a.m: then the āgnīdhra, having entered the fire chamber of the āgnīdh, issues the ritual call: "I announce tomorrow's soma pressing for Indra and Agni, for all the gods, for the Brahmins who are worthy of soma and drinkers of soma; O Subrahmaṇya, call out the subrahmaṇyā recitation!"

21.6.2.a.m: "He indeed should say, 'tomorrow's soma pressing'," according to Āśmarathya;

21.6.3.a.m: From then onwards he should say only "tomorrow's soma pressing".

21.6.4.a.m: The day concludes with the offerings to the wives of the gods.

21.6.5.a.m: When the day is concluded, the brahman priest releases his speech.

21.6.6.a.m: They carry water around for the wives.

21.6.8.a.m: having returned, they put it onto the āhavanīya fire.

21.6.10.a.m: Right then they commence the nine-versed Agniṣṭoma whose chant is the Rathantara.

21.6.11.a.m: With the sound of a chariot, he commences the Mahendra chant.

21.6.12.a.m: The sound takes the place of the mantra.

21.6.13.a.m: On the next day, they undertake the fifteenfold Ukthya having the Bṛhat-sāman.

21.6.14.a.m: With the sound of a drum, he commences the Mahendra chant.

21.6.15.a.s: yadyu vai stanayitnuḥ syātsa eva syācchabdo mantrasthāne
21.6.15.a.d: यद्यु वै स्तनयित्नुः स्यात्स एव स्याच्छब्दो मन्त्रस्थाने
21.6.15.a.m: If, indeed, there should be thunder, that itself would be the sound in place of the mantra.

21.6.16.a.m: On the next day, they undertake the seventeenfold Ukthya having the Vairūpa-sāman.

21.6.17.a.m: In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with a water-pail.

21.6.18.a.m: The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.

21.6.19.a.m: Then the udgātṛ shakes [the water] with the water-pail.

21.7.1.a.m: On the next day, they undertake the twenty-one-fold Ṣoḍaśin having the Vairāja-sāman.

21.7.2.a.m: This day is [characterized by] the nyuṅkha.

21.7.3.a.m: In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with the two churning sticks.

21.7.4.a.m: The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.

21.7.5.a.m: Then, having covered the right thigh of the udgātṛ with avakā plants, he churns fire on it.

21.7.6.a.m: Over that [fire], when produced, the udgātṛ utters "hiṅ" and hands it to the prastotṛ;

21.7.7.a.s: tamadhvaryuruttareṇa dhiṣṇiyānparyāhṛtyāhavanīye prahṛtya preddho agne dīdihīti virājābhijuhoti
21.7.7.a.d: तमध्वर्युरुत्तरेण धिष्णियान्पर्याहृत्याहवनीये प्रहृत्य प्रेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहीति विराजाभिजुहोति
21.7.7.a.m: The adhvaryu, having brought it around to the north of the dhiṣṇya hearths and cast it into the āhavanīya, makes an offering upon it with the virāj [verse]: "Kindled, O Agni, shine forth..."

21.7.8.a.m: On the next day, they undertake the twenty-seven-fold Ukthya having the Śākvara-sāman.

21.7.9.a.m: In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with water in which avakā plants are placed.

21.7.10.a.m: The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.

21.7.11.a.s: atha tisraḥ saharṣabhā agreṇa sado 'pareṇāgnīdhramudīcīnaṃ dakṣiṇāpathenātiyanti
21.7.11.a.d: अथ तिस्रः सहर्षभा अग्रेण सदो ऽपरेणाग्नीध्रमुदीचीनं दक्षिणापथेनातियन्ति
21.7.11.a.m: Then three [cows], accompanied by a bull, pass across along the dakṣiṇā path northwards, in front of the sadas [and] west of the āgnīdhra.

21.7.12.a.m: On the next day, they undertake the thirty-three-fold Ukthya having the Raivata-sāman.

21.7.13.a.m: This day is [characterized by] the nyūṅkha.

21.7.14.a.m: The adhvaryu himself offers the season sacrifice (ṛtuyāja);

21.7.15.a.s: adhvaryū yajataṃ gṛhapate yajetyabhijñāyādhvaryurhavirdhānaṃ praviśya praiṣottarayarcā yajati /
21.7.15.a.d: अध्वर्यू यजतं गृहपते यजेत्यभिज्ञायाध्वर्युर्हविर्धानं प्रविश्य प्रैषोत्तरयर्चा यजति ।
21.7.15.a.m: Upon recognising [the call], "O two adhvaryus, sacrifice! O householder, sacrifice!", the adhvaryu, having entered the havirdhāna shed, sacrifices with a verse following the ritual call,

21.7.15.b.m: or with the ritual call following the verse:

21.7.16.a.m: "O Aśvins, drink the pressed [soma], shining fires, of pure vows,

21.7.16.c.m: "With the season, drink the soma! Vauṣaṭ!"—if it is unshifted (avyūḍha).

21.7.17.a.s: vyūḍhe tvarvāñcamadya yayyaṃ nṛvāhaṇaṃ rathaṃ yuñjāthāmiha vāṃ vimocanam /
21.7.17.a.d: व्यूढे त्वर्वाञ्चमद्य यय्यं नृवाहणं रथं युञ्जाथामिह वां विमोचनम् ।
21.7.17.a.m: In the shifted (vyūḍha) [order], however: "Yoke your chariot today hitherward, going swiftly, carrying men; here is unyoking for the two of you;

21.7.17.b.s: pṛṅktaṃ havīṃṣi madhunā hi kaṃ gatamathā somaṃ pibataṃ vājinīvasū //
21.7.17.b.d: पृङ्क्तं हवींषि मधुना हि कं गतमथा सोमं पिबतं वाजिनीवसू ॥
21.7.17.b.m: mingle the oblations with honey, for indeed you have come; then drink the soma, rich in steeds!"

21.7.17.c.s: ṛtunā somaṃ pibataṃ vauṣaḍiti tasya pracaritaṃ marutvatīyairbhavati
21.7.17.c.d: ऋतुना सोमं पिबतं वौषडिति तस्य प्रचरितं मरुत्वतीयैर्भवति
21.7.17.c.m: "With the season, drink the soma! Vauṣaṭ!"—the proceeding for this takes place along with the Marutvatīya [draughts].

21.8.2.a.s: atha pratiprasthātottareṇāgnīdhramudīcīṃ tantiṃ vitatya tasyāṃ vatsānbadhnāti
21.8.2.a.d: अथ प्रतिप्रस्थातोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रमुदीचीं तन्तिं वितत्य तस्यां वत्सान्बध्नाति
21.8.2.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ, having stretched a tether northward to the north of the āgnīdhra, ties the calves to it.

21.8.3.a.m: To the south of the mārjālīya, they shut in the mothers [cows].

21.8.4.a.m: In place of the sacrificial grass, he commences the Mahendra chant with water in which dūrvā grass is placed.

21.8.5.a.m: The sāman is commenced, [yet] not [yet] chanted by the prastotṛ.

21.8.6.a.m: Then, having united these calves with the mothers, they make them low to one another.

21.8.7.a.m: They drive them across northwards along the dakṣiṇā path, in front of the sadas [and] west of the āgnīdhra.

21.8.8.a.m: The pṛṣṭhya six-day period is concluded.

21.8.9.a.m: When it is concluded, they consume ghee or honey.

21.8.10.a.m: "Just as one would anoint the shoulder of an ox, such indeed is that," it is known [from scripture].

21.8.11.a.m: Then, day after day, they undertake three Chandoma Ukthya [days]:

21.8.11.b.m: the twenty-four-fold, the forty-four-fold, [and] the forty-eight-fold.

21.8.12.b.m: the second has the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara sāmans;

21.9.1.a.m: Then they undertake the tenth day, the indisputable (avivākya):

21.9.1.b.m: a twenty-four-fold Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.

21.9.2.a.m: Here no one speaks to anyone who is challenged [or struck down].

21.9.3.a.m: Those outside who are lookers-on should speak in dispute;

21.9.4.a.m: if they do not find [an answer] there, it must be spoken from among the members of the sadas;

21.9.5.a.m: if they do not find [an answer] there, it must be spoken by the householder.

21.9.6.a.m: "It must indeed be spoken," he says finally.

21.9.7.a.m: "One should speak in an anuṣṭubh," it is known [from scripture].

21.9.8.a.m: Having recited an anuṣṭubh [verse], he should then say that.

21.9.9.a.m: With respect to that in which he is challenged, he accomplishes it by means of the anuṣṭubh.

21.9.10.a.m: On this day, they bring two kinds of firewood:

21.9.12.a.m: To the north of the āhavanīya, they set down those of udumbara wood.

21.9.13.a.m: Then, while [the others] touch him from behind, he offers two oblations into the gārhapatya:

21.9.13.b.s: amūryā upa sūrye yābhirvā sūryaḥ saha /
21.9.13.b.d: अमूर्या उप सूर्ये याभिर्वा सूर्यः सह ।
21.9.13.b.m: "Those [waters] which are up by the sun, or with which the sun is united,

21.9.13.d.s: iha ratiriha rantiriha ramatiriha ramadhvamiha vo ramatiḥ svāheti
21.9.13.d.d: इह रतिरिह रन्तिरिह रमतिरिह रमध्वमिह वो रमतिः स्वाहेति
21.9.13.d.m: with: "Here is delight, here is resting, here is rejoicing; rejoice here, here is your resting; svāhā!"

21.9.14.a.m: and with "Releasing the support..." Then, having gone to the āhavanīya,

21.9.15.a.d: अतिच्छन्दसोपतिष्ठन्ते ऽयं सहस्रमानवो दृशः कवीनां मतिर्ज्योतिर्विधर्मा ।
21.9.15.a.m: they worship [it] with an aticchandas verse: "This one, having thousandfold human forms, the vision of the poets, the thought, the light, the supporter of the cosmos;

21.9.15.b.m: the ruddy one sent forth the dawns together;

21.9.15.c.s: arepasaḥ samokasaḥ sacetasaḥ saretasaḥ svasare manyumantaścidākoriti
21.9.15.c.d: अरेपसः समोकसः सचेतसः सरेतसः स्वसरे मन्युमन्तश्चिदाकोरिति
21.9.15.c.m: spotless, dwelling together, having one mind, having the same seed, in the early morning, even those who are full of anger [brought gifts]..."

21.10.1.a.m: From there, they glide together for the mental draught (manograha) dedicated to Prajāpati.

21.10.2.a.s: prasṛpteṣūpāṃśupātreṇa gṛhṇātyanayā tvā pṛthivyā pātreṇa samudraṃ rasayā prajāpataye juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti
21.10.2.a.d: प्रसृप्तेषूपांशुपात्रेण गृह्णात्यनया त्वा पृथिव्या पात्रेण समुद्रं रसया प्रजापतये जुष्टं गृह्णामीति
21.10.2.a.m: When they have glided forward, he draws [the draught] with the upāṃśu vessel: "With this earth as a vessel, the ocean with juice, I draw you agreeable to Prajāpati."

21.10.3.a.m: "He should draw it from empty space," says one [view].

21.10.3.b.s: tārtīyasavanikasya somasya pariśāyayedyāvantamekasmai camasagaṇāya sagrahāyāptaṃ manyetetyaparam
21.10.3.b.d: तार्तीयसवनिकस्य सोमस्य परिशाययेद्यावन्तमेकस्मै चमसगणाय सग्रहायाप्तं मन्येतेत्यपरम्
21.10.3.b.m: "He should leave over from the soma of the third pressing as much as he considers sufficient for a set of goblets together with a draught," says another [view].

21.10.4.a.m: The beginning of the chant (stotropākaraṇa), the prastāva, the udgītha, and the pratihāra are [performed] mentally.

21.10.5.a.s: manasā tisṛṇāṃ sarparājñīnāṃ ṣaṭkṛtvaḥ pratigṛṇāti yadyardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati /
21.10.5.a.d: मनसा तिसृणां सर्पराज्ञीनां षट्कृत्वः प्रतिगृणाति यद्यर्धर्चशः शंसति ।
21.10.5.a.m: He responds mentally six times to the three Sarparājñī verses, if [the hotṛ] recites by half-verses;

21.10.6.a.m: The hotṛ recites the Caturhotṛ formulas.

21.10.7.a.m: "Om" is the response to the Daśahotṛ;

21.10.7.e.m: "We have prospered, O hotṛ!" [is the response] to the Saptahotṛ.

21.10.8.a.m: The call (āśruta), the counter-call (pratyāśruta), the consecratory verse, the vaṣaṭ-call, and the second vaṣaṭ-call are [performed] mentally.

21.10.9.a.m: Having offered mentally, he brings the portion for partaking.

21.10.10.a.m: The fact that they look at one another constitutes the mutual invitation.

21.10.12.a.m: It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: "They discuss the theological discourse (brahmavādya)."

21.10.13.a.m: "Having sat down, there should be a conversation," says one [view].

21.10.13.b.m: "The chief officiating priests, having sat around the master of the house (gṛhapati) himself, should question him," says another [view].

21.11.1.a.s: yaddaśahotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankena prajā asṛjanteti
21.11.1.a.d: यद्दशहोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केन प्रजा असृजन्तेति
21.11.1.a.m: "When the Daśahotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, and with what did they create creatures?"

21.11.2.a.s: prajāpatinā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvaṃstena prajā asṛjanteti prativacanaḥ
21.11.2.a.d: प्रजापतिना वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवंस्तेन प्रजा असृजन्तेति प्रतिवचनः
21.11.2.a.m: "Through Prajāpati as the master of the house they prospered; with him they created creatures," is the answer.

21.11.3.a.s: brahmā pṛcchati yaccaturhotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankenauṣadhīrasṛjanteti
21.11.3.a.d: ब्रह्मा पृच्छति यच्चतुर्होतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केनौषधीरसृजन्तेति
21.11.3.a.m: The brahman asks: "When the Caturhotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, and with what did they create plants?"

21.11.4.a.m: "Through Soma as the master of the house they prospered; with him they created plants," is the answer.

21.11.5.a.s: hotā pṛcchati yatpañcahotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankenaibhyo lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudanta kenaiṣāṃpaśūnavṛñjateti
21.11.5.a.d: होता पृच्छति यत्पञ्चहोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान्प्राणुदन्त केनैषांपशूनवृञ्जतेति
21.11.5.a.m: The hotṛ asks: "When the Pañcahotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, with what did they drive away the Asuras from these worlds, and with what did they take away their cattle?"

21.11.6.a.s: agninā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvaṃstenaibhyo lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudanta tenaiṣāṃ paśūnavṛñjateti prativacanaḥ
21.11.6.a.d: अग्निना वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवंस्तेनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान्प्राणुदन्त तेनैषां पशूनवृञ्जतेति प्रतिवचनः
21.11.6.a.m: "Through Agni as the master of the house they prospered; with him they drove away the Asuras from these worlds, and with him they took away their cattle," is the answer.

21.11.7.a.s: hotrakāḥ pṛcchanti yatṣaḍḍhotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankenartūnakalpayanteti
21.11.7.a.d: होत्रकाः पृच्छन्ति यत्षड्ढोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केनर्तूनकल्पयन्तेति
21.11.7.a.m: The hotrakas ask: "When the Ṣaḍḍhotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, and with what did they fashion the seasons?"

21.11.8.a.m: "Through Dhātṛ as the master of the house they prospered; with him they fashioned the seasons," is the answer.

21.11.9.a.s: udgātā pṛcchati yatsapatahotāraḥ sattramāsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvankena suvarāyankenemāṃllokānsamatanvanniti
21.11.9.a.d: उद्गाता पृच्छति यत्सपतहोतारः सत्त्रमासत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन्केन सुवरायन्केनेमांल्लोकान्समतन्वन्निति
21.11.9.a.m: The udgātṛ asks: "When the Saptahotṛs held a sacrificial session, through which master of the house did they prosper, with what did they go to heaven, and with what did they extend these worlds?"

21.11.10.a.s: aryamṇā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvaṃstena suvarāyaṃstenemāṃllokānsamatanvanniti prativacanaḥ
21.11.10.a.d: अर्यम्णा वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवंस्तेन सुवरायंस्तेनेमांल्लोकान्समतन्वन्निति प्रतिवचनः
21.11.10.a.m: "Through Aryaman as the master of the house they prospered; with him they went to heaven, and with him they extended these worlds," is the answer.

21.11.11.a.s: api vā yadevaitatūṣṇīkaṃ mānasaṃ tasyaiṣa vādaḥ
21.11.11.a.d: अपि वा यदेवैततूष्णीकं मानसं तस्यैष वादः
21.11.11.a.m: Or else, this is the discussion for whatever is performed silently and mentally.

21.11.12.a.m: Or rather, when the hotṛ recites the Caturhotṛ formulas,

21.11.13.a.m: it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: "They reproach Prajāpati."

21.12.1.a.s: akuśalo vā ayaṃ prajāpatiryo daṃśamaśakānsasṛje ya stenāniti prajāpatiparivādaḥ
21.12.1.a.d: अकुशलो वा अयं प्रजापतिर्यो दंशमशकान्ससृजे य स्तेनानिति प्रजापतिपरिवादः
21.12.1.a.m: "Indeed, unskilled is this Prajāpati who created biting flies and mosquitoes, who [created] thieves"—such is the reproach of Prajāpati.

21.12.2.a.m: Or rather, they recite the mantras reproaching Prajāpati.

21.12.3.b.m: "That Prajāpati created forests and cities, mountains

21.12.3.c.s: kartāni ca na tadbhadraṃ yadbhadraṃ tanma āsuva //
21.12.3.c.d: कर्तानि च न तद्भद्रं यद्भद्रं तन्म आसुव ॥
21.12.3.c.m: and chasms, that is not good. What is good, impel that to me!

21.12.3.d.m: That the dawn, joined with darkness, burned most fiercely by day;

21.12.3.e.m: both the flood of water and the excessive heat—so it was when heated by Prajāpati.

21.12.3.f.m: That there are thieves, that there are wolves, biting flies, and mosquitoes, that there are malicious ones—

21.12.3.g.s: tadu te vṛjinaṃ tvetadvratametanna me matam //
21.12.3.g.d: तदु ते वृजिनं त्वेतद्व्रतमेतन्न मे मतम् ॥
21.12.3.g.m: that is crookedness of yours; this vow is not my opinion.

21.12.3.h.m: Worship Prajāpati on the tenth day, the thought of poets, the bull of peoples;

21.12.3.i.s: sa suṣṭutiṃ sudraviṇaṃ dadhānaḥ pūto vipāpmā vijahāti loka iti
21.12.3.i.d: स सुष्टुतिं सुद्रविणं दधानः पूतो विपाप्मा विजहाति लोक इति
21.12.3.i.m: bearing good praise and good wealth, purified and free from evil, he leaves the world behind."

21.12.4.a.d: अथ व्रं वृणीते ऽदो नो ऽस्त्विति यत्कामयते ।
21.12.4.a.m: Then he chooses a wish: "May this be ours," whichever he desires.

21.12.4.b.m: And indeed, a brahmin has many desires.

21.12.5.a.s: bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ suprajāḥ prajayā bhūyāsaṃ suvīro vīraiḥ suvarcā varcasā supoṣaḥ poṣairityetadvidadaḥti
21.12.5.a.d: भूर्भुवः सुवः सुप्रजाः प्रजया भूयासं सुवीरो वीरैः सुवर्चा वर्चसा सुपोषः पोषैरित्येतद्विददःति
21.12.5.a.m: They perform this: "Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in luster through luster, rich in nourishment through nourishments!"

21.12.6.a.s: caturhotṝnvyākhyāya dvārau saṃvṛtya yathādhiṣṇiyaṃ patnīrvyāsādyāthābhyo vācamupākaroti
21.12.6.a.d: चतुर्होतॄन्व्याख्याय द्वारौ संवृत्य यथाधिष्णियं पत्नीर्व्यासाद्याथाभ्यो वाचमुपाकरोति
21.12.6.a.m: Having recited the caturhotṛ formulas, having closed the two doors, and having seated the wives according to their dhiṣṇya hearths, he then commences speech for them.

21.12.7.a.s: iha dhṛtiriha svadhṛtiriha rantiriha ramatirityaudumbarīṃ pariṣvajyodarairupaspṛśanto vāgyatāstiṣṭhanti
21.12.7.a.d: इह धृतिरिह स्वधृतिरिह रन्तिरिह रमतिरित्यौदुम्बरीं परिष्वज्योदरैरुपस्पृशन्तो वाग्यतास्तिष्ठन्ति
21.12.7.a.m: With [the words], "Here is firmness, here is self-firmness, here is delight, here is revelry," having embraced the audumbarī post, touching it with their bellies, they stand restraining their speech.

21.12.8.a.m: When the sun has reached above the tree-tops, they creep forward, keeping hold of one another.

21.12.9.a.s: yuvaṃ tamindrāparvatā puroyudhā yo naḥ pṛtanyādapa taṃtamiddhataṃ vajreṇa taṃtamiddhatam /
21.12.9.a.d: युवं तमिन्द्रापर्वता पुरोयुधा यो नः पृतन्यादप तंतमिद्धतं वज्रेण तंतमिद्धतम् ।
21.12.9.a.m: "You two, Indra and Parvata, fighting in the forefront, strike down whoever assails us; strike him down with the thunderbolt!

21.12.9.b.m: Let the deep [abode] please him driven far away, when he reaches it!

21.12.9.c.s: asmākaṃ śatrūnpari śūra viśvato darmā darṣīṣṭa viśvata ityuttareṇa havirdhānaṃ dakṣiṇairhastaiḥ kaṭāṃstejanīrvā niṣevamāṇāḥ prāñco gatvā pañca vacāṃsi vyāharanti vāgvāgaitu vāgupaitu vāk samaitūpa maitu vāgbhūrbhuvaḥ suvariti
21.12.9.c.d: अस्माकं शत्रून्परि शूर विश्वतो दर्मा दर्षीष्ट विश्वत इत्युत्तरेण हविर्धानं दक्षिणैर्हस्तैः कटांस्तेजनीर्वा निषेवमाणाः प्राञ्चो गत्वा पञ्च वचांसि व्याहरन्ति वाग्वागैतु वागुपैतु वाक् समैतूप मैतु वाग्भूर्भुवः सुवरिति
21.12.9.c.m: O hero, from every side, breaker [of forts], smash our enemies completely!"—touching mats or stalks with their right hands, having gone eastward to the north of the havirdhāna shed, they utter the five utterances: "May speech come! May speech approach! May speech assemble! May speech come unto me! Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svar!"

21.12.10.a.s: ahnā rātriṃ dhyātvādhivṛkṣasūrye subrahmaṇyayā vācaṃ visṛjyaudumbarīḥ samidha ādadhāti
21.12.10.a.d: अह्ना रात्रिं ध्यात्वाधिवृक्षसूर्ये सुब्रह्मण्यया वाचं विसृज्यौदुम्बरीः समिध आदधाति
21.12.10.a.m: Having meditated on the night by day, when the sun has reached above the tree-tops, having released speech with the Subrahmaṇyā formula, he puts kindling sticks of udumbara wood on [the fire].

21.13.1.a.m: They undertake the concluding day like the opening day.

21.13.3.a.m: What is done on a preceding day for the following day, those are the ahīna-continuations.

21.13.4.a.m: If it is a sacrificial session, they shave [their heads], including the tufts, at the time of shaving.

21.13.5.a.s: udavasānīyayeṣṭvānyānṛtvijo vṛtvā pṛṣṭhaśamanīyena yajanate jyotiṣṭomenāgniṣṭomena sahasradakṣiṇena
21.13.5.a.d: उदवसानीययेष्ट्वान्यानृत्विजो वृत्वा पृष्ठशमनीयेन यजनते ज्योतिष्टोमेनाग्निष्टोमेन सहस्रदक्षिणेन
21.13.5.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Udavasānīyā offering, having chosen other officiating priests, they sacrifice with the Pṛṣṭhaśamanīya, an Agniṣṭoma-Jyotiṣṭoma with a thousand [cows] as sacrificial gifts.

21.13.7.a.m: On the opening and concluding [days], and on the tenth day, he draws the Pṛśni and Prāṇa draughts

21.13.7.b.m: intertwining [them] with the measures of soma.

21.13.8.a.s: prākṛtaṃ yajurmānamanudrutya vāyurasi prāṇo nāmeti daśabhiḥ pṛśnigrahāṇāṃ mantrairdaśa mānāni mimīte
21.13.8.a.d: प्राकृतं यजुर्मानमनुद्रुत्य वायुरसि प्राणो नामेति दशभिः पृश्निग्रहाणां मन्त्रैर्दश मानानि मिमीते
21.13.8.a.m: Having recited the standard measuring yajus, he measures ten measures with the ten mantras of the Pṛśni draughts: "You are Vāyu; breath by name..."

21.13.9.a.s: uttaraṃ yajurmānamanudrutyāyaṃ puro bhuva iti daśabhiḥ prāṇagrahāṇāṃ mantrairdaśa mānāni mimīte
21.13.9.a.d: उत्तरं यजुर्मानमनुद्रुत्यायं पुरो भुव इति दशभिः प्राणग्रहाणां मन्त्रैर्दश मानानि मिमीते
21.13.9.a.m: Having recited the following measuring yajus, he measures ten measures with the ten mantras of the Prāṇa draughts: "This one in front, Bhuva..."

21.13.10.a.m: In this way, he intertwines the subsequent measures.

21.13.11.a.m: There are nine stalks each [for each measure, and] ten mantras.

21.13.12.a.m: Or rather, he measures with nine [mantras] of nine [stalks] each.

21.13.13.a.m: The remaining [mantras] are for the purpose of option.

21.13.14.a.s: api vā mānamanudrutya pṛśnī atha prāṇena nivapet
21.13.14.a.d: अपि वा मानमनुद्रुत्य पृश्नी अथ प्राणेन निवपेत्
21.13.14.a.m: Or rather, having recited the measuring [formula], one should scatter [stalks] with the two Pṛśni [mantras], then with the Prāṇa [mantra].

21.13.15.a.m: Then one should scatter [the stalks of] the Prāṇa [draught], the measure, with the two Pṛśni [mantras].

21.13.16.a.m: Then one should scatter [the stalks of] the two Pṛśni [draughts], the Prāṇa [draught], with the measuring [mantra].

21.13.17.a.m: In this manner the two subsequent rounds are arranged.

21.13.18.a.m: That which is the first is the fourth;

21.13.18.b.m: that which is the second is the fifth.

21.13.20.a.s: uttareṣu triṣu pṛṣṭhyāhaḥsu trīnatigrāhyāngṛhṇāti āgneyamekaviṃśa aindraṃ triṇave sauryaṃ trayastriṃśe
21.13.20.a.d: उत्तरेषु त्रिषु पृष्ठ्याहःसु त्रीनतिग्राह्यान्गृह्णाति आग्नेयमेकविंश ऐन्द्रं त्रिणवे सौर्यं त्रयस्त्रिंशे
21.13.20.a.m: On the later three days of the six-day pṛṣṭhya period, he draws three atigrāhya draughts: the one for Agni on the twenty-one-fold [day], the one for Indra on the twenty-seven-fold [day], the one for Sūrya on the thirty-three-fold [day].

21.13.21.a.m: The Vājasaneyins prescribe [them] in the former triad of days.

21.13.22.a.m: Where the Gaurīvīta sāman is [used], there he draws many atigrāhya draughts.

21.14.1.a.m: We shall explain the three-fronted arrangement [of draughts].

21.14.2.a.m: The opening and concluding days and the tenth day have the Aindravāyava draught first.

21.14.3.a.m: Then, of the other nine [days], the first day has the Aindravāyava draught first;

21.14.4.a.m: The three-fronted arrangement thus established rotates three times, if it is not shifted.

21.14.5.a.m: If it is shifted, however, the opening and concluding days have the Aindravāyava draught first;

21.14.5.b.m: then, of the other ten [days], the first day has the Aindravāyava draught first;

21.14.5.h.m: then two [days] have the Aindravāyava draught first.

21.14.7.a.m: They immolate a beast for Agni on the opening day;

21.14.7.b.m: on the next day, an ewe for Sarasvatī.

21.14.8.a.m: Thus arranged, they immolate the eleven animals day by day.

21.14.10.a.m: One who desires spiritual brilliance [offers] one for Sūrya.

21.14.11.a.m: If there should be eleven sacrificial posts, he should erect the posts one by one each day;

21.14.12.a.m: Day after day, the spare post is turned towards [the next post in order].

21.14.13.a.m: At the post standing opposite the fire, he dedicates the animal on the concluding day.

21.14.14.a.m: There are twelve Agniṣṭomas having the Rathaṃtara as chant.

21.15.1.a.s: gavāmayanena prajāṃ bhūtiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchantyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayantyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
21.15.1.a.d: गवामयनेन प्रजां भूतिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयन्त्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
21.15.1.a.m: By means of the Gavāmayana, they attain offspring, prosperity, and abundance; they win the heavenly world; they establish themselves firmly in these worlds.

21.15.2.a.m: Its procedure has been explained by means of the twelve-day rite constituting a sacrificial session.

21.15.4.a.m: It has been stated: "Those who are about to consecrate themselves for a year-long session should consecrate themselves on the Ekāṣṭakā."

21.15.5.a.m: They should consecrate themselves four days before the full-moon day.

21.15.6.a.m: "Before the Māghī full moon," says Āśmarathya.

21.15.8.a.m: Having undertaken the introductory Atirātra, they undertake the introductory twenty-four-stoma Ukthya day.

21.15.10.a.m: Then they undertake the Abhiplava six-day period:

21.15.11.a.m: They undertake four Abhiplava periods arranged in this manner,

21.15.11.b.m: and the Pṛṣṭhya six-day period at the end of the month.

21.15.12.a.m: They undertake five months arranged in this manner.

21.15.14.d.m: three Paraḥsāman days as Ukthyas, or as Agniṣṭomas,

21.15.16.a.m: Then they undertake the Viṣuvant day, a twenty-one-stoma Agniṣṭoma with the Divākīrtya-sāman.

21.15.17.a.m: When the sun has risen on it, he begins the morning recitation.

21.15.19.a.s: uttare pakṣa āvṛttā gaṇā anyatra dvādaśāhīyāddaśarātrāt
21.15.19.a.d: उत्तरे पक्ष आवृत्ता गणा अन्यत्र द्वादशाहीयाद्दशरात्रात्
21.15.19.a.m: In the latter half [of the year], the groups of days are reversed, except for the ten-day period of the twelve-day sacrifice.

21.15.20.a.m: Then they undertake three Arvāksāman days as Ukthyas,

21.15.23.a.m: Having undertaken the reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day period, [and] four reversed Abhiplava periods at the end of the month,

21.15.24.a.m: they undertake five months arranged in this manner.

21.16.2.c.m: the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice,

21.16.2.e.m: and the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra.

21.16.6.a.s: uttarasya pakṣasa upariṣṭādviśvajita āvṛttaṃ pṛṣṭhyaṃ ṣaḍahamupetya trīnabhiplavānāvṛttān
21.16.6.a.d: उत्तरस्य पक्षस उपरिष्टाद्विश्वजित आवृत्तं पृष्ठ्यं षडहमुपेत्य त्रीनभिप्लवानावृत्तान्
21.16.6.a.m: In the latter half [of the year], after the Viśvajit, having undertaken the reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day period and three reversed Abhiplava periods,

21.16.7.a.m: these, together with the earlier ones, are twenty-eight inserted days.

21.16.8.a.m: Having undertaken the reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day period, [and] four reversed Abhiplava periods at the end of the month,

21.16.9.a.m: they undertake four months arranged in this manner.

21.16.11.a.m: three Abhiplava periods, the Āyus and Go days, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice,

21.16.12.a.m: the latter twenty-eight inserted days, and the Mahāvrata and the Atirātra.

21.16.16.a.m: In the first half [of the year], before the final Pṛṣṭhya period, [they undertake] the Abhijit-Agniṣṭoma;

21.16.17.a.m: in the latter half, after the first Pṛṣṭhya period, [they undertake] the Viśvajit-Agniṣṭoma.

21.16.18.a.m: The rest is the same as the Śāṭyāyanaka.

21.16.19.a.s: api vā saṃvatsaraṃ saṃpādyottame māsi dvādaśāhīye daśarātre sakṛtpṛṣṭhānyupeyuḥ
21.16.19.a.d: अपि वा संवत्सरं संपाद्योत्तमे मासि द्वादशाहीये दशरात्रे सकृत्पृष्ठान्युपेयुः
21.16.19.a.m: Or rather, having completed the year, they should undertake the pṛṣṭha stotras only once, during the ten-day period of the twelve-day sacrifice in the last month.

21.16.20.a.m: In that case, Abhiplava periods should be substituted in place of the Pṛṣṭhya periods.

21.16.21.a.m: After the ten-day period of the Dvādaśāha is the Mahāvrata.

21.17.1.a.m: Then they undertake the Mahāvrata, a twenty-five-fold Agniṣṭoma.

21.17.3.a.m: With nine verses addressed to Indra and lacking a pratihāra, the adhvaryu sings as udgātṛ.

21.17.4.a.m: The wives sing along to the Bhadra Sāman.

21.17.5.a.m: Its performance has already proceeded through the Marutvatīya [draughts].

21.17.7.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ arranges the special artistic performances of the Mahāvrata.

21.17.8.a.m: There are ten holes bored through the neck of an udumbara harp.

21.17.9.a.m: Through each bored hole he strings ten strings of muñja grass.

21.17.11.b.m: Saying, 'Earth, thirty-three strings,' the adhvaryu stretches thirty-three strings;

21.17.11.c.m: Saying, 'Atmosphere, thirty-three strings,' the hotṛ thirty-three strings;

21.17.11.d.m: Saying, 'Heaven, thirty-three strings,' the udgātṛ thirty-three strings;

21.17.12.a.m: He sets down an udumbara chair at the place of the udgātṛs, woven with muñja grass, directly above the seat of the hotṛ.

21.17.13.a.s: audumbaraṃ pleṅkhaṃ hotre prabadhnāti mauñjyā rajjvā
21.17.13.a.d: औदुम्बरं प्लेङ्खं होत्रे प्रबध्नाति मौञ्ज्या रज्ज्वा
21.17.13.a.m: He fastens an udumbara swing for the hotṛ with a cord of muñja grass.

21.17.14.a.m: He places two udumbara wooden boards for the adhvaryu,

21.17.15.a.m: Upon grass cushions the assistant hotṛs, the accompanying singers, and the wives sit.

21.17.16.a.m: The wives prepare themselves with apāghāṭalikā lutes, tambalavīṇās, and piccholās.

21.17.17.a.m: The lute-players prepare themselves with conch shells, reed flutes, and tūṇava pipes.

21.17.18.a.s: nikalpete brahmacārī puṃścalī cāgreṇa sadaso dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhumārtiṣyamāṇau
21.17.18.a.d: निकल्पेते ब्रह्मचारी पुंश्चली चाग्रेण सदसो दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुमार्तिष्यमाणौ
21.17.18.a.m: A student and a courtesan prepare themselves in front of the sadas, intending to touch against the southern doorpost.

21.17.19.a.s: uttarasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ puṃścalyai māgadhāya ca pariśrayanti
21.17.19.a.d: उत्तरस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां पुंश्चल्यै मागधाय च परिश्रयन्ति
21.17.19.a.m: On the northern buttock of the altar ground they screen off [an enclosure] for the courtesan and a Māgadha.

21.18.1.a.m: They tie drums in the cardinal directions,

21.18.2.a.m: West of the āgnīdhra fire chamber they dig a pit for the earth-drum,

21.18.2.b.m: Half inside the altar ground, half outside the altar ground.

21.18.3.a.m: Having covered it with a wet hide whose hair is turned upwards and secured it around with pegs, he places this tail-stalk here to serve as a drumstick.

21.18.4.a.m: In front of the āgnīdhra fire chamber a Śūdra and an Āryan prepare themselves, about to wrestle over a piece of hide.

21.18.5.a.s: uttareṇāgnīdhraṃ kaṭasaṃghāte tejanasaṃghāte vārdraṃ carma vyadhanārthaṃ vitatyocchrayanti
21.18.5.a.d: उत्तरेणाग्नीध्रं कटसंघाते तेजनसंघाते वार्द्रं चर्म व्यधनार्थं वितत्योच्छ्रयन्ति
21.18.5.a.m: North of the āgnīdhra fire chamber they stretch out and raise a wet hide upon a clump of reed mats or cane stalks for target-piercing.

21.18.6.a.m: In front of the āhavanīya fire, armored men don their armor in chariots.

21.18.7.a.m: At the edge of the mārjālīya, eight maidservants prepare themselves with water pots.

21.18.8.a.s: vāgbhadraṃ mano bhadraṃ māno bhadraṃ tanno bhadramiti triḥ parvayet
21.18.8.a.d: वाग्भद्रं मनो भद्रं मानो भद्रं तन्नो भद्रमिति त्रिः पर्वयेत्
21.18.8.a.m: He should repeat three times: 'Speech is auspicious, mind is auspicious, measure is auspicious, that is auspicious for us.'

21.18.9.a.s: kaṭaśalākayekṣukāṇḍena veṇukāṇḍena vetasakāṇḍena vā vāṇaṃ saṃhrādya tena māhendrasya stotramupākaroti
21.18.9.a.d: कटशलाकयेक्षुकाण्डेन वेणुकाण्डेन वेतसकाण्डेन वा वाणं संह्राद्य तेन माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रमुपाकरोति
21.18.9.a.m: Having caused the harp to sound by means of a mat splint, a piece of sugarcane, a piece of bamboo, or a reed-stalk, he introduces the chant of the draught for Mahendra with it.

21.18.10.a.m: 'The udgātṛ plays [it],' so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.18.11.a.m: The udgātṛ gives it to the prastotṛ;

21.18.11.c.m: The adhvaryu gives it to another.

21.18.12.a.s: taṃ so 'greṇa sadaso dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhuṃ prativādayannāste
21.18.12.a.d: तं सो ऽग्रेण सदसो दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुं प्रतिवादयन्नास्ते
21.18.12.a.m: He sits in front of the sadas, playing it against the southern doorpost.

21.19.1.a.s: upākṛte māhendrasya stotre sarvā vāco vadanti
21.19.1.a.d: उपाकृते माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रे सर्वा वाचो वदन्ति
21.19.1.a.m: When the chant of the draught for Mahendra is introduced, all voices sound.

21.19.3.a.m: The wives play apāghāṭalikā lutes, tambalavīṇās, and piccholās.

21.19.4.a.m: The lute-players sound together conch shells, reed flutes, and tūṇava pipes.

21.19.5.a.s: ṛtīyete brahmacārī puṃścalī ca dakṣiṇaṃ dvārbāhumāśliṣyamāṇau
21.19.5.a.d: ऋतीयेते ब्रह्मचारी पुंश्चली च दक्षिणं द्वार्बाहुमाश्लिष्यमाणौ
21.19.5.a.m: The student and the courtesan revile each other, clinging to the southern doorpost.

21.19.6.a.m: The courtesan and the Māgadha unite.

21.19.8.b.m: [And beat] the earth-drum with the tail-stalk.

21.19.9.a.s: śūdrāryau carmakarte vyāyacchete ārdre śvete parimaṇḍale /
21.19.9.a.d: शूद्रार्यौ चर्मकर्ते व्यायच्छेते आर्द्रे श्वेते परिमण्डले ।
21.19.9.a.m: The Śūdra and the Āryan wrestle over the piece of hide, which is wet, white, and circular,

21.19.9.b.m: The Brahmin inside the altar ground, the Śūdra outside the altar ground.

21.19.11.a.m: 'These have succeeded; these have done well,' says the Brahmin;

21.19.11.b.m: 'These are evictors; these have done ill,' says the Śūdra.

21.19.12.a.m: Having won it, the Brahmin tosses the hide onto the āgnīdhra hearth.

21.19.13.a.m: The armored men drive around this hide.

21.19.14.a.m: He directs each of them: 'Do not miss! Do not shoot past!'

21.19.15.a.m: Piercing [it] when stretched, they do not shoot beyond it.

21.19.16.a.m: According to some, princely sons pierce [it].

21.19.17.a.m: Having gone an unmeasured distance towards the north and having returned, they unyoke [the chariots].

21.19.18.a.s: atraitā dāsakumārya udakumbhānadhinidhāya triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ mārjālīyaṃ parinṛtyanti dakṣiṇānpado nighnantīridaṃmadhuṃ gāyantyaḥ
21.19.18.a.d: अत्रैता दासकुमार्य उदकुम्भानधिनिधाय त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं मार्जालीयं परिनृत्यन्ति दक्षिणान्पदो निघ्नन्तीरिदंमधुं गायन्त्यः
21.19.18.a.m: Now these slave girls, having placed water-jars on [their heads], dance thrice clock-wise around the mārjālīya, beating their right feet, singing the Idaṃmadhu [song]:

21.19.19.a.s: idameva sāraghaṃ madhvayaṃ somaḥ suto iha /
21.19.19.a.d: इदमेव सारघं मध्वयं सोमः सुतो इह ।
21.19.19.a.m: "This indeed is honey made by bees; this soma is pressed here.

21.19.19.b.s: tasyeha piva tātṛpurhaimahā idaṃ madhvidaṃ madhvityeva gāyeyurityāśmarathyaḥ
21.19.19.b.d: तस्येह पिव तातृपुर्हैमहा इदं मध्विदं मध्वित्येव गायेयुरित्याश्मरथ्यः
21.19.19.b.m: Drink of it here, become satisfied! Haimahā!" They should sing just: "This is honey! This is honey!"—thus says Āśmarathya.

21.20.2.a.s: vāgveda himbinīṃ saināṃ gāyatu prāṇasya vādite /
21.20.2.a.d: वाग्वेद हिम्बिनीं सैनां गायतु प्राणस्य वादिते ।
21.20.2.a.m: "Speech knows the Himbinī; let her sing it when the breath is sounded.

21.20.2.b.m: May she, being sung, help the sacrificers here!

21.20.2.c.s: vāgveda hastāvārāṃ saināṃ gāyatu prāṇasya vādite /
21.20.2.c.d: वाग्वेद हस्तावारां सैनां गायतु प्राणस्य वादिते ।
21.20.2.c.m: "Speech knows the Hastāvārā; let her sing it when the breath is sounded.

21.20.2.d.m: May she, being sung, help the sacrificers here!"—so [runs the verse].

21.20.3.b.m: "Cows alone are fragrant; cows are scented like bdellium.

21.20.3.c.s: gāvo dhṛtasya mātarastā iha santu bhūyasīḥ //
21.20.3.c.d: गावो धृतस्य मातरस्ता इह सन्तु भूयसीः ॥
21.20.3.c.m: Cows are the mothers of ghee; may they be abundant here!

21.20.3.d.s: nanu gāvo maṅkīrasya gaṅgāyā udakaṃ papuḥ /
21.20.3.d.d: ननु गावो मङ्कीरस्य गङ्गाया उदकं पपुः ।
21.20.3.d.m: Did not the cows drink the water of the Gaṅgā of Maṅkīra?

21.20.3.e.m: They drank of the Sarasvatī river and plunged in, heading eastward.

21.20.3.f.m: We swim across these, like pegs across a ford.

21.20.3.g.s: nikīrya tubhyaṃ madhya ākarśye karśyo yathā //
21.20.3.g.d: निकीर्य तुभ्यं मध्य आकर्श्ये कर्श्यो यथा ॥
21.20.3.g.m: Scattering for you in the middle, like a lean one in a lean [pasture] (?).

21.20.3.h.d: यदा भङ्ग्यश्विनौ वदत ऋतपर्णक यो ऽवधीः ।
21.20.3.h.m: When the two Bhaṅgyaśvins say: 'O Ṛtaparṇaka, who struck

21.20.3.i.m: the spoil of what was manifested and what was unmanifested of both?'

21.20.3.j.m: When the two Rākhāṭīs say: 'The village-dwelling Maṅkīra and Dāśaka—

21.20.3.k.m: when peaceful ease is ruined by the village, the draft-ox suffers while carrying.'

21.20.3.l.m: "The dappled cows drank this; this soma was pressed.

21.20.3.m.m: Here with gold pieces they wove pegs, ointment for the thighs."

21.20.4.a.s: haimahā idaṃ madhu hilluhillviti sarvāsāmṛganteṣu samayaḥ
21.20.4.a.d: हैमहा इदं मधु हिल्लुहिल्ल्विति सर्वासामृगन्तेषु समयः
21.20.4.a.m: "Haimahā! This is honey! Hillu, hillu!"—such is the conclusion at the ends of all the verses.

21.20.5.a.m: Then these slave girls, having poured out the water-jars, go as they please.

21.20.6.a.m: Following the chant for Mahendra, the noises cease.

21.20.7.a.s: arkaḥ pavitraṃ rajaso vimānaḥ punāti devānāṃ bhuvanāni viśvā /
21.20.7.a.d: अर्कः पवित्रं रजसो विमानः पुनाति देवानां भुवनानि विश्वा ।
21.20.7.a.m: "The sun, the strainer, measuring out space, purifies all the realms of the gods.

21.20.7.b.s: dyāvāpṛthivī payasā saṃvidāne ghṛtaṃ duhāte amṛtaṃ prapīne //
21.20.7.b.d: द्यावापृथिवी पयसा संविदाने घृतं दुहाते अमृतं प्रपीने ॥
21.20.7.b.m: Heaven and earth, agreeing through milk, swell yielding ghee and nectar.

21.20.7.c.s: pavitramarko rajaso vimānaḥ punāti devānāṃ bhuvanāni viśvā /
21.20.7.c.d: पवित्रमर्को रजसो विमानः पुनाति देवानां भुवनानि विश्वा ।
21.20.7.c.m: "The sun, the strainer, measuring out space, purifies all the realms of the gods.

21.20.7.d.s: suvarjyotiryaśo mahadaśīmahi gādhamuta pratiṣṭhāmiti phalake kūrcau vādhiruhyādhvaryuḥ śastraṃ pratigṛṇāti
21.20.7.d.d: सुवर्ज्योतिर्यशो महदशीमहि गाधमुत प्रतिष्ठामिति फलके कूर्चौ वाधिरुह्याध्वर्युः शस्त्रं प्रतिगृणाति
21.20.7.d.m: May we attain light, splendour, great glory, and a firm footing!"—having mounted two planks or two grass bundles, the adhvaryu responds to the recitation.

21.21.1.a.m: The concluding rite (udayanīya) and the Pṛṣṭhya-śamanīya day have been explained.

21.21.3.a.m: On the three Paraḥsāman days he draws three atigrāhya draughts.

21.21.4.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्यद्भ्यस्त्वौषधीभ्यो जुष्टं गृह्णामीति प्रथमे ऽहनि गृह्णाति ।
21.21.4.a.m: On the first day he draws with: "You are taken with a base: I draw you, agreeable to the waters, to the plants";

21.21.4.b.m: on the second with: "To the plants, to the offspring";

21.21.4.c.m: on the third with: "To the offspring, to Prajāpati."

21.21.5.a.m: These same ones in reverse order on the Arvāksāman days;

21.21.6.a.m: those same ones in forward and reverse order on the Viṣuvant day.

21.21.7.a.m: In their middle is the one for Sūrya: "Up that all-knowing god..."

21.21.8.a.s: etasminnevāhani vaiśvakarmaṇamatigrāhyāṇāmaṣṭamaṃ gṛhṇāti vācaspatiṃ viśvakarmāṇamūtaya iti
21.21.8.a.d: एतस्मिन्नेवाहनि वैश्वकर्मणमतिग्राह्याणामष्टमं गृह्णाति वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतय इति
21.21.8.a.m: On this very day, he draws the eighth among the atigrāhya draughts, the one for Viśvakarman, with: "The lord of speech, Viśvakarman, for help..."

21.21.9.a.s: śvo bhūta ādityaṃ mahīmū ṣu mātaramiti
21.21.9.a.d: श्वो भूत आदित्यं महीमू षु मातरमिति
21.21.9.a.m: On the next day, the one for Āditya, with: "The great mother..."

21.21.10.a.m: In this very manner he draws the two alternately until the Mahāvrata.

21.21.11.b.m: and the five-cup draught for Prajāpati.

21.21.12.a.m: On this day he draws thirty-three atigrāhya draughts:

21.21.13.a.s: daśāgneyā daśindrā daśa sauryā vaiśvakarmaṇa ādityaḥ pañcapātra iti trayastriṃśat
21.21.13.a.d: दशाग्नेया दशिन्द्रा दश सौर्या वैश्वकर्मण आदित्यः पञ्चपात्र इति त्रयस्त्रिंशत्
21.21.13.a.m: ten for Agni, ten for Indra, ten for Sūrya, the one for Viśvakarman, the one for Āditya, and the five-cup draught—thus thirty-three.

21.21.14.a.m: In the place for the atigrāhya draughts, four atigrāhya cups are set down, one in each direction;

21.21.16.a.s: indramidgāthina ityanudrutyopayāmagṛhīto 'sīndrāya tvārkavate juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvaiṣa te yonirindrāya tvārkavata iti sādayati
21.21.16.a.d: इन्द्रमिद्गाथिन इत्यनुद्रुत्योपयामगृहीतो ऽसीन्द्राय त्वार्कवते जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वैष ते योनिरिन्द्राय त्वार्कवत इति सादयति
21.21.16.a.m: Having recited along: "Indra indeed the singers...", he draws with: "You are taken with a base; I draw you, agreeable to Indra possessing Arka"; having drawn, he sets it down with: "This is your womb; for Indra possessing Arka!"

21.21.17.a.m: In this manner he adapts the drawing and setting-down formulas everywhere.

21.21.18.a.s: abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti dakṣiṇārdhe
21.21.18.a.d: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुम इति दक्षिणार्धे
21.21.18.a.m: In the southern part with: "Towards you, hero, we shout..."

21.22.1.a.s: imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhemendraśca viśve ca devāḥ /
21.22.1.a.d: इमा नु कं भुवना सीषधेमेन्द्रश्च विश्वे च देवाः ।
21.22.1.a.m: "May Indra and all the gods accomplish these realms for us!

21.22.1.b.s: yajñaṃ ca nastanvaṃ ca prajāṃ cādityairindraḥ saha sīṣadhātu /
21.22.1.b.d: यज्ञं च नस्तन्वं च प्रजां चादित्यैरिन्द्रः सह सीषधातु ।
21.22.1.b.m:
May Indra, along with the Ādityas, accomplish our sacrifice, our body, and our offspring!

[With the verse] "May Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas and the band of Maruts, grant us healing remedies," on the western half;

21.22.1.c.s: ādityairindraḥ sagaṇo marudbhirasmabhyaṃ bheṣajā karaditi paścārdhe
21.22.1.c.d: आदित्यैरिन्द्रः सगणो मरुद्भिरस्मभ्यं भेषजा करदिति पश्चार्धे

21.22.2.a.m: [with the verse] "Thee alone do we invoke," on the northern half.

21.22.3.a.s: tadidāsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ yato jajña ugrastveṣanṛmṇaḥ /
21.22.3.a.d: तदिदास भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठं यतो जज्ञ उग्रस्त्वेषनृम्णः ।
21.22.3.a.m: "That indeed was the eldest in the worlds, from which was born the fierce one of glittering valour;

21.22.3.b.s: sadyo jajñāno ni riṇāti śatrūnanu yaṃ viśve madantyūmā iti madhyame
21.22.3.b.d: सद्यो जज्ञानो नि रिणाति शत्रूननु यं विश्वे मदन्त्यूमा इति मध्यमे
21.22.3.b.m: Born immediately, he lays low the foes, whom all the protectors cheer": [with these two verses] on the middle [cup].

21.22.4.a.s: tānanyasminpātra ānīya sarvānmadhyame gṛhṇāti tve kratumapi vṛñjanti viśva iti
21.22.4.a.d: तानन्यस्मिन्पात्र आनीय सर्वान्मध्यमे गृह्णाति त्वे क्रतुमपि वृञ्जन्ति विश्व इति
21.22.4.a.m: Pouring them all together into another vessel, he takes [the draught] on the middle [cup] with: "In you all direct their insight."

21.22.5.b.m: "If he should offer them separately, he would sever the limbs from himself.

21.22.5.c.m: If he should withhold the oblations by bringing them together, the sacrificers would then be restricted.

21.22.5.d.m: Just drops, having been poured back into oneself, are to be offered.

21.22.5.e.s: pratyahāṅgāni dadāti nāhutīḥ saṃruṇaddhi na yajñaṃ vicchinattīti vijñāyate
21.22.5.e.d: प्रत्यहाङ्गानि ददाति नाहुतीः संरुणद्धि न यज्ञं विच्छिनत्तीति विज्ञायते
21.22.5.e.m: Day after day he gives limbs; he does not withhold the oblations, nor does he sever the sacrifice": thus it is known from scripture.

21.22.6.a.s: taṃ bhakṣayati mahaste bhakṣayāmi te bhakṣayāmi bhujaṃ te bhakṣayāmyannādyaṃ te bhaksāyāmīti
21.22.6.a.d: तं भक्षयति महस्ते भक्षयामि ते भक्षयामि भुजं ते भक्षयाम्यन्नाद्यं ते भक्सायामीति
21.22.6.a.m: He consumes it with: "I consume your greatness, I consume you, I consume your enjoyment, I consume your food."

21.22.7.a.m: We shall explain the three-pointed arrangement.

21.22.8.a.m: The first day has the draught for Indra and Vāyu first, then [a day] with the Śukra draught first, then [a day] with the Āgrayaṇa draught first.

21.22.9.a.s: evaṃvihitā tryanīkā parivartata ita ūrdhvā pragviṣuvataḥ
21.22.9.a.d: एवंविहिता त्र्यनीका परिवर्तत इत ऊर्ध्वा प्रग्विषुवतः
21.22.9.a.m: The three-pointed arrangement arranged in this way revolves upwards from here before the central day.

21.22.10.a.m: After the central day, [it revolves] through the reversed [days].

21.22.13.a.m: They immolate a victim for Agni on the opening day;

21.22.13.b.m: on the next day, a ewe for Sarasvatī.

21.22.14.a.m: They immolate day after day the sets of eleven victims arranged in this manner.

21.23.1.a.m: On the central day, an additional victim for Sūrya is to be immolated.

21.23.2.a.s: teṣāmevamupākurvatāṃ dvādaśāhīyasya daśarātrasya saptadaśa ukthye dvātriṃśatamekādaśinyo 'pavṛjyante
21.23.2.a.d: तेषामेवमुपाकुर्वतां द्वादशाहीयस्य दशरात्रस्य सप्तदश उक्थ्ये द्वात्रिंशतमेकादशिन्यो ऽपवृज्यन्ते
21.23.2.a.m: For them performing thus, on the seventeenth day, an Ukthya day, of the ten-day period of the twelve-day rite, thirty-two sets of eleven victims are completed.

21.23.4.a.m: On these they immolate the extra victims belonging to the cow [rite]:

21.23.4.b.m: a dwarf [victim] for Viṣṇu on the twenty-first [day];

21.23.4.d.m: one for the All-gods on the thirty-third;

21.23.4.e.m: a milch cow for Heaven and Earth on the first Chandoma day;

21.23.4.f.m: a calf for Vāyu, from that very cow, on the middle [Chandoma day];

21.23.4.g.m: a barren sheep for the Ādityas on the last [Chandoma day];

21.23.4.h.m: one for Mitra and Varuṇa on the Avivākya day;

21.23.4.i.m: a hornless bull for Prajāpati on the Mahāvrata day;

21.23.7.a.m: They immolate the sets of eleven victims on the opening and concluding days, either distributing them or not distributing them.

21.23.8.a.m: On the intermediate [days], an [animal] for Agni on those with the Rathaṃtara as the Pṛṣṭha chant, and one for Indra on those with the Bṛhat as the Pṛṣṭha chant.

21.23.9.a.m: Or rather, one for Agni and Indra on those with the Rathaṃtara as the Pṛṣṭha chant, and one for Indra and Agni on those with the Bṛhat as the Pṛṣṭha chant.

21.23.12.a.m: one with a white back for Bṛhaspati on the thirty-third [day];

21.23.12.c.m: a hornless bull of two colours, marked on both sides, for Viśvakarman on the Mahāvrata day.

21.23.13.a.m: They should immolate day after day the rite victims just like an accumulation, if there should be sufficient victims;

21.23.13.b.m: or the sets of eleven distributed: thus the Vājasaneyaka [holds].

21.23.14.a.m: Or one for Indra and Agni everywhere.

21.24.1.a.m: The Course of the Days-omitters is the Gavāmayana modified in attributes.

21.24.2.a.m: "Is [a day] to be omitted or not to be omitted?" has been declared.

21.24.3.a.s: yadyahānyutsṛjeyuḥ prathamaṃ pṛṣṭhyaṃ saṃsthāpyāparasmā ahne vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya vastīvarīṣu mṛtpiṇḍamavadhāyaindraṃ sāṃnāyyaṃ nirupyopavasanti
21.24.3.a.d: यद्यहान्युत्सृजेयुः प्रथमं पृष्ठ्यं संस्थाप्यापरस्मा अह्ने वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य वस्तीवरीषु मृत्पिण्डमवधायैन्द्रं सांनाय्यं निरुप्योपवसन्ति
21.24.3.a.m: If they omit days, having concluded the first Pṛṣṭhya six-day period, having carried around the Vasatīvarī waters for the next day, having put a lump of clay into the Vasatīvarī waters, and having apportioned the ritual milk offering for Indra, they observe fast.

21.24.4.a.m: On the next day, having omitted the day, they immolate an animal victim for Prajāpati.

21.24.5.a.s: tasya yathākālaṃ vapayā pracaryāgnaye vasumate puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapatyaindraṃ ca dadhi
21.24.5.a.d: तस्य यथाकालं वपया प्रचर्याग्नये वसुमते पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपत्यैन्द्रं च दधि
21.24.5.a.m: Having proceeded with its omentum at the proper time, he apportions a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds for Agni accompanied by the Vasus, and curd for Indra.

21.24.6.a.m: For both of them, the Sviṣṭakṛt offering and the iḍā are common.

21.24.7.a.m: When the iḍā has been invoked, having invoked the ritual milk offering together, they consume it.

21.24.8.a.s: mādhyaṃdinakāle paśupuroḍāśena pracaryendrāya marutvate puroḍāśamekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatyaindraṃ ca carum
21.24.8.a.d: माध्यंदिनकाले पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्येन्द्राय मरुत्वते पुरोडाशमेकादशकपालं निर्वपत्यैन्द्रं च चरुम्
21.24.8.a.m: At midday, having proceeded with the animal cake, he apportions a sacrificial cake on eleven potsherds for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, and a cooked mess for Indra.

21.24.9.a.s: havirāhutiprabhṛtīḍāntaṃ saṃsthāpya tṛtīyasavanakāle paśunā pracarya vaiśvadevaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati vaiśvadevaṃ ca caruṃ
21.24.9.a.d: हविराहुतिप्रभृतीडान्तं संस्थाप्य तृतीयसवनकाले पशुना प्रचर्य वैश्वदेवं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति वैश्वदेवं च चरुं
21.24.9.a.m: Having concluded [the rites] beginning with the oblations of the offering and ending with the iḍā, having proceeded with the animal victim at the time of the third pressing, he apportions a sacrificial cake on twelve potsherds for the All-gods, and a cooked mess for the All-gods.

21.24.10.a.m: He should conclude the two oblations as before.

21.24.11.a.s: api vā savanīyāneva puroḍāśāneteṣāṃ haviṣāṃ sthāne /
21.24.11.a.d: अपि वा सवनीयानेव पुरोडाशानेतेषां हविषां स्थाने ।
21.24.11.a.m: Or else just the pressing cakes in place of these oblations;

21.24.12.a.m: "Agnīdh, bring the embers for the after-offerings": beginning with this, he undertakes the animal rites.

21.25.1.a.m: In this manner, having completed the months with six-day periods from here on, having omitted the seventh [day], they perform this.

21.25.2.a.m: Five Jyotiṣ [days] are omitted before the Viṣuvant.

21.25.3.a.m: Four Trayastriṃśa [days] and one Jyotiṣ [day] after [the Viṣuvant], in the Saṃbhārya [period].

21.25.4.a.m: Some [teachers hold that] they should not omit [days] in the first and seventh [months] alone.

21.25.5.b.m: Those days which are due to be omitted should instead have the Ekatrika-stotra.

21.25.6.a.m: Or, they should omit a single stotriyā [verse] of these [days],

21.25.7.a.m: On the last day of the year, they should omit only a single stotriyā [verse].

21.25.7.b.m: Thus [the day] becomes both omitted and not omitted.

21.25.8.b.m: Whatever day they would omit, that very [day] they should perform on the following morning.

21.25.9.b.m: for that becomes a rent in the year.

21.25.10.a.m: Having come up from the avabhṛtha, they should perform those very [omitted days]:

21.25.11.a.m: twelve, if they omit on the new moon [days],

21.25.11.b.m: twenty-four, if on both [new and full moon days].

21.25.12.a.m: That this [ritual] brings grandsons, brings cattle, brings longevity, and leads to heaven.

21.25.13.a.m: The session of the Utsargins concludes; the session of the Utsargins [concludes].

22.1.1.a.m: In the one-day rites (ekāha) and multi-day rites (ahīna), he gives the standard sacrificial gifts,

22.1.2.a.m: The Agniṣṭoma is the model for all soma sacrifices.

22.1.2.b.m: In the case of groups [of sacrifices], however, the first is [the model] everywhere,

22.1.3.a.m: Jyotiṣ, Gauḥ, and Āyus: these are the Trikadrukas.

22.1.4.a.m: The first is an Agniṣṭoma, or all are Ukthyas.

22.1.5.a.m: At the Jyotiṣ, he gives a thousand [cows as sacrificial gift].

22.1.5.b.m: On account of the rule of the Śyaita [sāman], it has the Bṛhat as [first] pṛṣṭha[-stotra].

22.1.6.c.m: The Agniṣṭoma, however, is for one who has a rival.

22.1.6.d.m: The Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma is for one who desires pre-eminence.

22.1.7.a.s: sahasraṃ dakṣiṇā sarvavedasaṃ vā yāvatīrvā kratoḥ stotrīyāḥ
22.1.7.a.d: सहस्रं दक्षिणा सर्ववेदसं वा यावतीर्वा क्रतोः स्तोत्रीयाः
22.1.7.a.m: The sacrificial gift is a thousand [cows], or one's entire property (sarvavedasa), or as many [cows] as there are stotriyā verses in the sacrifice.

22.1.8.a.m: In the case of one's entire property, having allotted a share to the eldest son, he should beg back what is agreed upon.

22.1.9.a.m: Whatever property he possesses at the time of giving the sacrificial gifts, he should give all of that, other than land and human beings.

22.1.10.a.s: uttamāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ nītvodavasāya vā dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ prāṅniṣadya brūyādyanme 'da ṛṇaṃ yadadastatsarvaṃ dadāmīti
22.1.10.a.d: उत्तमां दक्षिणां नीत्वोदवसाय वा दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं प्राङ्निषद्य ब्रूयाद्यन्मे ऽद ऋणं यददस्तत्सर्वं ददामीति
22.1.10.a.m: Having led forth the final sacrificial gift, or having performed the udavasānīyā rite, seated facing east south of the audumbarī post, he should say: 'Whatever debt I owe of that, whatever of that, all of that I give.'

22.1.11.a.m: Having performed the udavasānīyā rite, [he puts on] a red skin of a calf; thus it is uniform.

22.1.12.a.m: Indra's Abhijit Agniṣṭoma is for the conquest of what has not yet been conquered.

22.1.13.a.m: Both Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara [sāmans] are used, or it has a transcendent pṛṣṭha.

22.1.14.a.m: The Bṛhat is for the hotṛ, and there are eleven sacrificial animals at a single sacrificial post.

22.1.15.a.s: sahasraṃ dakṣiṇā varāṇāṃ vā dvādaśaṃ śatam
22.1.15.a.d: सहस्रं दक्षिणा वराणां वा द्वादशं शतम्
22.1.15.a.m: The sacrificial gift is a thousand, or one hundred and twelve choice [cows].

22.1.16.a.m: By means of the Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma, one obtains everything and conquers everything,

22.2.2.a.m: Its Mahāvrata is recited as the Arkya pṛṣṭha-recitation.

22.2.3.a.m: The sacrificial gift is a thousand, or twenty times twenty-eight [cows].

22.2.5.a.m: The first is the Jyotiṣ Agniṣṭoma with the Rathaṃtara sāman.

22.2.5.b.m: He is established in the vital breaths and in the eating of food.

22.2.5.c.m: The second is the Gauḥ Ukthya with the Bṛhat sāman.

22.2.5.e.m: The third is the Sarvajyotiṣ Agniṣṭoma with both sāmans.

22.2.5.f.m: He obtains everything and conquers everything.

22.2.5.g.m: The fourth is the Agniṣṭoma equal to a three-day rite (trirātra), with the Bṛhat sāman.

22.2.5.h.m: He obtains the fruit of a three-day rite.

22.2.8.a.m: The first has the Rathaṃtara sāman, the Bṛhat sāman, or both sāmans.

22.2.9.a.s: tasminkāmāḥ spardhāyāṃ bhrātṛvyatistīrṣā svargaḥ paśavo vā
22.2.9.a.d: तस्मिन्कामाः स्पर्धायां भ्रातृव्यतिस्तीर्षा स्वर्गः पशवो वा
22.2.9.a.m: In it, the desired objects are: in a rivalry, the desire to overcome a rival, heaven, or cattle.

22.2.10.a.m: On the previous day of those [rites], there are animals dedicated to Agni, to Soma, and to Bṛhaspati.

22.2.11.a.m: They have the characteristics of an ekādaśinī [group of victims].

22.2.12.a.m: In the absence of these [animals], the first [offering] to these deities is an [eight-potsherd cake] on eight potsherds, and the other two are carus.

22.2.14.a.m: He pours clarified butter across the uttaravedi.

22.2.16.a.s: hiraṇyaṃ mukhe nyasyāntarorū priyāyai bhāryāyai brahmacārī śete śva iṣṭyā paśunā vā yakṣya iti
22.2.16.a.d: हिरण्यं मुखे न्यस्यान्तरोरू प्रियायै भार्यायै ब्रह्मचारी शेते श्व इष्ट्या पशुना वा यक्ष्य इति
22.2.16.a.m: Having placed gold in his mouth, keeping celibacy between the thighs of his dear wife, he lies down, thinking: 'Tomorrow I shall sacrifice with an iṣṭi or with an animal sacrifice.'

22.2.18.a.s: tānyathālokaṃ vinidhāya sarvā diśaḥ sakṣīradṛtayo 'śvarathāḥ somapravākā vidhāvanti
22.2.18.a.d: तान्यथालोकं विनिधाय सर्वा दिशः सक्षीरदृतयो ऽश्वरथाः सोमप्रवाका विधावन्ति
22.2.18.a.m: Having placed them according to their respective places, horse-drawn chariots carrying skin bags with milk run forth in all directions as soma-announcers.

22.2.19.a.m: Whatever butter should rise from them, that he should pour into the clarified butter.

22.2.20.a.m: In the eastern direction [they go] one yojana with a four-yoked [chariot];

22.2.20.b.m: In the northern [direction], three krośas with a three-yoked [chariot];

22.2.20.c.m: In the western [direction], two krośas with a two-yoked [chariot];

22.2.20.d.m: In the southern [direction], one krośa with a single-yoked [vehicle].

22.2.22.a.m: The release is clockwise, beginning with the east.

22.2.23.a.m: Or distances starting with a yojana down to two krośas [may be used].

22.2.24.a.m: The southern release is done with a horse-drawn chariot.

22.2.25.a.m: A three-year-old uncastrated bull is the soma-purchase price.

22.3.1.a.m: When the sacrificer is consecrated after sunrise, the avabhṛtha takes place before sunset.

22.3.2.a.m: During the upasads, he should close his eyes three times;

22.3.2.c.m: Or there are no afternoon upasads.

22.3.4.a.m: The threshing floor for barley is the uttaravedi.

22.3.7.a.s: sphyo yūpaḥ sphyāgro vā khalevālī lāṅgaleṣā vā
22.3.7.a.d: स्फ्यो यूपः स्फ्याग्रो वा खलेवाली लाङ्गलेषा वा
22.3.7.a.m: A wooden sword is the sacrificial post, or one with the tip shaped like a wooden sword, or the post of the threshing floor, or the shaft of a plough.

22.3.9.a.m: At the time of the Agnīṣomīya [rite], he should draw the vasatīvarī waters from the house of a person who has already sacrificed.

22.3.10.a.d: सवनीयकाले सह पशूनालभते ऽग्निषोमीयं सवनीयमनूबन्ध्यां च
22.3.10.a.m: At the time of the savanīya [animal rite], he seizes the animals together: the Agnīṣomīya, the savanīya, and the anūbandhyā.

22.3.11.a.m: In place of the Agnīṣomīya [animal], an eleven-potsherd cake for Agni-Soma;

22.3.11.b.m: In place of the anūbandhyā, a curd-mess for Mitra-Varuṇa.

22.3.12.a.m: At the time of its sacrificial gift, a noble white horse is the sacrificial gift.

22.3.13.a.m: He should give it to an Āṅgirasa or to a rival.

22.3.14.a.s: dveṣyaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vṛtvā tasmā aśvaṃ rukmapratimuktaṃ dadyāt
22.3.14.a.d: द्वेष्यं वा ब्राह्मणं वृत्वा तस्मा अश्वं रुक्मप्रतिमुक्तं दद्यात्
22.3.14.a.m: Or having chosen an enemy brahmin, he should give him a horse adorned with a gold ornament.

22.3.16.a.m: For a year afterwards, he should avoid washing the feet [by another], meat, women, untruth, sleeping on a raised bed, and collyrium and body-salve.

22.3.18.a.m: If he cannot [endure] a year, twelve days.

22.4.1.a.m: By this the subsequent [rites] are explained.

22.4.2.a.s: dvitīyasya pañcadaśamagniṣṭomasāma kṛtvāmayāvinamannādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ vā yājayet
22.4.2.a.d: द्वितीयस्य पञ्चदशमग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वामयाविनमन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वा याजयेत्
22.4.2.a.m: Having made the Agniṣṭoma chant of the second [rite] fifteen-versed, one should perform sacrifice for one who is chronically ill, or desirous of proper food, or desirous of offspring, or desirous of cattle.

22.4.4.a.m: Its two subsequent pavamāna chants are eighteen-versed.

22.4.5.a.d: अश्वसादः सोमप्रवाको दधिदृतिश्च त्रिक्रोषे ऽन्ततः प्राह
22.4.5.a.m: A horseman as soma-announcer and a curd-skin bag announce at the distance of three krośas at the farthest.
