22.4.9.a.m: The threshing floor for rice is the uttaravedi.

22.4.11.a.m: The fourth [rite] is the Viśvajit-Śilpa, with all pṛṣṭhas, all stomas, and one's entire property as the sacrificial gift.

22.4.12.a.m: He obtains the impulse of all proper food.

22.4.13.a.m: Practicing sorcery, he should sacrifice with the Śyena.

22.4.15.a.m: The sacrificial post is of tilvaka wood or badhaka wood, with a tip shaped like a wooden sword.

22.4.16.a.m: Two hearse-wheel hubs serve as the two pressing boards.

22.4.17.a.m: A red animal is for Agni Rudravat.

22.4.18.a.m: They deposit the upāṃśu and antaryāma [cups].

22.4.23.a.m: Wearing red turbans, dressed in red garments, with sacred threads suspended from the neck, the priests proceed.

22.4.24.a.s: navanava dakṣiṇāḥ kūṭāḥ karṇāḥ kāṇāḥ khaṇḍā baṇḍāḥ
22.4.24.a.d: नवनव दक्षिणाः कूटाः कर्णाः काणाः खण्डा बण्डाः
22.4.24.a.m: Nine each are the sacrificial gifts: hornless, with deformed ears, one-eyed, mutilated, or tailless.

22.4.25.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, they should prick them with thorns.

22.4.26.a.m: If he wishes that [his enemy] should be struck down, he should make the Rathaṃtara the Pavamāna [chant] and the Bṛhat the Pṛṣṭha [chant].

22.4.26.b.m: If he wishes that [his enemy] should be vanquished, it is the reverse of this.

22.4.27.a.s: parāṃ parāvataṃ gacchenna pratitiṣṭhediti pūrvavatplavaṃ ca brahmasāma kuryāt
22.4.27.a.d: परां परावतं गच्छेन्न प्रतितिष्ठेदिति पूर्ववत्प्लवं च ब्रह्मसाम कुर्यात्
22.4.27.a.m: If he wishes that [his enemy] should depart to the farthest distance and not find support, [he should proceed] as before and make the Brahma-sāman the Plava.

22.4.28.a.d: प्रजापतेरेकतिर्को ऽग्निष्टोमः सर्वस्य पाप्मनो निर्दिश्य गच्छति
22.4.28.a.m: The Ekatrika Agniṣṭoma belongs to Prajāpati; having singled out all evil, he departs [free from it].

22.4.29.a.m: He gives twenty-four cows as the sacrificial gift.

22.5.2.a.m: The first two are Agniṣṭomas having the Rathaṃtara as their chant;

22.5.2.b.m: the latter is an Atirātra containing all the Stomas.

22.5.3.a.s: tasminsarvā ṛcaḥ sarvāṇi sāmāni sarvāṇi yajūṃṣu prayujyante
22.5.3.a.d: तस्मिन्सर्वा ऋचः सर्वाणि सामानि सर्वाणि यजूंषु प्रयुज्यन्ते
22.5.3.a.m: In it all the Ṛc verses, all the Sāmans, and all the Yajus formulas are employed.

22.5.4.a.m: When Vrātyas dwell away from home, the Vrātyastomas are Ukthyas having the Rathaṃtara as their chant;

22.5.5.a.s: uṣṇīṣaṃ pratodo jyāhroḍo ratho vipathaḥ phalakāstīrṇo 'śvo 'śvataraśca yugyau kṛṣṇaśaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇabalakṣe ajine rajato niṣkaḥ
22.5.5.a.d: उष्णीषं प्रतोदो ज्याह्रोडो रथो विपथः फलकास्तीर्णो ऽश्वो ऽश्वतरश्च युग्यौ कृष्णशं वासः कृष्णबलक्षे अजिने रजतो निष्कः
22.5.5.a.m: A turban, a goad, a bow without an arrow, a rough wagon covered with planks, a horse and a mule as draught animals, a black-bordered cloth, two black-and-white skins, and a silver coin—

22.5.7.a.m: The others have garments with borders of balūka grass and fringed cords.

22.5.8.a.m: There are two cords for each;

22.5.10.a.m: They join the householder in groups of thirty-three each.

22.5.12.a.m: Or they may procure sixty-six cows.

22.5.13.a.m: Now they also say: whatever they have acquired, they should give that; for that is the wealth of the Vrātyas.

22.5.14.b.m: the Dviṣoḍaśin is for the youngest;

22.5.14.c.m: the Ūrdhvastoma is for the eldest;

22.5.15.a.m: The Prayati of the Ādityas is an Ukthya, the first of the Nākasads;

22.5.16.a.m: they attain separation from evil, from their rival.

22.5.17.d.m: by the fourth, which belongs to the Maruts, one obtains vigor and valor;

22.5.18.a.m: Desiring heaven, one overcomes one's rival with the Abhibhū;

22.5.18.b.m: with the Vinutti, one repulses one's rival.

22.6.1.a.m: The Citistoma is for one desiring procreation.

22.6.2.a.m: A brāhmaṇa desiring spiritual luster [should sacrifice] with the Gāyatra Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara as its chant.

22.6.3.a.m: The two Gāyatra Agniṣṭomas are initial sacrifices:

22.6.4.a.m: by the first, [is obtained] brilliance and spiritual luster for a brāhmaṇa;

22.6.4.b.m: by the second, a mighty, unshakeable realm for a kṣatriya;

22.6.4.c.m: they do not, however, bring many cattle.

22.6.5.a.m: One who is impure should sacrifice with the threefold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma.

22.6.7.a.d: आग्नेयीषु स्तुवते ऽजा हिरण्यं च दक्षिणा
22.6.7.a.m: they chant on verses dedicated to Agni; a she-goat and gold are the sacrificial gift.

22.6.8.a.s: etameva catuṣṭomaṃ kṛtvā śrotriyo 'kṣahataḥ strīhataḥ kāmahataścaraṇahato vā yajeta
22.6.8.a.d: एतमेव चतुष्टोमं कृत्वा श्रोत्रियो ऽक्षहतः स्त्रीहतः कामहतश्चरणहतो वा यजेत
22.6.8.a.m: Having made this very [sacrifice] a Catuṣṭoma, a learned brāhmaṇa who is ruined by dice, ruined by women, ruined by desire, or ruined in conduct should sacrifice.
